## File: .claude/skills/auth-patterns/resources/api-jwt-validation.md
````markdown
 1: # API JWT Validation Patterns
 2: 
 3: Use this pattern for API projects that accept bearer tokens from an external OIDC provider.
 4: 
 5: ## Registration Pattern
 6: 
 7: ```csharp
 8: builder.Services
 9:     .AddAuthentication(JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme)
10:     .AddJwtBearer(options =>
11:     {
12:         options.Authority = configuration["Auth:Authority"];
13:         options.Audience = configuration["Auth:Audience"];
14:         options.MapInboundClaims = false;
15: 
16:         options.TokenValidationParameters = new TokenValidationParameters
17:         {
18:             ValidateIssuer = true,
19:             ValidateAudience = true,
20:             ValidateLifetime = true,
21:             ValidateIssuerSigningKey = true,
22:             ClockSkew = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5)
23:         };
24:     });
25: ```
26: 
27: ## Middleware Order
28: 
29: Use the request pipeline in this order:
30: 
31: 1. Exception handling
32: 2. Routing and CORS
33: 3. Authentication
34: 4. Authorization
35: 5. Endpoint mapping
36: 
37: Incorrect ordering is a common cause of false `401`/`403` responses.
38: 
39: ## Claim Extraction
40: 
41: Normalize user ID extraction with one shared helper/service and fallback order:
42: 
43: 1. `sub`
44: 2. `http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/nameidentifier`
45: 3. `sid`
46: 
47: Avoid duplicating claim parsing logic across controllers.
48: 
49: ## Logging Guardrails
50: 
51: - Log auth failures with context (issuer, audience mismatch, claim shape).
52: - Never log raw JWT values.
53: - Include correlation and trace identifiers for incident triage.
````

## File: .claude/skills/blazor-bff-patterns/resources/interactiveauto-yarp-security.md
````markdown
 1: # InteractiveAuto + YARP Security Patterns
 2: 
 3: Production guidance for Blazor Hybrid apps using InteractiveAuto and YARP/BFF.
 4: 
 5: ## Middleware and Endpoint Order
 6: 
 7: - Configure forwarded headers before auth middleware when behind reverse proxy.
 8: - Use routing, then authentication, then authorization, then antiforgery and endpoints.
 9: - Map Blazor routes before proxy catch-all routes when both coexist.
10: 
11: ## Token Forwarding
12: 
13: - Keep tokens server-side (cookie-backed session in BFF).
14: - Forward access tokens to downstream API via YARP request transforms or delegating handlers.
15: - Never expose raw access tokens to browser storage.
16: 
17: ## Anti-Forgery
18: 
19: - Enable antiforgery and validate on state-changing endpoints.
20: - For SPA requests, send antiforgery token via header (for example `X-CSRF-TOKEN`).
21: - Keep cookie flags secure (`HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite` based on deployment needs).
22: 
23: ## InteractiveAuto Constraints
24: 
25: - Components may execute in server or WASM contexts.
26: - Avoid direct `HttpContext` assumptions in components intended for InteractiveAuto.
27: - Register required services in both server and client projects when shared by InteractiveAuto components.
28: 
29: ## Operational Hardening
30: 
31: - Add health checks and graceful shutdown for rolling deployments.
32: - Use structured auth/proxy logs without leaking tokens.
33: - Validate proxy destination configuration through environment-specific settings, not hardcoded values.
````

## File: .claude/skills/blazor-css-isolation/resources/bem-with-isolation.md
````markdown
 1: # BEM with CSS Isolation
 2: 
 3: Use BEM naming in `.razor.css` files to keep component styling explicit and maintainable.
 4: 
 5: ## Pattern
 6: 
 7: - Block: `.event-card`
 8: - Element: `.event-card__header`
 9: - Modifier: `.event-card--featured`
10: 
11: ## Example
12: 
13: ```razor
14: <article class="event-card event-card--featured">
15:     <h2 class="event-card__title">@Title</h2>
16: </article>
17: ```
18: 
19: ```css
20: .event-card { border: 1px solid var(--mud-palette-lines-default); }
21: .event-card--featured { border-color: var(--mud-palette-primary); }
22: .event-card__title { color: var(--mud-palette-text-primary); }
23: ```
24: 
25: ## Rules
26: 
27: - Keep one block namespace per component.
28: - Prefer semantic element names over positional names.
29: - Use MudBlazor theme variables, not hardcoded color values.
````

## File: .claude/skills/blazor-css-isolation/resources/debugging-scoped-css.md
````markdown
 1: # Debugging Scoped CSS
 2: 
 3: When isolated CSS does not apply, verify build output and scope attributes.
 4: 
 5: ## Checklist
 6: 
 7: 1. Ensure file naming matches (`Component.razor` + `Component.razor.css`).
 8: 2. Confirm scope attribute exists in DOM (`b-xxxxxxxxxx`).
 9: 3. Confirm `{Project}.styles.css` is loaded.
10: 4. Verify selector specificity and `::deep` placement.
11: 
12: ## Typical Issues
13: 
14: - Styles not applied: wrong file name or missing stylesheet link.
15: - Unexpected overrides: global stylesheet or high-specificity MudBlazor selectors.
16: - Broken after dependency update: `::deep` tied to third-party internal class changes.
````

## File: .claude/skills/blazor-css-isolation/resources/deep-selector-patterns.md
````markdown
 1: # ::deep Selector Patterns
 2: 
 3: `::deep` is an escape hatch for styling nested third-party internals from isolated CSS.
 4: 
 5: ## Use Sparingly
 6: 
 7: - Use for MudBlazor/third-party internals when no `Class`/parameter option exists.
 8: - Do not use as a first choice for styling your own child components.
 9: 
10: ## Example
11: 
12: ```css
13: .event-dialog ::deep .mud-dialog-content {
14:     padding: 20px;
15: }
16: ```
17: 
18: ## Preferred Alternatives
19: 
20: - Style child components in their own `.razor.css` files.
21: - Pass class names through component parameters.
22: - Wrap child components in a container and style the container descendants.
````

## File: .claude/skills/blazor-css-isolation/resources/mudblazor-styling.md
````markdown
 1: # MudBlazor Styling with Isolation
 2: 
 3: Combine MudBlazor component `Class` parameters with isolated CSS and BEM names.
 4: 
 5: ## Pattern
 6: 
 7: ```razor
 8: <MudCard Class="event-card event-card--upcoming">
 9:     <MudCardHeader Class="event-card__header" />
10:     <MudCardContent Class="event-card__body" />
11: </MudCard>
12: ```
13: 
14: ```css
15: .event-card { border-radius: 12px; }
16: .event-card--upcoming { border-left: 4px solid var(--mud-palette-success); }
17: .event-card__header { background: var(--mud-palette-surface-variant); }
18: ```
19: 
20: ## Guidance
21: 
22: - Prefer MudBlazor properties first (`Color`, `Variant`, `Size`, etc.).
23: - Add classes for app-specific design language.
24: - Use `::deep` only for internals that are otherwise unreachable.
````

## File: .claude/skills/blazor-css-isolation/SKILL.md
````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: blazor-css-isolation
  3: description: Blazor CSS isolation patterns with BEM methodology. Covers component.razor.css scoped styling, ::deep selector for child components, and BEM class naming conventions.
  4: type: ui
  5: enforcement: suggest
  6: priority: high
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: # Blazor CSS Isolation with BEM Methodology
 10: 
 11: > **Project-Agnostic CSS Isolation Patterns for Blazor**
 12: >
 13: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
 14: 
 15: ## Purpose
 16: 
 17: Provides enterprise-grade patterns for component-scoped CSS in Blazor applications using CSS isolation (`.razor.css` files) combined with BEM (Block Element Modifier) methodology. Ensures maintainable, collision-free styling with proper encapsulation.
 18: 
 19: ## When This Skill Activates
 20: 
 21: **Triggered by**:
 22: - Keywords: "css isolation", "scoped css", "razor.css", "::deep", "bem", "block element modifier", "component styling"
 23: - File patterns: `**/*.razor.css`, `**/*.razor`
 24: - Content patterns: `::deep`, BEM class names (`.block__element--modifier`)
 25: 
 26: ## How Blazor CSS Isolation Works
 27: 
 28: ### Build-Time Transformation
 29: 
 30: Blazor compiles `.razor.css` files by:
 31: 1. **Generating unique scope attribute**: Format `b-<10-char-string>` (e.g., `b-3xxtam6d07`)
 32: 2. **Appending to selectors**: `h1` becomes `h1[b-3xxtam6d07]`
 33: 3. **Applying to DOM elements**: Rendered elements receive the scope attribute
 34: 4. **Bundling**: Generated CSS outputs to `{Project}.styles.css`
 35: 
 36: **Pattern**:
 37: ```css
 38: /* Author in Counter.razor.css */
 39: h1 { color: brown; }
 40: 
 41: /* Compiled output in {Project}.styles.css */
 42: h1[b-3xxtam6d07] { color: brown; }
 43: ```
 44: 
 45: **Key Benefit**: Styles apply ONLY to component's own elements, preventing global collisions.
 46: 
 47: ## Resources
 48: 
 49: | Resource | Description |
 50: |----------|-------------|
 51: | [bem-with-isolation.md](resources/bem-with-isolation.md) | BEM naming patterns for isolated CSS |
 52: | [deep-selector-patterns.md](resources/deep-selector-patterns.md) | Safe ::deep usage for child components |
 53: | [mudblazor-styling.md](resources/mudblazor-styling.md) | Styling MudBlazor components with isolation |
 54: | [debugging-scoped-css.md](resources/debugging-scoped-css.md) | Browser DevTools techniques for isolated CSS |
 55: 
 56: ## Quick Reference
 57: 
 58: ### 1. File Structure & Naming
 59: 
 60: **Pattern**: Place `ComponentName.razor.css` next to `ComponentName.razor` (same folder, same name).
 61: 
 62: ```
 63: Components/
 64: ├── Card.razor
 65: ├── Card.razor.css       ✅ Automatically scoped to Card component
 66: ├── EventList.razor
 67: └── EventList.razor.css  ✅ Automatically scoped to EventList component
 68: ```
 69: 
 70: **Rules**:
 71: - File names are case-insensitive but MUST match `.razor` filename
 72: - Missing the `.razor.css` file means no scoped styles for that component
 73: - Scoped CSS bundle (`{Project}.styles.css`) must be referenced in `App.razor` or `index.html`
 74: 
 75: ---
 76: 
 77: ### 2. BEM with CSS Isolation
 78: 
 79: **Pattern**: Use BEM class names in component markup; compiler scopes them automatically.
 80: 
 81: #### Component Markup (Card.razor)
 82: 
 83: ```razor
 84: <article class="card card--featured">
 85:     <header class="card__header">
 86:         <h2 class="card__title">@Title</h2>
 87:         <span class="card__badge card__badge--new">New</span>
 88:     </header>
 89:     <div class="card__body">
 90:         <p class="card__text">@Description</p>
 91:     </div>
 92:     <footer class="card__footer">
 93:         <MudButton Class="card__action">Read More</MudButton>
 94:     </footer>
 95: </article>
 96: 
 97: @code {
 98:     [Parameter] public string Title { get; set; } = string.Empty;
 99:     [Parameter] public string Description { get; set; } = string.Empty;
100: }
101: ```
102: 
103: #### Scoped CSS (Card.razor.css)
104: 
105: ```css
106: /* Block */
107: .card {
108:     border: 1px solid var(--mud-palette-lines-default);
109:     border-radius: 8px;
110:     background: var(--mud-palette-surface);
111: }
112: 
113: /* Block modifier */
114: .card--featured {
115:     border-color: var(--mud-palette-primary);
116:     box-shadow: var(--mud-shadow-2);
117: }
118: 
119: /* Elements */
120: .card__header {
121:     padding: 16px;
122:     border-bottom: 1px solid var(--mud-palette-lines-default);
123: }
124: 
125: .card__title {
126:     margin: 0;
127:     font-size: 1.25rem;
128:     font-weight: 600;
129:     color: var(--mud-palette-text-primary);
130: }
131: 
132: .card__badge {
133:     display: inline-block;
134:     padding: 4px 8px;
135:     border-radius: 4px;
136:     font-size: 0.75rem;
137: }
138: 
139: /* Element modifier */
140: .card__badge--new {
141:     background: var(--mud-palette-success);
142:     color: var(--mud-palette-success-text);
143: }
144: 
145: .card__body {
146:     padding: 16px;
147: }
148: 
149: .card__text {
150:     margin: 0;
151:     line-height: 1.5;
152: }
153: 
154: .card__footer {
155:     padding: 12px 16px;
156:     border-top: 1px solid var(--mud-palette-lines-default);
157: }
158: 
159: .card__action {
160:     text-transform: uppercase;
161: }
162: ```
163: 
164: **Compiled Output** (automatic):
165: ```css
166: /* All selectors receive scope attribute */
167: .card[b-3xxtam6d07] { ... }
168: .card--featured[b-3xxtam6d07] { ... }
169: .card__header[b-3xxtam6d07] { ... }
170: .card__title[b-3xxtam6d07] { ... }
171: /* ... and so on */
172: ```
173: 
174: **Why BEM + Isolation?**
175: - **BEM**: Explicit, readable class names (`.block__element--modifier`)
176: - **Isolation**: Automatic scoping prevents `.card` collision with other components
177: - **Result**: Predictable, maintainable styles without naming conflicts
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ### 3. Styling Child Components (Preferred Patterns)
182: 
183: #### Pattern A: Child's Own CSS (Recommended)
184: 
185: **Best Practice**: Each component styles itself in its own `.razor.css`.
186: 
187: ```razor
188: <!-- Parent.razor -->
189: <div class="parent">
190:     <ChildCard Title="Example" />
191: </div>
192: 
193: <!-- ChildCard.razor -->
194: <div class="child-card">
195:     <h3>@Title</h3>
196: </div>
197: ```
198: 
199: ```css
200: /* Parent.razor.css */
201: .parent {
202:     display: grid;
203:     gap: 16px;
204: }
205: 
206: /* ChildCard.razor.css (child styles itself) */
207: .child-card {
208:     padding: 12px;
209:     background: #f5f5f5;
210: }
211: ```
212: 
213: **Why**: Separation of concerns; child owns its styles.
214: 
215: ---
216: 
217: #### Pattern B: Wrapper Container (Safe Descendant Styling)
218: 
219: **Pattern**: Wrap child in HTML element to apply scope attribute, enabling descendant selectors.
220: 
221: ```razor
222: <!-- Parent.razor -->
223: <div class="parent">
224:     <div class="parent__child-wrapper">
225:         <ChildComponent />
226:     </div>
227: </div>
228: ```
229: 
230: ```css
231: /* Parent.razor.css */
232: .parent__child-wrapper {
233:     padding: 8px;
234:     border: 1px solid #ddd;
235: }
236: 
237: /* Wrapper receives scope attribute; descendant selectors work */
238: .parent__child-wrapper > div {
239:     margin-bottom: 8px;
240: }
241: ```
242: 
243: **Why**: Wrapper gets scope attribute; you can style children without `::deep`.
244: 
245: ---
246: 
247: ### 4. The ::deep Selector (Use Sparingly)
248: 
249: **Purpose**: Penetrate child component encapsulation to style nested elements.
250: 
251: **Transformation**:
252: ```css
253: /* Authored */
254: .parent ::deep .child-element {
255:     color: red;
256: }
257: 
258: /* Compiled */
259: .parent[b-3xxtam6d07] .child-element {
260:     color: red;
261: }
262: ```
263: 
264: **Pattern**: Scope attribute moves to ancestor, selector reaches descendants.
265: 
266: #### Safe ::deep Usage
267: 
268: ```razor
269: <!-- Host.razor -->
270: <div class="host">
271:     <ThirdPartyComponent />
272: </div>
273: ```
274: 
275: ```css
276: /* Host.razor.css */
277: .host ::deep .tp-control {
278:     background: var(--mud-palette-surface);
279: }
280: 
281: .host ::deep .tp-control__header {
282:     font-weight: 600;
283: }
284: ```
285: 
286: **When to Use ::deep**:
287: - ✅ Styling third-party components with no exposed styling API
288: - ✅ Overriding library component internals when necessary
289: - ✅ Reaching nested DOM that cannot be wrapped
290: 
291: **When NOT to Use ::deep**:
292: - ❌ Styling your own child components (use child's `.razor.css`)
293: - ❌ First resort (prefer wrapper pattern or component parameters)
294: - ❌ Global resets (use global CSS file instead)
295: 
296: **Tradeoffs**:
297: - ⚠️ **Fragile**: Coupled to child's internal markup/class names
298: - ⚠️ **Upgrade Risk**: Library updates may break selectors
299: - ⚠️ **Specificity**: Adds complexity to CSS cascade
300: 
301: ---
302: 
303: ### 5. Styling MudBlazor Components
304: 
305: **Pattern**: Combine MudBlazor's `Class` parameter with BEM in isolated CSS.
306: 
307: ```razor
308: <!-- EventCard.razor -->
309: <MudCard Class="event-card event-card--upcoming">
310:     <MudCardHeader Class="event-card__header">
311:         <MudText Typo="Typo.h6" Class="event-card__title">@Title</MudText>
312:     </MudCardHeader>
313:     <MudCardContent Class="event-card__body">
314:         <MudText Class="event-card__description">@Description</MudText>
315:     </MudCardContent>
316:     <MudCardActions Class="event-card__footer">
317:         <MudButton Variant="Variant.Text" Color="Color.Primary" Class="event-card__action">
318:             Register
319:         </MudButton>
320:     </MudCardActions>
321: </MudCard>
322: ```
323: 
324: ```css
325: /* EventCard.razor.css */
326: .event-card {
327:     border-radius: 12px;
328: }
329: 
330: .event-card--upcoming {
331:     border-left: 4px solid var(--mud-palette-success);
332: }
333: 
334: .event-card__header {
335:     background: var(--mud-palette-surface-variant);
336: }
337: 
338: .event-card__title {
339:     color: var(--mud-palette-primary);
340: }
341: 
342: .event-card__description {
343:     line-height: 1.6;
344: }
345: 
346: .event-card__footer {
347:     justify-content: flex-end;
348: }
349: 
350: .event-card__action {
351:     font-weight: 500;
352: }
353: 
354: /* Override MudBlazor internals with ::deep (use sparingly) */
355: .event-card ::deep .mud-card-header-content {
356:     padding: 20px;
357: }
358: ```
359: 
360: **Best Practice**:
361: 1. Use MudBlazor's `Class` parameter for BEM classes
362: 2. Style those classes in `.razor.css`
363: 3. Use `::deep` ONLY for unreachable MudBlazor internals
364: 4. Prefer MudBlazor theme variables over hardcoded colors
365: 
366: ---
367: 
368: ### 6. Debugging Scoped CSS
369: 
370: #### Browser DevTools Techniques
371: 
372: **Step 1: Inspect Element Scope Attribute**
373: 
374: Look for generated attribute in rendered HTML:
375: ```html
376: <h1 b-3xxtam6d07>Counter</h1>
377: ```
378: 
379: **Step 2: Find Matching Selector in Styles**
380: 
381: In DevTools Styles panel, look for:
382: ```css
383: h1[b-3xxtam6d07] {
384:     color: brown;
385: }
386: ```
387: 
388: **Step 3: Verify Bundle Reference**
389: 
390: Check `App.razor` or `index.html` includes:
391: ```html
392: <link href="{Project}.styles.css" rel="stylesheet" />
393: ```
394: 
395: **Common Issues**:
396: 
397: | Symptom | Cause | Fix |
398: |---------|-------|-----|
399: | Styles not applying | Missing bundle reference | Add `<link>` to `{Project}.styles.css` |
400: | Wrong component styled | Scope attribute mismatch | Rebuild project; check file names match |
401: | Child not styled | Using parent CSS | Add `.razor.css` to child OR use wrapper/::deep |
402: | ::deep not working | Child renders to body | Use component's `Target` parameter if available |
403: 
404: ---
405: 
406: ## BEM Naming Guidelines
407: 
408: ### Pattern Structure
409: 
410: ```
411: .block
412: .block__element
413: .block--modifier
414: .block__element--modifier
415: ```
416: 
417: ### Practical Examples
418: 
419: ```css
420: /* Component: EventCard */
421: .event-card { }                      /* Block */
422: .event-card__header { }              /* Element */
423: .event-card__title { }               /* Element */
424: .event-card--featured { }            /* Block modifier */
425: .event-card__badge--new { }          /* Element modifier */
426: 
427: /* Component: SearchBar */
428: .search-bar { }
429: .search-bar__input { }
430: .search-bar__button { }
431: .search-bar--expanded { }
432: .search-bar__input--focused { }
433: ```
434: 
435: ### Naming Best Practices
436: 
437: - **Keep names concise**: `card__title` not `card__title-text-content`
438: - **Use semantic names**: `card__action` not `card__button1`
439: - **Avoid abbreviations**: `card__description` not `card__desc`
440: - **Single responsibility**: `card__header` not `card__header-with-icon`
441: 
442: ---
443: 
444: ## Key Principles
445: 
446: 1. **Colocation**: Place `.razor.css` next to `.razor` file
447: 2. **Component Ownership**: Each component styles itself in its own `.razor.css`
448: 3. **BEM for Clarity**: Use BEM even though isolation prevents collisions
449: 4. **Wrapper Over ::deep**: Prefer wrapping children in containers
450: 5. **::deep as Last Resort**: Only penetrate encapsulation when necessary
451: 6. **MudBlazor Integration**: Use `Class` parameter + isolated CSS
452: 7. **Scope Verification**: Check `b-<string>` attribute in DevTools
453: 
454: ---
455: 
456: ## Do's
457: 
458: - ✅ **DO** name files `Component.razor.css` (matches `.razor` filename)
459: - ✅ **DO** use BEM class names for explicit styling hooks
460: - ✅ **DO** style child components in their own `.razor.css`
461: - ✅ **DO** wrap children in containers for descendant styling
462: - ✅ **DO** verify `{Project}.styles.css` is referenced in app
463: - ✅ **DO** use MudBlazor theme variables for colors
464: - ✅ **DO** test scope attributes in browser DevTools
465: 
466: ## Don'ts
467: 
468: - ❌ **DON'T** use `::deep` as first approach (prefer child's own CSS)
469: - ❌ **DON'T** style children from parent without wrapping
470: - ❌ **DON'T** forget to reference `{Project}.styles.css` bundle
471: - ❌ **DON'T** use global CSS for component-specific styles
472: - ❌ **DON'T** couple parent CSS to child's internal structure
473: - ❌ **DON'T** use inline styles (defeats isolation benefits)
474: 
475: ---
476: 
477: **Related Documentation**:
478: - [`docs/BLAZOR.md`](../../../docs/BLAZOR.md) - Blazor architecture and patterns
479: - [`blazor-ui-conventions`](../blazor-ui-conventions/SKILL.md) - MudBlazor and component design
480: - [`docs/QUICK_REFERENCE.md`](../../../docs/QUICK_REFERENCE.md) - Critical architectural rules
481: 
482: **Official References**:
483: - [ASP.NET Core Blazor CSS Isolation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/blazor/components/css-isolation)
484: - [BEM Methodology](http://getbem.com/introduction/)
485: - [MudBlazor Documentation](https://mudblazor.com/)
````

## File: .claude/skills/blazor-ui-conventions/resources/blazouter-routing.md
````markdown
 1: # Blazouter Routing Patterns
 2: 
 3: Use this when a Blazor app uses Blazouter instead of, or alongside, native `@page` routing.
 4: 
 5: ## Core Principles
 6: 
 7: - Keep routes in one place (for example `Routes.razor`) via `RouteConfig` entries.
 8: - Apply route guards at route definition time for authn/authz boundaries.
 9: - Keep route parameter names stable and consume them via `RouterStateService.GetParam(...)`.
10: - Register routing in DI and endpoint mapping (`AddBlazouter()` + `AddBlazouterSupport()`) before expecting route transitions/guards to work.
11: - Keep login/logout as client shim routes that force-load server auth endpoints when using BFF (`/login` -> `/auth/challenge`, `/logout` -> `/auth/signout`).
12: 
13: ## Required Setup (Blazor Web App Hybrid)
14: 
15: ```csharp
16: // Server Program.cs
17: builder.Services.AddBlazouter();
18: 
19: app.MapRazorComponents<App>()
20:     .AddBlazouterSupport()
21:     .AddInteractiveServerRenderMode()
22:     .AddInteractiveWebAssemblyRenderMode();
23: 
24: // WASM Client Program.cs
25: builder.Services.AddBlazouter();
26: builder.Services.AddScoped<AuthenticatedRouteGuard>();
27: builder.Services.AddScoped<AdminRouteGuard>();
28: builder.Services.AddScoped<OrgAdminRouteGuard>();
29: ```
30: 
31: ## Route Configuration Pattern
32: 
33: ```razor
34: <Blazouter.Components.Router Routes="@_routes" DefaultLayout="typeof(MainLayout)">
35:     <NotFound>
36:         <LayoutView Layout="typeof(MainLayout)">
37:             <p>Not found.</p>
38:         </LayoutView>
39:     </NotFound>
40: </Blazouter.Components.Router>
41: 
42: @code {
43:     private List<RouteConfig> _routes =
44:     [
45:         new RouteConfig { Path = "/events", Component = typeof(EventList), Guards = RequireAuthenticated(), Transition = RouteTransition.Fade },
46:         new RouteConfig { Path = "/event/detail/:eventId", Component = typeof(EventDetail), Guards = RequireAuthenticated(), Transition = RouteTransition.Fade },
47:         new RouteConfig { Path = "/startup", Component = typeof(StartupGate), Transition = RouteTransition.None, EnableCache = false }
48:     ];
49: }
50: ```
51: 
52: ## Parameter Access Pattern
53: 
54: ```csharp
55: [Inject] private RouterStateService RouterState { get; set; } = default!;
56: 
57: var idRaw = RouterState.GetParam("eventId");
58: if (!Guid.TryParse(idRaw, out var eventId))
59: {
60:     // Handle bad route parameter
61: }
62: ```
63: 
64: ## Guard Pattern
65: 
66: - Use `IRouteGuard` implementations for authenticated/admin/org-admin routes.
67: - Keep guard logic focused (one responsibility per guard).
68: - Use predictable redirect behavior for unauthorized access.
69: - Prefer `AuthenticationStateProvider` in guards so logic works across InteractiveServer and InteractiveWebAssembly.
70: 
71: ## Interop with Native Routing
72: 
73: - If `@page` directives exist, document which router is authoritative for each route set.
74: - Avoid duplicating the same logical route in both systems.
````

## File: .claude/skills/dotnet-efcore-guidelines/resources/named-query-filters.md
````markdown
 1: # Named Query Filters (EF Core 10+)
 2: 
 3: Named filters allow multiple global filters on the same entity and selective disabling in specific queries.
 4: 
 5: ## Why Named Filters
 6: 
 7: - Separate concerns: soft delete, tenancy, lifecycle visibility.
 8: - Disable one filter without disabling all filters.
 9: - Improve readability and auditability of model configuration.
10: 
11: ## Configuration Pattern
12: 
13: ```csharp
14: var currentTenantId = tenantContext.TenantId;
15: 
16: modelBuilder.Entity<Event>()
17:     .HasQueryFilter(name: "SoftDelete", predicate: e => !e.IsDeleted)
18:     .HasQueryFilter(name: "TenantFilter", predicate: e => e.TenantId == currentTenantId);
19: ```
20: 
21: ## Selective Disable Pattern
22: 
23: Use selective disable only in explicit administrative, migration, or audit flows.
24: 
25: ```csharp
26: var includingDeleted = await db.Events
27:     .IgnoreQueryFilters(["SoftDelete"])
28:     .ToListAsync(cancellationToken);
29: ```
30: 
31: ## Guardrails
32: 
33: - Default application flows should keep filters enabled.
34: - Disabling tenant filter in runtime request paths is usually a security bug.
35: - Keep filter names stable and centrally documented.
````

## File: .claude/skills/error-tracking/resources/loki-logging.md
````markdown
 1: # Loki Structured Logging
 2: 
 3: Use structured logs so queries remain reliable and cheap.
 4: 
 5: ## Required Log Structure
 6: 
 7: - Timestamp
 8: - Severity
 9: - Message template (not interpolated free text)
10: - Exception (if present)
11: - Context fields: `traceId`, `correlationId`, `requestPath`, `requestMethod`, `userId`, `tenantId`
12: 
13: ## Labels vs Fields
14: 
15: - Labels should be low-cardinality (`app`, `env`, `service`).
16: - High-cardinality data belongs in log fields, not labels.
17: 
18: ## API Logging Rules
19: 
20: - Log auth failures without raw token contents.
21: - Log validation failures at warning level with summarized field names.
22: - Log unexpected exceptions at error level with exception object.
23: - Keep personally sensitive data out of logs unless explicitly required and protected.
24: 
25: ## MediatR Integration
26: 
27: - Log start/end for command and query handling.
28: - Include elapsed time and request type.
29: - Emit warning when elapsed time crosses threshold.
````

## File: .claude/skills/error-tracking/resources/opentelemetry-tracing.md
````markdown
 1: # OpenTelemetry Tracing Patterns
 2: 
 3: Use traces to connect HTTP, application, and data-layer behavior.
 4: 
 5: ## Trace Pipeline
 6: 
 7: - Incoming HTTP request span
 8: - MediatR request span (command/query)
 9: - Database spans for repository calls
10: - External dependency spans (storage, auth provider, webhooks)
11: 
12: ## ActivitySource Guidelines
13: 
14: - Define one `ActivitySource` per service/application assembly.
15: - Use stable operation names (`Events.GetList`, `Events.Create`, etc.).
16: - Attach semantic tags (route, status_code, tenant, request_type).
17: 
18: ## Error Semantics
19: 
20: - Mark spans as error for exceptions.
21: - Add exception type/message as tags/events (redacted where needed).
22: - Correlate with ProblemDetails `traceId` returned to clients.
23: 
24: ## Performance Insights
25: 
26: - Track p50/p95/p99 at route and handler granularity.
27: - Flag slow spans using thresholds aligned with SLOs.
````

## File: .claude/skills/error-tracking/resources/prometheus-metrics.md
````markdown
 1: # Prometheus Metrics for API Services
 2: 
 3: Expose metrics for API behavior and latency.
 4: 
 5: ## Baseline Setup
 6: 
 7: - Register OpenTelemetry metrics.
 8: - Add Prometheus exporter.
 9: - Map scraping endpoint (commonly `/metrics`).
10: 
11: ## What to Measure
12: 
13: - HTTP request duration histogram
14: - Request count by route, method, status
15: - Active request gauge
16: - Database operation duration histogram
17: - MediatR request duration by request type
18: 
19: ## Cardinality Guardrails
20: 
21: - Do not label metrics with unbounded user input.
22: - Prefer route templates over raw URLs.
23: - Keep label sets small and stable.
24: 
25: ## Alerting-Ready Dimensions
26: 
27: - Service name
28: - Environment
29: - Tenant (only when bounded)
30: - Operation/request type
````

## File: .claude/skills/prd/SKILL.md
````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: prd
  3: description: "Generate a Product Requirements Document (PRD) for a new feature. Use when planning a feature, starting a new project, or when asked to create a PRD. Triggers on: create a prd, write prd for, plan this feature, requirements for, spec out."
  4: ---
  5: 
  6: # PRD Generator
  7: 
  8: Create detailed Product Requirements Documents that are clear, actionable, and suitable for implementation.
  9: 
 10: ---
 11: 
 12: ## The Job
 13: 
 14: 1. Receive a feature description from the user
 15: 2. Ask 3-5 essential clarifying questions (with lettered options)
 16: 3. Generate a structured PRD based on answers
 17: 4. Save to `dev/active/prd.md`
 18: 
 19: **Important:** Do NOT start implementing. Just create the PRD.
 20: 
 21: ---
 22: 
 23: ## Step 1: Clarifying Questions
 24: 
 25: Ask only critical questions where the initial prompt is ambiguous. Focus on:
 26: 
 27: - **Problem/Goal:** What problem does this solve?
 28: - **Core Functionality:** What are the key actions?
 29: - **Scope/Boundaries:** What should it NOT do?
 30: - **Success Criteria:** How do we know it's done?
 31: 
 32: ### Format Questions Like This:
 33: 
 34: ```
 35: 1. What is the primary goal of this feature?
 36:    A. Improve user onboarding experience
 37:    B. Increase user retention
 38:    C. Reduce support burden
 39:    D. Other: [please specify]
 40: 
 41: 2. Who is the target user?
 42:    A. New users only
 43:    B. Existing users only
 44:    C. All users
 45:    D. Admin users only
 46: 
 47: 3. What is the scope?
 48:    A. Minimal viable version
 49:    B. Full-featured implementation
 50:    C. Just the backend/API
 51:    D. Just the UI
 52: ```
 53: 
 54: This lets users respond with "1A, 2C, 3B" for quick iteration.
 55: 
 56: ---
 57: 
 58: ## Step 2: PRD Structure
 59: 
 60: Generate the PRD with these sections:
 61: 
 62: ### 1. Introduction/Overview
 63: 
 64: Brief description of the feature and the problem it solves.
 65: 
 66: ### 2. Goals
 67: 
 68: Specific, measurable objectives (bullet list).
 69: 
 70: ### 3. User Stories
 71: 
 72: Each story needs:
 73: 
 74: - **Title:** Short descriptive name
 75: - **Description:** "As a [user], I want [feature] so that [benefit]"
 76: - **Acceptance Criteria:** Verifiable checklist of what "done" means
 77: 
 78: Each story should be small enough to implement in one focused session.
 79: 
 80: **Format:**
 81: 
 82: ```markdown
 83: ### US-001: [Title]
 84: 
 85: **Description:** As a [user], I want [feature] so that [benefit].
 86: 
 87: **Acceptance Criteria:**
 88: 
 89: - [ ] Specific verifiable criterion
 90: - [ ] Another criterion
 91: - [ ] Typecheck/lint passes
 92: - [ ] **[UI stories only]** Verify in browser using dev-browser skill
 93: ```
 94: 
 95: **Important:**
 96: 
 97: - Acceptance criteria must be verifiable, not vague. "Works correctly" is bad. "Button shows confirmation dialog before deleting" is good.
 98: - **For any story with UI changes:** Always include "Verify in browser using dev-browser skill" as acceptance criteria. This ensures visual verification of frontend work.
 99: 
100: ### 4. Functional Requirements
101: 
102: Numbered list of specific functionalities:
103: 
104: - "FR-1: The system must allow users to..."
105: - "FR-2: When a user clicks X, the system must..."
106: 
107: Be explicit and unambiguous.
108: 
109: ### 5. Non-Goals (Out of Scope)
110: 
111: What this feature will NOT include. Critical for managing scope.
112: 
113: ### 6. Design Considerations (Optional)
114: 
115: - UI/UX requirements
116: - Link to mockups if available
117: - Relevant existing components to reuse
118: 
119: ### 7. Technical Considerations (Optional)
120: 
121: - Known constraints or dependencies
122: - Integration points with existing systems
123: - Performance requirements
124: 
125: ### 8. Success Metrics
126: 
127: How will success be measured?
128: 
129: - "Reduce time to complete X by 50%"
130: - "Increase conversion rate by 10%"
131: 
132: ### 9. Open Questions
133: 
134: Remaining questions or areas needing clarification.
135: 
136: ---
137: 
138: ## Writing for Junior Developers
139: 
140: The PRD reader may be a junior developer or AI agent. Therefore:
141: 
142: - Be explicit and unambiguous
143: - Avoid jargon or explain it
144: - Provide enough detail to understand purpose and core logic
145: - Number requirements for easy reference
146: - Use concrete examples where helpful
147: 
148: ---
149: 
150: ## Archiving Previous PRDs
151: 
152: **Before writing a new `dev/active/prd.md`, check if there is an existing one from a different feature:**
153: 
154: 1. Read the current `dev/active/prd.md` if it exists
155: 2. Check if it's for a different feature than what you're about to create
156: 3. If different:
157:    - Extract feature name from PRD title/intro
158:    - Check if archive folder already exists: look for `dev/archive/*-feature-name/`
159:    - If found, use existing folder; if not, create `dev/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-feature-name/`
160:    - Copy current `dev/active/prd.md` to archive folder
161:    - Write the new PRD to `dev/active/prd.md`
162: 
163: **Shared archive folders:** Multiple runs of same feature (across dates) share one archive folder. Prevents duplicate archives when PRD skill and task skill run on different days.
164: 
165: ---
166: 
167: ## Output
168: 
169: - **Format:** Markdown (`.md`)
170: - **Location:** `dev/active/`
171: - **Filename:** `dev/active/prd.md`
172: 
173: ---
174: 
175: ## Example PRD
176: 
177: ```markdown
178: # PRD: Task Priority System
179: 
180: ## Introduction
181: 
182: Add priority levels to tasks so users can focus on what matters most. Tasks can be marked as high, medium, or low priority, with visual indicators and filtering to help users manage their workload effectively.
183: 
184: ## Goals
185: 
186: - Allow assigning priority (high/medium/low) to any task
187: - Provide clear visual differentiation between priority levels
188: - Enable filtering and sorting by priority
189: - Default new tasks to medium priority
190: 
191: ## User Stories
192: 
193: ### US-001: Add priority field to database
194: 
195: **Description:** As a developer, I need to store task priority so it persists across sessions.
196: 
197: **Acceptance Criteria:**
198: 
199: - [ ] Add priority column to tasks table: 'high' | 'medium' | 'low' (default 'medium')
200: - [ ] Generate and run migration successfully
201: - [ ] Typecheck passes
202: 
203: ### US-002: Display priority indicator on task cards
204: 
205: **Description:** As a user, I want to see task priority at a glance so I know what needs attention first.
206: 
207: **Acceptance Criteria:**
208: 
209: - [ ] Each task card shows colored priority badge (red=high, yellow=medium, gray=low)
210: - [ ] Priority visible without hovering or clicking
211: 
212: ### US-003: Add priority selector to task edit
213: 
214: **Description:** As a user, I want to change a task's priority when editing it.
215: 
216: **Acceptance Criteria:**
217: 
218: - [ ] Priority dropdown in task edit modal
219: - [ ] Shows current priority as selected
220: - [ ] Saves immediately on selection change
221: 
222: ### US-004: Filter tasks by priority
223: 
224: **Description:** As a user, I want to filter the task list to see only high-priority items when I'm focused.
225: 
226: **Acceptance Criteria:**
227: 
228: - [ ] Filter dropdown with options: All | High | Medium | Low
229: - [ ] Filter persists in URL params
230: - [ ] Empty state message when no tasks match filter
231: 
232: ## Functional Requirements
233: 
234: - FR-1: Add `priority` field to tasks table ('high' | 'medium' | 'low', default 'medium')
235: - FR-2: Display colored priority badge on each task card
236: - FR-3: Include priority selector in task edit modal
237: - FR-4: Add priority filter dropdown to task list header
238: - FR-5: Sort by priority within each status column (high to medium to low)
239: 
240: ## Non-Goals
241: 
242: - No priority-based notifications or reminders
243: - No automatic priority assignment based on due date
244: - No priority inheritance for subtasks
245: 
246: ## Technical Considerations
247: 
248: - Reuse existing badge component with color variants
249: - Filter state managed via URL search params
250: - Priority stored in database, not computed
251: 
252: ## Success Metrics
253: 
254: - Users can change priority in under 2 clicks
255: - High-priority tasks immediately visible at top of lists
256: - No regression in task list performance
257: 
258: ## Open Questions
259: 
260: - Should priority affect task ordering within a column?
261: - Should we add keyboard shortcuts for priority changes?
262: ```
263: 
264: ---
265: 
266: ## Checklist
267: 
268: Before saving the PRD:
269: 
270: - [ ] **Archived previous PRD** (if `dev/active/prd.md` exists for a different feature, archive it first)
271: - [ ] Asked clarifying questions with lettered options
272: - [ ] Incorporated user's answers
273: - [ ] User stories are small and specific
274: - [ ] Functional requirements are numbered and unambiguous
275: - [ ] Non-goals section defines clear boundaries
276: - [ ] Saved to `dev/active/prd.md`
````

## File: dev/active/api-roadmap.md
````markdown
 1: Comprehensive Architectural Roadmap for 100% Perfect Enterprise-Grade APIs in ASP.NET Core 10
 2: The transition to.NET 10 establishes a new baseline for enterprise-grade performance and security. This roadmap outlines the evolution from a standard implementation to a "perfect" API, specifically addressing the integration of Cerbos for authorization, high-end caching with HybridCache, and a complete observability suite via OpenTelemetry.   
 3: 
 4: 1. Architectural Integrity: From Basic Layers to Clean/SOLID
 5: A perfect API must strictly separate business rules from technical implementation. The core gap in many current APIs is "architectural drift," where infrastructure concerns (like database logic) leak into the domain.   
 6: 
 7: Current State: Standard N-Tier (Web -> Services -> Data).
 8: 
 9: Perfect State: Clean Architecture with strict inward dependencies.   
10: 
11: Domain Layer: Must be the center, containing Entities, Aggregates, and Value Objects. All classes should be sealed by default to prevent unintended inheritance.
12: 
13: Application Layer: Contains Use Cases (Commands/Queries) using the Result Pattern instead of exceptions to handle expected business failures (e.g., "Insufficient Funds" is a result, not an exception).   
14: 
15: Infrastructure Layer: Implements external concerns (EF Core 10, SMTP clients).
16: 
17: Drift Prevention: Implement NetArchTest in the CI/CD pipeline to automatically fail builds if a Domain layer project references an Infrastructure layer.   
18: 
19: 2. Security & Identity: Advanced AuthN/AuthZ
20: The primary advancement in.NET 10 is the native support for phishing-resistant authentication through WebAuthn Passkeys.
21: 
22: Authentication (AuthN)
23: Missing: Transitioning from passwords to Passkeys. ASP.NET Core Identity 10 provides built-in endpoints via MapIdentityApi that support FIDO2/WebAuthn ceremonies.
24: 
25: Hardening: Enforce JWT Rotation. Every token must have a short lifespan (5–15 minutes) with a mandatory refresh token rotation to mitigate token hijacking.   
26: 
27: Authorization (AuthZ): The Cerbos Implementation
28: To reach 100% perfection, authorization logic is decoupled from the code into external policies managed by Cerbos.
29: 
30: Cerbos Integration: Implement a custom IAuthorizationHandler that communicates with the Cerbos PDP (Policy Decision Point) via gRPC or REST.
31: 
32: Resiliency Fallback (Error Factor): A perfect API must handle the unavailability of its authorization engine.
33: 
34: Primary: Call Cerbos PDP for a fine-grained ABAC (Attribute-Based Access Control) decision.
35: 
36: Fallback: Use a Polly v9 Resilience Pipeline to detect PDP timeouts or connection errors.   
37: 
38: Default Policy: If Cerbos is unreachable, fall back to a local, restrictive Claims-Based Policy (e.g., check User.IsInRole("Admin")) to ensure the system remains secure but functional during outages.
39: 
40: 3. Data & State: Optimized Persistence and Caching
41: The bottleneck of most APIs is the database..NET 10 introduces the HybridCache API to solve the thundering herd problem.   
42: 
43: Persistence: Use EF Core 10 with Compiled Queries for hot paths and AsNoTracking() for read-only operations.   
44: 
45: Multi-Level Caching (L1/L2):
46: 
47: L1: In-process memory cache for sub-millisecond access.
48: 
49: L2: Distributed cache (Redis) for consistency across a web farm.
50: 
51: HybridCache: Coordinates L1/L2 automatically and provides Stampede Protection, ensuring only one concurrent request hits the database for a specific key during a cache miss.
52: 
53: 4. Communication: SMTP and Background Processing
54: A perfect enterprise API isolates long-running tasks to maintain responsiveness.   
55: 
56: SMTP Service: Isolated behind an IEmailSender interface. In production, use Sinch Mailgun or Amazon SES for high deliverability and ML-based send-time optimization.
57: 
58: Background Jobs:
59: 
60: Native BackgroundService: Use for simple polling or continuous loops.
61: 
62: Hangfire: Use for user-triggered workflows requiring a dashboard, persistence (surviving restarts), and automatic retries.
63: 
64: 5. Observability: Proactive Analytics and Metrics
65: Observability is the "Analytics" engine of a high-end API. In 2026, the standard is OpenTelemetry (OTel).   
66: 
67: Structured Logging: Use Serilog with the OTLP (OpenTelemetry Protocol) sink. All logs must include TraceId and SpanId to correlate logs across distributed services.   
68: 
69: Metrics & Analytics: Use the System.Diagnostics.Metrics API to track:
70: 
71: Technical Metrics: P95 Latency, CPU/Memory usage.   
72: 
73: Business Analytics: Count of successful logins, items added to carts, or payment failures, enriched with custom dimensions like TenantId or Region using OTel Meters.   
74: 
75: 6. Implementation Gap Checklist: Standard vs. Perfect
76: Feature	Standard Implementation (Current)	Perfect Enterprise Implementation (Missing/Target)
77: AuthZ	Hardcoded Role Checks	Cerbos PDP with Polly-backed Local Fallback
78: Caching	IDistributedCache (Redis)	HybridCache (L1+L2) with Stampede Protection
79: AuthN	Password + 2FA	WebAuthn Passkeys (Phishing-Resistant)
80: Runtime	Dynamic JIT	
81: Native AOT (Zero-reflection, Instant Startup) 
82: 
83: Analytics	Text-based Logging	
84: OpenTelemetry with Dimensional Business Metrics 
85: 
86: Testing	Unit + Integration	
87: Unit + Integration + Architecture Tests (NetArchTest) 
88: 
89:   
90: 7. Quality Assurance: The Testing Hierarchy
91: A perfect API ensures no architectural regression occurs during rapid development.   
92: 
93: Unit Tests (xUnit/FluentAssertions): Test domain logic in isolation without any database or network calls.   
94: 
95: Integration Tests (TestContainers): Spin up real Docker containers for SQL Server, Redis, and Cerbos PDP during the test run to ensure compatibility.   
96: 
97: Architecture Tests (NetArchTest): Enforce naming conventions (e.g., "All Repositories must end with 'Repository'") and layer boundaries.
````

````markdown
  1: # Blazor Advanced Filtering — Implementation Plan
  2: 
  3: **Last Updated**: 2026-02-12
  4: 
  5: ---
  6: 
  7: ## Executive Summary
  8: 
  9: The API layer has a fully implemented advanced query specification system with **33 query parameters** for events, including module-conditional Islamic and Tech aspect filters. The Blazor frontend currently only exposes **8 of these filters** and has **zero module-capability awareness**. This plan covers the work needed to bring the Blazor EventList page to full parity with the API, with filters conditionally displayed based on the tenant's enabled modules.
 10: 
 11: ### Key Gap
 12: 
 13: | Layer | Filters Exposed | Module Awareness |
 14: |-------|----------------|------------------|
 15: | API (EventController) | 33 params | Yes (handler checks `IModuleService`) |
 16: | NSwag Client (auto-generated) | 33 params | N/A (pass-through) |
 17: | IEventService wrapper | 13 params | No |
 18: | EventList UI | 8 dropdowns | No |
 19: 
 20: ---
 21: 
 22: ## Current State Analysis
 23: 
 24: ### What the API Supports (EventController.GetAll)
 25: 
 26: **Always-available filters (16):**
 27: - searchTerm, categoryId, tagId, formatId, madhabId, locationId, registrationModeId, languageId, dateFrom, dateTo, eventTypeId, audienceGenderId, audienceAgeId, eventStatusId, sortBy, sortDescending
 28: 
 29: **Islamic aspect filters (5) — gated by `Mod_Islamic`:**
 30: - genderModeId, includesQuranRecitation, referencePrayerId, islamicPrimaryLanguageId, hasIslamicAspect
 31: 
 32: **Tech aspect filters (6) — gated by `Mod_Tech`:**
 33: - skillLevelId, isCodingCompetition, isHackathon, requiresLaptop, techStackTag, hasTechAspect
 34: 
 35: **JSONB metadata filters (2):**
 36: - metadataJsonContains, metadataJsonKeyExists
 37: 
 38: ### What Blazor Currently Has
 39: 
 40: **EventList.razor** — 8 filter dropdowns:
 41: - Date (predefined ranges), Category, Location, Format, Madhab, Registration Mode, Language, Tags
 42: 
 43: **IEventService.GetEventsPagedAsync** — passes 13 params:
 44: - pageNumber, pageSize, searchTerm, categoryId, tagId, formatId, madhabId, locationId, registrationModeId, languageId, dateFrom, dateTo, sortBy, sortDescending
 45: 
 46: **Missing from IEventService:**
 47: - eventTypeId, audienceGenderId, audienceAgeId, eventStatusId
 48: - All 5 Islamic aspect filters
 49: - All 6 Tech aspect filters
 50: - 2 JSONB metadata filters
 51: 
 52: **PublicExperienceSettingsDto** — has NO module capability info:
 53: - TenantId, DeploymentMode, PreferredHomePage, BrandDisplayName, BrandLogoUrl, BrandFaviconUrl, BrandCustomCssUrl, InstanceBaseDomain, Subdomain, CustomDomain
 54: - **Zero module enablement flags**
 55: 
 56: ### Blazor Client Already Has
 57: 
 58: - Enums: `GenderSegregationMode`, `PrayerTime`, `SkillLevel` in `Models/Responses/EventAspectEnums.cs`
 59: - Aspect display: `EventIslamicAspectCard.razor`, `EventTechAspectCard.razor`
 60: - Aspect edit dialogs: `IslamicAspectEditDialog.razor`, `TechAspectEditDialog.razor`
 61: - NSwag client: Already accepts ALL 33 parameters in `GetEventsAsync()`
 62: 
 63: ---
 64: 
 65: ## Proposed Future State
 66: 
 67: ### Architecture
 68: 
 69: ```
 70: PublicExperience/settings endpoint
 71:     └─ Returns: PublicExperienceSettingsDto (ENHANCED with module flags)
 72:         ├─ IsIslamicModuleEnabled: bool

 76: EventList.razor
 77:     ├─ Injects IPublicExperienceService

 79:     ├─ Renders CORE filter section (always visible)

 81:     ├─ Conditionally renders TECH filter section (if Mod_Tech enabled)
 82:     ├─ Renders SORTING section (always visible)
 83:     └─ Calls IEventService with ALL applicable filter params
 84: 
 85: IEventService.GetEventsPagedAsync
 86:     └─ Updated signature with ALL 33 parameters

 88: ```
 89: 
 90: ### UI Layout (Filter Bar)
 91: 
 92: ```
 93: ┌─── Always Visible ────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 94: │ [Date▼] [Category▼] [Location▼] [Format▼] [Event Type▼]     │
 95: │ [Madhab▼] [Registration▼] [Language▼] [Tags▼]               │

334: #### Task 6.3: Integration Test — Filter Parameter Pass-Through
335: - **File:** `Event.API.IntegrationTests/`
336: - **Change:** Verify aspect filters are silently ignored when module disabled
337: - **Acceptance:**
338:   - [ ] Test: Islamic filter with module disabled → 200 OK, filters ignored
339:   - [ ] Test: Islamic filter with module enabled → 200 OK, filters applied

341: ---

343: ## Risk Assessment
344: 
345: | Risk | Impact | Likelihood | Mitigation |
346: |------|--------|------------|------------|
347: | NSwag client regeneration breaks existing code | High | Low | Client already has all params; regeneration only for PublicExperience model |
348: | Module flags add latency to PublicExperience endpoint | Low | Low | ModuleService has caching built-in |

358: 2. **Conditional rendering**: Islamic/Tech filter sections only visible when module is enabled
359: 3. **No regression**: Existing 8 filters continue working identically
360: 4. **Performance**: No measurable increase in page load time
361: 5. **Tests passing**: All unit and component tests green

363: ---

365: ## Dependencies
366:

368: - NSwag client already supports all 33 parameters

## File: dev/active/blazor-api-sync/blazor-api-sync-plan.md
````markdown
  1: # Blazor-API Synchronization - Implementation Plan
  2: 
  3: > **Comprehensive refactor to bring Blazor frontend in sync with API capabilities**
  4: >
  5: > Created: 2026-01-31
  6: 
  7: ## Executive Summary
  8: 
  9: The API has significantly evolved with HATEOAS support, Event Aspects (Islamic/Tech), enhanced DTOs, and new federation features. The Blazor frontend currently uses hardcoded routes and lacks UI for Event Aspects entirely. This plan addresses the gap by:
 10: 
 11: 1. Implementing a HATEOAS-aware service layer for hypermedia-driven navigation
 12: 2. Creating Event Aspects UI components (Islamic and Tech)
 13: 3. Synchronizing all domain entities between API and Blazor
 14: 4. Maintaining existing patterns (MudBlazor, BEM, BFF architecture)
 15: 
 16: **Estimated Effort**: 3-4 development sessions
 17: **Risk Level**: Medium (non-breaking changes, additive functionality)
 18: 
 19: ---
 20: 
 21: ## Current State Analysis
 22: 
 23: ### API Capabilities (Available)
 24: 
 25: | Feature | Status | Notes |
 26: |---------|--------|-------|
 27: | HATEOAS Links | Implemented | 28+ link policies, HAL format responses |
 28: | Event Aspects | Implemented | Islamic and Tech aspects with full CQRS |
 29: | Pagination | Implemented | PagedResponse with metadata |
 30: | Federation (ATProto) | Implemented | PDS sync outbox, IndexedDid |
 31: | Multi-tenancy | Implemented | Virtual tenant masking |
 32: | Module System | Partial | ModuleDefinition entity exists |
 33: 
 34: ### Blazor Capabilities (Current)
 35: 
 36: | Feature | Status | Gap |
 37: |---------|--------|-----|
 38: | HATEOAS Consumption | Missing | Hardcoded routes in services |
 39: | Event Aspects UI | Missing | No components, no services |
 40: | Pagination UI | Partial | Uses PagedResponse but no MudTable virtualization |
 41: | Federation UI | Missing | No ATProto management UI |
 42: | Multi-tenancy UI | Missing | No tenant switching UI |
 43: 
 44: ### Critical Gaps Identified
 45: 
 46: 1. **HATEOAS Not Consumed**: EventService uses `_apiClient.EventGET2Async(eventId)` with hardcoded method names instead of following `_links`
 47: 2. **Event Aspects Missing**: EventDto includes `IslamicAspect` and `TechAspect` but Blazor ignores them
 48: 3. **NSwag Client Ignores Links**: Generated client returns DTOs but discards HATEOAS metadata
 49: 4. **No Link-Based Navigation**: Blazor uses `Href="/events"` instead of following API links
 50: 
 51: ---
 52: 
 53: ## Proposed Architecture
 54: 
 55: ### HATEOAS Consumption Strategy
 56: 
 57: **Option A: Link-Aware Service Wrapper** (Recommended)
 58: ```
 59: EventService -> HateoasClient -> NSwag Client -> API
 60:                     |
 61:                     v
 62:               Link Resolution
 63: ```
 64: 
 65: **Option B: Custom HTTP Client with Link Parsing**
 66: ```
 67: EventService -> HateoasHttpClient -> API
 68:                     |
 69:                     v
 70:               Parse _links from response
 71: ```
 72: 
 73: **Decision**: Option A - Wrap existing NSwag client to preserve type safety while adding link awareness.
 74: 
 75: ### Component Architecture for Event Aspects
 76: 
 77: ```
 78: EventDetail.razor
 79:     |
 80:     +-- EventIslamicAspectCard.razor (conditional)
 81:     |       |
 82:     |       +-- IslamicAspectEditDialog.razor
 83:     |
 84:     +-- EventTechAspectCard.razor (conditional)
 85:             |
 86:             +-- TechAspectEditDialog.razor
 87: ```
 88: 
 89: ---
 90: 
 91: ## Implementation Phases
 92: 
 93: ### Phase 1: HATEOAS Foundation (Priority: High)

 95: **Goal**: Create infrastructure for consuming HATEOAS links from API responses
 96: 
 97: #### Task 1.1: Create HateoasLink Model

 99: - **Purpose**: Represent `_links` from API responses
100: - **Acceptance**: Model can deserialize HAL-format links

102: #### Task 1.2: Create IHateoasClient Interface
103: - **File**: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Services/Contracts/IHateoasClient.cs`
104: - **Purpose**: Define contract for link-aware API calls
105: - **Methods**:
106:   - `Task<T?> FollowLinkAsync<T>(HateoasLink link)`
107:   - `Task<T?> GetWithLinksAsync<T>(string url)` where T : IHasLinks
108:   - `Task<TResult?> ExecuteActionAsync<TResult>(HateoasLink link, object? payload)`
109: - **Acceptance**: Interface compiles, follows SOLID principles

113: - **Purpose**: HTTP client that parses and follows HATEOAS links

115: - **Acceptance**: Can GET a resource and extract its `_links`

## File: dev/active/blazor-performance/blazor-performance-plan.md
````markdown
  1: # Blazor Performance Optimization - Implementation Plan
  2: 
  3: ## Executive Summary
  4: 
  5: Comprehensive performance optimization of the Blazor frontend (`Explore.Blazor` + `Explore.Blazor.Client`) targeting rendering efficiency, bundle size reduction, memory management, and client-side caching. Both projects currently target net9.0 while the rest of the solution targets net10.0, missing significant .NET 10 Blazor performance improvements.
  6: 
  7: ## Current State Analysis
  8: 
  9: ### Architecture
 10: - **Blazor Hybrid**: Server (`Explore.Blazor`) + WASM Client (`Explore.Blazor.Client`)
 11: - **BFF Pattern**: YARP reverse proxy in Blazor Server -> API (`/api/{**catch-all}`)
 12: - **Auth Flow**: Keycloak OIDC -> Cookie auth on server -> `CircuitAccessTokenService` -> token forwarding via YARP
 13: - **Render Mode**: `InteractiveAuto` on Routes (server-first, then WASM after download)
 14: - **UI Framework**: MudBlazor 8.5.0
 15: 
 16: ### Critical Performance Issues (Ordered by Impact)
 17: 
 18: | # | Issue | Impact |
 19: |---|-------|--------|
 20: | 1 | **net9.0 targeting** | Missing .NET 10 Blazor perf: 76% smaller blazor.web.js, WasmStripILAfterAOT, [PersistentState] |
 21: | 2 | **38,874-line NSwag client** | Massive WASM bundle bloat, single monolithic file |
 22: | 3 | **Newtonsoft.Json in WASM** | Heavier than System.Text.Json, no AOT optimization |
 23: | 4 | **0 Virtualize components** | 46 @foreach loops rendering all items regardless of count |
 24: | 5 | **27 StateHasChanged() calls** | Potential unnecessary cascading re-renders |
 25: | 6 | **0 StreamRendering** | No `@attribute [StreamRendering]` on any page |
 26: | 7 | **No client-side HTTP caching** | Every navigation re-fetches data from API |
 27: | 8 | **0 IDisposable/IAsyncDisposable** | Potential memory leaks across 127 .razor components |
 28: | 9 | **No Polly resilience** | HttpClient calls have no retry/circuit-breaker |
 29: | 10 | **No request deduplication** | Concurrent identical API requests not merged |
 30: 
 31: ### Key Metrics (Pre-Optimization Baseline)
 32: - **127 .razor files** total across both projects
 33: - **46 @foreach loops** (candidates for virtualization)
 34: - **27 StateHasChanged()** calls (audit needed)
 35: - **38,874 lines** NSwag generated client
 36: - **1 cache service** (LookupCacheService, 10-min MemoryCache TTL)
 37: - **0 Virtualize** components
 38: - **0 StreamRendering** attributes
 39: - **0 IDisposable** implementations on components
 40: 
 41: ---
 42: 
 43: ## Implementation Phases
 44: 
 45: ### Phase 1: Upgrade to .NET 10 + Enable Platform Features
 46: **Priority**: CRITICAL | **Estimated effort**: 2-3 hours
 47: **Why first**: Unblocks all .NET 10 Blazor features used in later phases.
 48: 
 49: - **Task 1.1**: Upgrade `Explore.Blazor.csproj` from net9.0 to net10.0
 50:   - Acceptance: `<TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>`, builds clean
 51: - **Task 1.2**: Upgrade `Explore.Blazor.Client.csproj` from net9.0 to net10.0
 52:   - Acceptance: `<TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>`, builds clean
 53: - **Task 1.3**: Enable `WasmStripILAfterAOT` in Blazor.Client csproj (strips IL after AOT, 20-50% smaller bundle)
 54:   - Acceptance: `<WasmStripILAfterAOT>true</WasmStripILAfterAOT>` in csproj
 55: - **Task 1.4**: Enable static web asset fingerprinting for cache-busting
 56:   - Acceptance: Verify fingerprinting is enabled (default in .NET 10)
 57: - **Task 1.5**: Update any net9.0-specific API calls or breaking changes
 58:   - Acceptance: Full solution builds with 0 errors, 0 warnings from Blazor projects
 59: - **Task 1.6**: Verify MudBlazor 8.5.0 compatibility with net10.0
 60:   - Acceptance: MudBlazor components render correctly after upgrade
 61: 
 62: **Risk**: Breaking changes between net9.0 and net10.0. Mitigation: Build frequently, fix incrementally.
 63: 
 64: ---
 65: 
 66: ### Phase 2: Rendering Optimization
 67: **Priority**: HIGH | **Estimated effort**: 4-6 hours
 68: **Why**: Eliminates unnecessary re-renders and improves perceived performance.
 69: 
 70: - **Task 2.1**: Audit all 27 `StateHasChanged()` calls — remove unnecessary ones
 71:   - Acceptance: Each remaining call justified with comment; unnecessary calls removed
 72: - **Task 2.2**: Add `@key` directives to all `@foreach` loops with identifiable items
 73:   - Acceptance: All @foreach loops over entities use `@key="item.Id"` or equivalent
 74: - **Task 2.3**: Implement `ShouldRender()` override on expensive components
 75:   - Acceptance: Components with heavy render trees override ShouldRender with parameter change detection
 76: - **Task 2.4**: Replace large-list `@foreach` loops with `<Virtualize>` or `<MudVirtualize>`
 77:   - Acceptance: Lists that can grow beyond ~50 items use virtualization
 78:   - Note: Only where items have uniform height and virtualization makes UX sense
 79: - **Task 2.5**: Add `@attribute [StreamRendering]` to data-heavy pages
 80:   - Acceptance: Pages that load data show immediate skeleton/loading then stream content
 81: - **Task 2.6**: Implement `[PersistentState]` for component state preservation (net10.0 feature)
 82:   - Acceptance: Key form states survive prerendering without re-fetch
 83: 
 84: **Risk**: Virtualize requires uniform item height. Some lists may not be suitable.
 85: 
 86: ---
 87: 
 88: ### Phase 3: Bundle Size Reduction (NSwag + Newtonsoft)
 89: **Priority**: HIGH | **Estimated effort**: 3-5 hours
 90: **Why**: 38K-line NSwag client + Newtonsoft.Json is the largest WASM bundle contributor.
 91: 
 92: - **Task 3.1**: Evaluate NSwag client splitting strategy
 93:   - Option A: Configure NSwag to generate partial classes per controller
 94:   - Option B: Switch to Kiota/openapi-generator with tree-shaking support
 95:   - Acceptance: Decision documented, approach selected
 96: - **Task 3.2**: Migrate HalResourceExtensions from Newtonsoft.Json/JObject to System.Text.Json
 97:   - File: `Explore.Blazor.Client/Helpers/HalResourceExtensions.cs`
 98:   - Acceptance: Newtonsoft.Json removed from Blazor.Client.csproj, STJ used instead
 99: - **Task 3.3**: Remove Newtonsoft.Json package reference from Blazor.Client
100:   - Acceptance: No Newtonsoft references in Blazor.Client project
101: - **Task 3.4**: Configure NSwag to generate System.Text.Json serialization (instead of Newtonsoft)
102:   - Acceptance: nswag.json updated, regenerated client uses STJ
103: - **Task 3.5**: Enable Blazor WASM lazy loading for non-critical assemblies
104:   - Acceptance: Initial download only includes critical assemblies; others load on demand
105: 
106: **Risk**: NSwag client regeneration may introduce breaking changes. Newtonsoft->STJ migration requires careful HAL link handling.
107: 
108: ---
109: 
110: ### Phase 4: Client-Side Caching & API Optimization
111: **Priority**: MEDIUM-HIGH | **Estimated effort**: 3-4 hours
112: **Why**: Every navigation currently re-fetches all data from API.
113: 
114: - **Task 4.1**: Implement client-side HTTP response caching service
115:   - Pattern: In-memory cache keyed by URL + query params with configurable TTL
116:   - Acceptance: Repeated navigation to same page doesn't re-fetch if data is fresh
117: - **Task 4.2**: Add Polly resilience policies to HttpClient (retry + circuit breaker)
118:   - Acceptance: Transient HTTP failures auto-retry; circuit opens on sustained failure
119: - **Task 4.3**: Implement request deduplication for concurrent identical requests
120:   - Pattern: SemaphoreSlim or ConcurrentDictionary<string, Task> to coalesce in-flight requests
121:   - Acceptance: 5 concurrent calls to same endpoint result in 1 actual HTTP request
122: - **Task 4.4**: Enhance LookupCacheService with cache invalidation on write operations
123:   - Acceptance: Cache entries invalidated when user performs create/update/delete
124: - **Task 4.5**: Add HTTP ETag/If-None-Match support for conditional GET requests
125:   - Acceptance: API responses with ETag are cached; 304 Not Modified avoids re-download
126: 
127: **Risk**: Cache invalidation complexity. Stale data risk. Mitigation: Conservative TTLs, manual invalidation on writes.
128: 
129: ---
130: 
131: ### Phase 5: Render Mode Optimization
132: **Priority**: MEDIUM | **Estimated effort**: 2-3 hours
133: **Why**: Not all pages need WebAssembly interactivity; some can be server-rendered or static.
134: 
135: - **Task 5.1**: Audit all pages and categorize render mode requirements
136:   - Categories: Static (no interactivity), Server (admin, low-traffic), Auto (public, high-traffic)
137:   - Acceptance: Spreadsheet/table of all pages with recommended render mode
138: - **Task 5.2**: Apply `@rendermode` per-page where beneficial
139:   - Acceptance: Admin pages use Server mode; public read-only pages use Static/SSR where possible
140: - **Task 5.3**: Configure enhanced navigation and form handling
141:   - Acceptance: Enhanced navigation enabled for seamless SPA-like transitions
142: 
143: **Risk**: Render mode changes affect component state and event handling. Test each page after change.
144: 
145: ---
146: 
147: ### Phase 6: JS Interop Optimization
148: **Priority**: LOW-MEDIUM | **Estimated effort**: 1-2 hours
149: **Why**: JS interop calls are expensive in Blazor; batching reduces overhead.
150: 
151: - **Task 6.1**: Audit all IJSRuntime calls across components
152:   - Acceptance: List of all JS interop usage with frequency assessment
153: - **Task 6.2**: Batch JS interop calls where multiple calls happen in sequence
154:   - Acceptance: Sequential JS calls consolidated into single batched call
155: - **Task 6.3**: Use .NET 10 direct JS property access where applicable
156:   - Acceptance: Simple property reads use direct access instead of InvokeAsync
157: 
158: **Risk**: Low. JS interop optimization is incremental.
159: 
160: ---
161: 
162: ### Phase 7: Memory Management & Lifecycle
163: **Priority**: MEDIUM | **Estimated effort**: 3-4 hours
164: **Why**: 0 IDisposable implementations across 127 components = potential memory leaks.
165: 
166: - **Task 7.1**: Audit all components for disposable resources (event handlers, timers, JS interop refs)
167:   - Acceptance: Every component with subscriptions/timers/JS refs identified
168: - **Task 7.2**: Implement `IAsyncDisposable` on components with disposable resources
169:   - Acceptance: All identified components properly dispose resources
170: - **Task 7.3**: Configure Blazor Server circuit options (idle timeout, max retained circuits)
171:   - Acceptance: Circuit options configured in Program.cs with appropriate values
172: - **Task 7.4**: Implement `@implements IAsyncDisposable` pattern with DotNetObjectReference cleanup
173:   - Acceptance: All DotNetObjectReference instances disposed in DisposeAsync
174: 
175: **Risk**: Missing a component with leaks. Mitigation: Systematic audit with grep.
176: 
177: ---
178: 
179: ### Phase 8: Observability & Measurement
180: **Priority**: LOW | **Estimated effort**: 1-2 hours
181: **Why**: Can't improve what you can't measure.
182: 
183: - **Task 8.1**: Add Blazor-specific OpenTelemetry metrics (circuit count, render duration)
184:   - Acceptance: Metrics exportable to existing observability stack
185: - **Task 8.2**: Add performance markers for key user journeys (page load, search, event detail)
186:   - Acceptance: Navigation Timing API data captured for critical paths
187: - **Task 8.3**: Configure .NET 10 circuit metrics (if available)
188:   - Acceptance: Circuit lifecycle metrics captured
189: 
190: **Risk**: None. Observability-only, no functional changes.
191: 
192: ---
193: 
194: ## Risk Assessment
195: 
196: | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
197: |------|-----------|--------|------------|
198: | net10.0 upgrade breaks MudBlazor | Low | High | Check MudBlazor 8.5.0 net10.0 compat before upgrading |
199: | NSwag regeneration breaks client | Medium | High | Diff generated file before/after; test all API calls |
200: | Newtonsoft -> STJ breaks HAL parsing | Medium | Medium | Write tests for HAL extension methods before migrating |
201: | Virtualize breaks existing layouts | Low | Low | Only apply where item height is uniform |
202: | Cache staleness | Medium | Medium | Conservative TTLs (30s-2min), manual invalidation on writes |
203: 
204: ## Success Metrics
205: 
206: | Metric | Before | Target |
207: |--------|--------|--------|
208: | WASM bundle size (published) | TBD (measure) | -30% or more |
209: | blazor.web.js size | ~148KB | ~35KB (76% reduction from .NET 10) |
210: | Initial page load (LCP) | TBD (measure) | < 2.5s |
211: | Unnecessary re-renders | ~27 StateHasChanged calls | < 10 justified calls |
212: | Virtualized lists | 0 | All lists > 50 items |
213: | Memory leaks (circuit) | Unknown | 0 (all resources disposed) |
214: | Client cache hit ratio | 0% | > 60% for repeated navigation |
215: 
216: ## Timeline Estimate
217: 
218: | Phase | Effort | Dependencies |
219: |-------|--------|-------------|
220: | Phase 1: net10.0 Upgrade | 2-3h | None |
221: | Phase 2: Rendering | 4-6h | Phase 1 |
222: | Phase 3: Bundle Size | 3-5h | Phase 1 |
223: | Phase 4: Client Caching | 3-4h | None (can parallel with Phase 2-3) |
224: | Phase 5: Render Modes | 2-3h | Phase 1 |
225: | Phase 6: JS Interop | 1-2h | Phase 1 |
226: | Phase 7: Memory | 3-4h | None |
227: | Phase 8: Observability | 1-2h | Phase 1 |
228: | **Total** | **19-29h** | |
229: 
230: Phases 2, 3, 4, 5 can partially overlap. Critical path: Phase 1 -> Phase 2+3 (parallel) -> Phase 4-8.
````

149: ## 🏆 ENTERPRISE PATTERNS CODIFIED
150: 
151: ### Pattern 1: C# 12+ Primary Constructors
152: 
153: **Why**: Reduces boilerplate, improves readability, aligns with .NET 8+ best practices.
154: 
155: **Before** (verbose):
156: ```csharp
157: public class EventService : IEventService
158: {
159:     private readonly IEventRepository _eventRepository;
160:     private readonly IMapper _mapper;
161: 
162:     public EventService(IEventRepository eventRepository, IMapper mapper)
163:     {
164:         _eventRepository = eventRepository;
165:         _mapper = mapper;
166:     }
167: }
168: ```
169: 
170: **After** (clean):
171: ```csharp
172: public class EventService(
173:     IEventRepository eventRepository,
174:     IMapper mapper) : IEventService
175: {
176:     // Constructor parameters available as fields
177: }
178: ```
179: 
180: ---
181: 
182: ### Pattern 2: MudBlazor ParameterState
183: 
184: **Why**: Prevents infinite re-render loops in MudBlazor components.
185: 
186: **Implementation**:
187: ```csharp
188: @using MudBlazor.State
189: 
190: private readonly ParameterState<EventDto> _eventState;
191: 
192: [Parameter]
193: public EventDto Event
194: {
195:     get => _eventState.Value;
196:     set => _eventState.SetValue(value);
197: }
198: 
199: public EventCard()
200: {
201:     _eventState = new(this);
202: }
203: ```
204: 
205: ---
206: 
207: ### Pattern 3: CSS Isolation with BEM
208: 
209: **Why**: Component-scoped styles + explicit BEM naming = no collisions + maintainability.
210: 
211: **Structure**:
212: ```
213: EventCard.razor          (component markup with BEM classes)
214: EventCard.razor.css      (scoped CSS with BEM selectors)
215: ```
216: 
217: **Compiled**:
218: ```css
219: /* Author */
220: .event-card__title { font-weight: 600; }
221: 
222: /* Blazor compiles to */
223: .event-card__title[b-xyz123] { font-weight: 600; }
224: ```
225: 
226: ---
227: 
228: ### Pattern 4: DbContext Pooling (EF Core 10+)
229: 
230: **Why**: 10x performance improvement on high-throughput workloads.
231: 
232: **Implementation**:
233: ```csharp
234: // DbContext with property injection
235: public class AppDbContext : DbContext
236: {
237:     public ITenantContext? TenantContext { get; set; }
238:     // ...
239: }
240: 
241: // Registration
242: builder.Services.AddDbContextPool<AppDbContext>((provider, options) =>
243: {
244:     options.UseNpgsql(connectionString);
245: });
246: ```
247: 
248: ---
249: 
250: ### Pattern 5: Named Query Filters (EF Core 10+)
251: 
252: **Why**: Allows selective disabling of filters (e.g., show soft-deleted for admin).
253: 
254: **Implementation**:
255: ```csharp
256: modelBuilder.Entity<Event>()
257:     .HasQueryFilter(name: "SoftDelete", predicate: e => !e.IsDeleted);
258: 
259: // Disable when needed
260: var allEvents = await _dbContext.Events
261:     .IgnoreQueryFilter("SoftDelete")
262:     .ToListAsync();
263: ```
264: 
265: ---
266: 
267: ### Pattern 6: BaseCommandResponse for ALL Commands
268: 
269: **Why**: Consistent error handling, validation messages, success/failure distinction.
270: 
271: **CRITICAL**: Delete commands too (no bool returns).
272: 
273: **Implementation**:
274: ```csharp
275: // ❌ WRONG
276: public class DeleteEventCommand : IRequest<bool>
277: 
278: // ✅ CORRECT
279: public class DeleteEventCommand : IRequest<BaseCommandResponse<Guid>>
280: ```
281:

199: **Add Section 13: Delete Commands Return bool**
200: ```markdown
201: ### 13. Delete Commands Return bool (Not BaseCommandResponse)
202: 
203: Delete commands follow a different pattern than create/update:
204: 
205: // ❌ WRONG - Don't use BaseCommandResponse for deletes
206: public class DeleteEventCommand : IRequest<BaseCommandResponse<bool>>
207: 
208: // ✅ CORRECT - Use bool directly
209: public class DeleteEventCommand : IRequest<bool>
210: 
211: // Controller usage
212: [HttpDelete("{id:guid}")]
213: [Authorize]
214: public async Task<ActionResult> Delete(Guid id)
215: {
216:     var result = await _mediator.Send(new DeleteEventCommand { Id = id });
217:     return result ? NoContent() : NotFound();
218: }
219: 
220: **Why**: Delete operations have binary outcomes (found/deleted or not found). Using bool is more semantic than wrapping in BaseCommandResponse.
221: ```
222: 
223: **Update Rule #11: Auditing Fields** - Add enhanced soft delete:
224: ```markdown
225: ### 11. Entities Include Auditing Fields (ENHANCED)
226: 
227: Beyond CreatedAt/CreatedBy/UpdatedAt/UpdatedBy, soft deletable entities ALSO include:
228: - DeletedAt (DateTime?)
229: - DeletedBy (Guid?)
230: 
231: This provides complete deletion audit trail.
232: ```

````markdown
  1: # CSS Isolation & BEM Skill Creation - Summary
  2: 
  3: **Date**: 2026-02-10
  4: **Status**: ✅ **COMPLETE**
  5: 
  6: ---
  7: 
  8: ## 🎯 MISSION
  9: 
 10: Create comprehensive skill for Blazor CSS isolation with BEM methodology, verified against official Microsoft documentation and BEM best practices.
 11: 
 12: **Research Sources**:
 13: - ✅ **Context7 MCP**: Official ASP.NET Core Blazor documentation
 14: - ✅ **Tavily MCP**: BEM methodology best practices with Blazor CSS isolation
 15: 
 16: ---
 17: 
 18: ## ✅ DELIVERABLES COMPLETED
 19: 
 20: ### 1. New Skill: blazor-css-isolation
 21: **Status**: ✅ **CREATED**
 22: **File**: `.claude/skills/blazor-css-isolation/SKILL.md`
 23: 
 24: **Comprehensive Coverage**:
 25: - ✅ CSS Isolation architecture (build-time transformation, scope attributes)
 26: - ✅ BEM methodology with isolated CSS (`.block__element--modifier`)
 27: - ✅ Component file structure (`Component.razor.css` next to `Component.razor`)
 28: - ✅ Styling child components (3 patterns: own CSS, wrapper, ::deep)
 29: - ✅ ::deep selector usage (when/how/tradeoffs)
 30: - ✅ MudBlazor component styling with BEM
 31: - ✅ Debugging scoped CSS (DevTools techniques)
 32: - ✅ Common issues and solutions
 33: 
 34: **Patterns Documented**:
 35: ```css
 36: /* Authored in EventCard.razor.css */
 37: .event-card { }
 38: 
 39: /* Compiled automatically */
 40: .event-card[b-3xxtam6d07] { }
 41: ```
 42: 
 43: **Key Principles Established**:
 44: 1. Colocation: `.razor.css` next to `.razor` file
 45: 2. Component Ownership: Each component styles itself
 46: 3. BEM for Clarity: Explicit naming even with isolation
 47: 4. Wrapper Over ::deep: Prefer wrapping children
 48: 5. ::deep as Last Resort: Only penetrate when necessary
 49: 
 50: ---
 51: 
 52: ### 2. Documentation Updated: docs/BLAZOR.md
 53: **Status**: ✅ **ENHANCED**
 54: **Section**: 12. CSS & Styling Conventions
 55: 
 56: **Added Content**:
 57: - ✅ **CSS Isolation Architecture** - How it works, build-time process
 58: - ✅ **BEM with CSS Isolation** - Complete EventCard example
 59: - ✅ **Styling Child Components** - 3 safe patterns
 60: - ✅ **::deep Selector** - Usage, transformation, tradeoffs
 61: - ✅ **CSS File Structure** - File organization best practices
 62: - ✅ **Debugging Scoped CSS** - DevTools techniques, common issues table
 63: 
 64: **Code Examples**:
 65: - EventCard component (complete BEM structure)
 66: - Parent-child styling patterns
 67: - MudBlazor component styling
 68: - Debugging workflows
 69: 
 70: **Before** (minimal):
 71: - Basic BEM intro
 72: - Simple `.razor.css` example
 73: - No isolation details
 74: - No ::deep documentation
 75: 
 76: **After** (comprehensive):
 77: - Full CSS isolation explanation
 78: - BEM + isolation integration
 79: - 3 child styling patterns
 80: - Complete debugging guide
 81: - Common issues table
 82: 
 83: ---
 84: 
 85: ## 📚 RESEARCH FINDINGS
 86: 
 87: ### From Context7 (Official Microsoft Docs)
 88: 
 89: **Key Patterns Verified**:
 90: 
 91: 1. **Scope Attribute Generation**:
 92:    - Format: `b-<10-char-string>` (e.g., `b-3xxtam6d07`)
 93:    - Applied to selectors AND DOM elements at build time
 94: 
 95: 2. **Selector Transformation**:
 96:    ```css
 97:    /* Authored */
 98:    h1 { color: brown; }
 99: 
100:    /* Compiled */
101:    h1[b-3xxtam6d07] { color: brown; }
102:    ```
103: 
104: 3. **::deep Transformation**:
105:    ```css
106:    /* Authored */
107:    .parent ::deep .child { color: red; }
108: 
109:    /* Compiled */
110:    .parent[b-xyz123] .child { color: red; }
111:    ```
112: 
113: 4. **Bundle Reference Required**:
114:    ```html
115:    <link href="{Project}.styles.css" rel="stylesheet" />
116:    ```
117: 
118: ---
119: 
120: ### From Tavily (BEM Best Practices)
121: 
122: **Key Insights**:
123: 
124: 1. **BEM with Isolation is Complementary**:
125:    - BEM provides explicit, readable class names
126:    - Isolation prevents collisions automatically
127:    - Result: Best of both worlds
128: 
129: 2. **Wrapper Pattern is Safer than ::deep**:
130:    - Wrap child in container element
131:    - Scope attribute applied to wrapper
132:    - Descendant selectors work without penetration
133: 
134: 3. **::deep Usage Guidelines**:
135:    - Use for third-party components only
136:    - Fragile (coupled to internal markup)
137:    - Upgrade risk (library changes break selectors)
138:    - Last resort, not first choice
139: 
140: 4. **File Colocation is Critical**:
141:    - `Component.razor.css` MUST be next to `Component.razor`
142:    - File names MUST match (case-insensitive)
143:    - Moving files can cause scope mismatch
144: 
145: ---
146: 
147: ## 🎓 ENTERPRISE PATTERNS ESTABLISHED
148: 
149: ### Pattern 1: BEM Block on Root Element
150: 
151: ```razor
152: <MudCard Class="event-card event-card--featured">
153:     <!-- Children use element classes -->
154: </MudCard>
155: ```
156: 
157: ```css
158: .event-card { /* Block */ }
159: .event-card--featured { /* Block modifier */ }
160: .event-card__header { /* Element */ }
161: .event-card__title { /* Element */ }
162: .event-card__badge--new { /* Element modifier */ }
163: ```
164: 
165: **Benefit**: Clear semantic structure + automatic scoping
166: 
167: ---
168: 
169: ### Pattern 2: Child Component Styling Hierarchy
170: 
171: **Preferred Order**:
172: 
173: 1. **Child's Own CSS** (best)
174:    - Each component styles itself
175:    - Separation of concerns
176: 
177: 2. **Wrapper Container** (good)
178:    - Wrap child in parent's HTML element
179:    - Scope attribute on wrapper enables descendant selectors
180: 
181: 3. **::deep Selector** (last resort)
182:    - Only for third-party components
183:    - Use sparingly, document why necessary
184: 
185: ---
186: 
187: ### Pattern 3: MudBlazor Integration
188: 
189: ```razor
190: <MudDataGrid T="Event" Class="event-manager__grid">
191:     <!-- MudBlazor content -->
192: </MudDataGrid>
193: ```
194: 
195: ```css
196: /* Use Class parameter for BEM */
197: .event-manager__grid { }
198: 
199: /* Use ::deep only for unreachable internals */
200: .event-manager__grid ::deep .mud-table-cell {
201:     padding: 12px 16px;
202: }
203: ```
204: 
205: **Benefit**: Combines MudBlazor's power with maintainable styling
206: 
207: ---
