 17: 
 18: 
 19: public sealed class AesEncryptionService : IEncryptionService
 20: {
 21:     private const int NonceSize = 12;
 22:     private const int TagSize = 16;
 23:     private const int KeySize = 32;
 24: 
 25:     private readonly Dictionary<int, byte[]> _keyVersions;
 26:     private readonly int _currentKeyVersion;
 27:     private readonly ILogger<AesEncryptionService>? _logger;
 28:     private bool _disposed;
 29: 
 30: 
 31: 
 32: 
 33: 
 34: 
 35:     public AesEncryptionService(
 36:         IOptions<EncryptionOptions> options,
 37:         ILogger<AesEncryptionService>? logger = null)
 38:     {
 39:         ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(options);
 40:         ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(options.Value);
 41: 
 42:         _logger = logger;
 43:         _keyVersions = new Dictionary<int, byte[]>();
 44:         var config = options.Value;
 45: 
 46: 
 47:         if (config.KeyVersions.Count > 0)
 48:         {
 49:             foreach (var (version, base64Key) in config.KeyVersions)
 50:             {
 51:                 var keyBytes = DecodeAndValidateKey(base64Key, version);
 52:                 _keyVersions[version] = keyBytes;
 53:             }
 54:         }
 55: 
 56:         else if (config.AutoLoadFromEnvironment)
 57:         {
 58:             var envKey = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable(config.MasterKeyEnvironmentVariable);
 59:             if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(envKey))
 60:             {
 61:                 var keyBytes = DecodeAndValidateKey(envKey, 1);
 62:                 _keyVersions[1] = keyBytes;
 63:                 _logger?.LogDebug("Loaded encryption key version 1 from environment variable");
 64:             }
 65:         }
 66: 
 67:         if (_keyVersions.Count == 0)
 68:         {
 69:             throw new InvalidOperationException(
 70:                 "No encryption keys configured. Provide keys via EncryptionOptions.KeyVersions " +
 71:                 $"or set environment variable '{config.MasterKeyEnvironmentVariable}'.");
 72:         }
 73: 
 74:         _currentKeyVersion = config.CurrentKeyVersion;
 75:         if (!_keyVersions.ContainsKey(_currentKeyVersion))
 76:         {
 77:             throw new InvalidOperationException(
 78:                 $"Current key version {_currentKeyVersion} not found in available keys. " +
 79:                 $"Available versions: {string.Join(", ", _keyVersions.Keys)}");
 80:         }
 81: 
 82:         _logger?.LogInformation(
 83:             "AES encryption service initialized with {Count} key version(s), current version: {Version}",
 84:             _keyVersions.Count,
 85:             _currentKeyVersion);
 86:     }
 87: 
 88: 
 89: 
 90: 
 91: 
 92: 
 93: 
 94:     public AesEncryptionService(
 95:         Dictionary<int, byte[]> keyVersions,
 96:         int currentKeyVersion,
 97:         ILogger<AesEncryptionService>? logger = null)
 98:     {
 99:         ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(keyVersions);
100: 
101:         if (keyVersions.Count == 0)
102:         {
103:             throw new ArgumentException("At least one key version is required.", nameof(keyVersions));
104:         }
105: 
106:         _logger = logger;
107:         _keyVersions = new Dictionary<int, byte[]>();
108: 
109:         foreach (var (version, key) in keyVersions)
110:         {
111:             if (key.Length != KeySize)
112:             {
113:                 throw new ArgumentException(
114:                     $"Key version {version} must be exactly {KeySize} bytes (256 bits), got {key.Length} bytes.",
115:                     nameof(keyVersions));
116:             }
117: 
118: 
119:             var keyCopy = new byte[KeySize];
120:             key.CopyTo(keyCopy, 0);
121:             _keyVersions[version] = keyCopy;
122:         }
123: 
124:         if (!_keyVersions.ContainsKey(currentKeyVersion))
125:         {
126:             throw new ArgumentException(
127:                 $"Current key version {currentKeyVersion} not found in provided keys.",
128:                 nameof(currentKeyVersion));
129:         }
130: 
131:         _currentKeyVersion = currentKeyVersion;
132:     }
133: 
134: 
135:     public int CurrentKeyVersion => _currentKeyVersion;
136: 
137: 
138:     public IReadOnlyCollection<int> AvailableKeyVersions => _keyVersions.Keys.ToList().AsReadOnly();
139: 
140: 
141:     public EncryptionResult Encrypt(string plaintext)
142:     {
143:         ObjectDisposedException.ThrowIf(_disposed, this);
144:         ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(plaintext);
145: 
146:         var key = _keyVersions[_currentKeyVersion];
147:         var plaintextBytes = Encoding.UTF8.GetBytes(plaintext);
148: 
149:         try
150:         {
151: 
152:             var nonce = new byte[NonceSize];
153:             var tag = new byte[TagSize];
154:             var ciphertext = new byte[plaintextBytes.Length];
155: 
156: 
157:             RandomNumberGenerator.Fill(nonce);
158: 
159: 
160:             using var aesGcm = new AesGcm(key, TagSize);
161:             aesGcm.Encrypt(nonce, plaintextBytes, ciphertext, tag);
162: 
163: 
164:             var result = new byte[NonceSize + TagSize + ciphertext.Length];
165:             Buffer.BlockCopy(nonce, 0, result, 0, NonceSize);
166:             Buffer.BlockCopy(tag, 0, result, NonceSize, TagSize);
167:             Buffer.BlockCopy(ciphertext, 0, result, NonceSize + TagSize, ciphertext.Length);
168: 
169:             var base64Result = Convert.ToBase64String(result);
170: 
171:             _logger?.LogDebug(
172:                 "Encrypted {Length} bytes using key version {Version}",
173:                 plaintextBytes.Length,
174:                 _currentKeyVersion);
175: 
176:             return new EncryptionResult(base64Result, _currentKeyVersion);
177:         }
178:         finally
179:         {
180: 
181:             CryptographicOperations.ZeroMemory(plaintextBytes);
182:         }
183:     }
184: 
185: 
186:     public string Decrypt(string ciphertext, int keyVersion)
187:     {
188:         ObjectDisposedException.ThrowIf(_disposed, this);
189:         ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(ciphertext);
190: 
191:         if (!_keyVersions.TryGetValue(keyVersion, out var key))
192:         {
193:             throw new InvalidOperationException(
194:                 $"Key version {keyVersion} not found. Available versions: {string.Join(", ", _keyVersions.Keys)}");
195:         }
196: 
197:         byte[] combined;
198:         try
199:         {
200:             combined = Convert.FromBase64String(ciphertext);
201:         }
202:         catch (FormatException ex)
203:         {
204:             throw new InvalidOperationException("Invalid ciphertext format: not valid base64.", ex);
205:         }
206: 
207:         if (combined.Length < NonceSize + TagSize)
208:         {
209:             throw new InvalidOperationException(
210:                 $"Invalid ciphertext: too short. Expected at least {NonceSize + TagSize} bytes, got {combined.Length}.");
211:         }
212: 
213: 
214:         var nonce = new byte[NonceSize];
215:         var tag = new byte[TagSize];
216:         var encryptedData = new byte[combined.Length - NonceSize - TagSize];
217: 
218:         Buffer.BlockCopy(combined, 0, nonce, 0, NonceSize);
219:         Buffer.BlockCopy(combined, NonceSize, tag, 0, TagSize);
220:         Buffer.BlockCopy(combined, NonceSize + TagSize, encryptedData, 0, encryptedData.Length);
221: 
222:         var plaintextBytes = new byte[encryptedData.Length];
223: 
224:         try
225:         {
226:             using var aesGcm = new AesGcm(key, TagSize);
227:             aesGcm.Decrypt(nonce, encryptedData, tag, plaintextBytes);
228: 
229:             var plaintext = Encoding.UTF8.GetString(plaintextBytes);
230: 
231:             _logger?.LogDebug(
232:                 "Decrypted {Length} bytes using key version {Version}",
233:                 encryptedData.Length,
234:                 keyVersion);
235: 
236:             return plaintext;
237:         }
238:         catch (AuthenticationTagMismatchException ex)
239:         {
240:             throw new InvalidOperationException(
241:                 "Decryption failed: authentication tag mismatch. Data may be corrupted or tampered.", ex);
242:         }
243:         finally
244:         {
245: 
246:             CryptographicOperations.ZeroMemory(plaintextBytes);
247:         }
248:     }
249: 
250: 
251:     public bool HasKeyVersion(int keyVersion)
252:     {
253:         ObjectDisposedException.ThrowIf(_disposed, this);
254:         return _keyVersions.ContainsKey(keyVersion);
255:     }
256: 
257: 
258: 
259: 
260:     private static byte[] DecodeAndValidateKey(string base64Key, int version)
261:     {
262:         byte[] keyBytes;
263:         try
264:         {
265:             keyBytes = Convert.FromBase64String(base64Key);
266:         }
267:         catch (FormatException ex)
268:         {
269:             throw new InvalidOperationException(
270:                 $"Key version {version} is not valid base64.", ex);
271:         }
272: 
273:         if (keyBytes.Length != KeySize)
274:         {
275:             throw new InvalidOperationException(
276:                 $"Key version {version} must be exactly {KeySize} bytes (256 bits), " +
277:                 $"got {keyBytes.Length} bytes.");
278:         }
279: 
280:         return keyBytes;
281:     }
282: 
283: 
284:     public void Dispose()
285:     {
286:         if (_disposed)
287:         {
288:             return;
289:         }
290: 
291: 
292:         foreach (var key in _keyVersions.Values)
293:         {
294:             CryptographicOperations.ZeroMemory(key);
295:         }
296: 
297:         _keyVersions.Clear();
298:         _disposed = true;
299: 
300:         _logger?.LogDebug("AES encryption service disposed, key material zeroed");
301:     }
302: }
````

 58: public sealed class KeyRotationService
 59: {
 60:     private readonly IEncryptionService _encryptionService;
 61:     private readonly ILogger<KeyRotationService>? _logger;
 62: 
 63: 
 64:

 66: 
 67: 
 68:     public KeyRotationService(
 69:         IEncryptionService encryptionService,
 70:         ILogger<KeyRotationService>? logger = null)
 71:     {
 72:         ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(encryptionService);
 73:         _encryptionService = encryptionService;
 74:         _logger = logger;
 75:     }
 76: 
 77: 
 78: 
 79: 
 80: 
 81: 
 82: 
 83: 
 84: 
 85:     public async Task<KeyRotationResult> ReEncryptAllAsync(
 86:         GetSettingsToRotateAsync getSettings,
 87:         UpdateSettingAsync updateSetting,
 88:         IProgress<KeyRotationProgress>? progress = null,
 89:         CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 90:     {
 91:         ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(getSettings);
 92:         ArgumentNullException.ThrowIfNull(updateSetting);
 93: 
 94:         var currentVersion = _encryptionService.CurrentKeyVersion;
 95:         _logger?.LogInformation(
 96:             "Starting key rotation to version {Version}",
 97:             currentVersion);
 98: 
 99:         var settings = await getSettings(currentVersion).ConfigureAwait(false);
100:         var total = settings.Count;
101: 
102:         _logger?.LogInformation(
103:             "Found {Count} settings to re-encrypt",
104:             total);
105: 
106:         if (total == 0)
107:         {
108:             return new KeyRotationResult(0, 0, 0, 0, []);
109:         }
110: 
111:         var reEncryptedCount = 0;
112:         var skippedCount = 0;
113:         var errors = new List<KeyRotationError>();
114:         var current = 0;
115: 
116:         foreach (var setting in settings)
117:         {
118:             cancellationToken.ThrowIfCancellationRequested();
119: 
120:             current++;
121:             progress?.Report(new KeyRotationProgress(current, total, setting.Key));
122: 
123: 
124:             if (setting.KeyVersion >= currentVersion)
125:             {
126:                 _logger?.LogDebug(
127:                     "Skipping {Key}: already at version {Version}",
128:                     setting.Key, setting.KeyVersion);
129:                 skippedCount++;
130:                 continue;
131:             }
132: 
133: 
134:             if (!_encryptionService.HasKeyVersion(setting.KeyVersion))
135:             {
136:                 var error = $"Missing key version {setting.KeyVersion}";
137:                 _logger?.LogError(
138:                     "Cannot re-encrypt {Key}: {Error}",
139:                     setting.Key, error);
140:                 errors.Add(new KeyRotationError(setting.Key, setting.KeyVersion, error));
141:                 continue;
142:             }
143: 
144:             try
145:             {
146: 
147:                 var plaintext = _encryptionService.Decrypt(
148:                     setting.EncryptedValue,
149:                     setting.KeyVersion);
150: 
151: 
152:                 var result = _encryptionService.Encrypt(plaintext);
153: 
154: 
155:                 await updateSetting(
156:                     setting.Key,
157:                     result.Ciphertext,
158:                     result.KeyVersion,
159:                     DateTime.UtcNow).ConfigureAwait(false);
160: 
161:                 reEncryptedCount++;
162:                 _logger?.LogDebug(
163:                     "Re-encrypted {Key}: v{OldVersion} -> v{NewVersion}",
164:                     setting.Key, setting.KeyVersion, result.KeyVersion);
165:             }
166:             catch (Exception ex)
167:             {
168:                 _logger?.LogError(ex,
169:                     "Failed to re-encrypt {Key}",
170:                     setting.Key);
171:                 errors.Add(new KeyRotationError(setting.Key, setting.KeyVersion, ex.Message));
172:             }
173:         }
174: 
175:         _logger?.LogInformation(
176:             "Key rotation complete: {ReEncrypted} re-encrypted, {Skipped} skipped, {Errors} errors",
177:             reEncryptedCount, skippedCount, errors.Count);
178: 
179:         return new KeyRotationResult(
180:             total,
181:             reEncryptedCount,
182:             skippedCount,
183:             errors.Count,
184:             errors.AsReadOnly());
185:     }
186: 
187: 
188: 
189: 
190: 
191: 
192: 
193:     public EncryptionResult ReEncryptSingle(string encryptedValue, int oldKeyVersion)
194:     {
195:         ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrEmpty(encryptedValue);
196: 
197:         if (!_encryptionService.HasKeyVersion(oldKeyVersion))
198:         {
199:             throw new InvalidOperationException(
200:                 $"Cannot re-encrypt: key version {oldKeyVersion} not available.");
201:         }
202: 
203:         var plaintext = _encryptionService.Decrypt(encryptedValue, oldKeyVersion);
204:         return _encryptionService.Encrypt(plaintext);
205:     }
206: }

 24: public sealed class RotationAwareDbContextFactory<TContext> : IDbContextFactory<TContext>, IDisposable
 25:     where TContext : DbContext
 26: {
 27:     private readonly Func<DbContextOptions<TContext>, TContext> _contextFactory;
 28:     private readonly IOptionsMonitor<DatabaseConnectionOptions> _connectionOptions;
 29:     private readonly IOptionsMonitor<RotationOptions> _rotationOptions;
 30:     private readonly ILogger<RotationAwareDbContextFactory<TContext>> _logger;
 31:     private readonly IDisposable? _connectionChangeListener;
 32:     private readonly object _optionsLock = new();
 33: 
 34:     private string? _currentConnectionString;
 35:     private DateTime _lastConnectionStringChange;
 36:     private int _rotationCount;
 37:     private bool _disposed;
 38: 
 39: 
 40: 
 41: 
 42: 
 43: 
 44: 
 45: 
 46:     public RotationAwareDbContextFactory(
 47:         Func<DbContextOptions<TContext>, TContext> contextFactory,
 48:         IOptionsMonitor<DatabaseConnectionOptions> connectionOptions,
 49:         IOptionsMonitor<RotationOptions> rotationOptions,
 50:         ILogger<RotationAwareDbContextFactory<TContext>> logger)
 51:     {
 52:         _contextFactory = contextFactory ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(contextFactory));
 53:         _connectionOptions = connectionOptions ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(connectionOptions));
 54:         _rotationOptions = rotationOptions ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(rotationOptions));
 55:         _logger = logger ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(logger));
 56: 
 57: 
 58:         _currentConnectionString = connectionOptions.CurrentValue.ConnectionString;
 59:         _lastConnectionStringChange = DateTime.UtcNow;
 60: 
 61: 
 62:         _connectionChangeListener = _connectionOptions.OnChange(OnConnectionOptionsChanged);
 63: 
 64:         _logger.LogDebug(
 65:             "RotationAwareDbContextFactory<{ContextType}> initialized",
 66:             typeof(TContext).Name);
 67:     }
 68: 
 69: 
 70: 
 71: 
 72:     public int RotationCount => _rotationCount;
 73: 
 74: 
 75: 
 76: 
 77:     public DateTime LastConnectionStringChange => _lastConnectionStringChange;
 78: 
 79: 
 80: 
 81: 
 82:     public string? CurrentConnectionStringRedacted => RedactConnectionString(_currentConnectionString);
 83: 
 84: 
 85: 
 86: 
 87: 
 88:     public TContext CreateDbContext()
 89:     {
 90:         ObjectDisposedException.ThrowIf(_disposed, this);
 91: 
 92:         string? connectionString;
 93:         lock (_optionsLock)
 94:         {
 95:             connectionString = _currentConnectionString;
 96:         }
 97: 
 98:         if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(connectionString))
 99:         {
100:             throw new InvalidOperationException(
101:                 $"Connection string is not configured for {typeof(TContext).Name}. " +
102:                 $"Ensure DatabaseConnectionOptions is properly configured.");
103:         }
104: 
105:         var optionsBuilder = new DbContextOptionsBuilder<TContext>();
106:         ConfigureDbContextOptions(optionsBuilder, connectionString);
107: 
108:         var context = _contextFactory(optionsBuilder.Options);
109: 
110:         _logger.LogTrace(
111:             "Created DbContext<{ContextType}> (rotations: {RotationCount})",
112:             typeof(TContext).Name,
113:             _rotationCount);
114: 
115:         return context;
116:     }
117: 
118: 
119: 
120: 
121:     private void ConfigureDbContextOptions(
122:         DbContextOptionsBuilder<TContext> optionsBuilder,
123:         string connectionString)
124:     {
125:         var dbOptions = _connectionOptions.CurrentValue;
126: 
127: 
128:         var npgsqlConnectionString = connectionString;
129: 
130: 
131: 
132:         if (dbOptions.MaxPoolSize.HasValue)
133:         {
134:             _logger.LogDebug("MaxPoolSize configured: {MaxPoolSize}", dbOptions.MaxPoolSize);
135:         }
136: 
137:         optionsBuilder.UseNpgsql(npgsqlConnectionString);
138:     }
139: 
140:     private void OnConnectionOptionsChanged(DatabaseConnectionOptions newOptions, string? name)
141:     {
142:         if (!_rotationOptions.CurrentValue.Enabled)
143:         {
144:             _logger.LogDebug("Connection rotation is disabled, ignoring change");
145:             return;
146:         }
147: 
148:         var newConnectionString = newOptions.ConnectionString;
149: 
150:         lock (_optionsLock)
151:         {
152: 
153:             if (string.Equals(_currentConnectionString, newConnectionString, StringComparison.Ordinal))
154:             {
155:                 _logger.LogDebug("Connection string unchanged, skipping rotation");
156:                 return;
157:             }
158: 
159:             _currentConnectionString = newConnectionString;
160:             _lastConnectionStringChange = DateTime.UtcNow;
161:             Interlocked.Increment(ref _rotationCount);
162:         }
163: 
164:         if (_rotationOptions.CurrentValue.LogRotationEvents)
165:         {
166:             _logger.LogInformation(
167:                 "Connection string rotated for {ContextType} (rotation #{RotationCount}). New connection: {ConnectionString}",
168:                 typeof(TContext).Name,
169:                 _rotationCount,
170:                 RedactConnectionString(newConnectionString));
171:         }
172:     }
173: 
174: 
175: 
176: 
177:     private static string? RedactConnectionString(string? connectionString)
178:     {
179:         if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(connectionString))
180:         {
181:             return null;
182:         }
183: 
184: 
185:         var patterns = new[]
186:         {
187:             ("Password=", "Password=***"),
188:             ("password=", "password=***"),
189:             ("Pwd=", "Pwd=***"),
190:             ("pwd=", "pwd=***"),
191:             ("Secret=", "Secret=***"),
192:             ("secret=", "secret=***"),
193:         };
194: 
195:         var redacted = connectionString;
196:         foreach (var (pattern, replacement) in patterns)
197:         {
198:             var index = redacted.IndexOf(pattern, StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase);
199:             if (index >= 0)
200:             {
201:                 var endIndex = redacted.IndexOf(';', index);
202:                 if (endIndex > 0)
203:                 {
204:                     redacted = redacted[..index] + replacement + redacted[endIndex..];
205:                 }
206:                 else
207:                 {
208:                     redacted = redacted[..index] + replacement;
209:                 }
210:             }
211:         }
212: 
213:         return redacted;
214:     }
215: 
216: 
217: 
218: 
219: 
220:     public void ForceRefresh()
221:     {
222:         ObjectDisposedException.ThrowIf(_disposed, this);
223: 
224:         var currentOptions = _connectionOptions.CurrentValue;
225:         OnConnectionOptionsChanged(currentOptions, null);
226:     }
227: 
228: 
229: 
230: 
231:     public void Dispose()
232:     {
233:         if (_disposed)
234:         {
235:             return;
236:         }
237: 
238:         _disposed = true;
239: 
240:         _logger.LogDebug(
241:             "Disposing RotationAwareDbContextFactory<{ContextType}> (total rotations: {RotationCount})",
242:             typeof(TContext).Name,
243:             _rotationCount);
244: 
245:         _connectionChangeListener?.Dispose();
246:     }
247: }
248: 
249: 
250: 
251: 
252: public interface IRotationAwareDbContextFactory
253: {
254: 
255: 
256: 
257:     int RotationCount { get; }
258: 
259: 
260: 
261: 
262:     DateTime LastConnectionStringChange { get; }
263: 
264: 
265: 
266: 
267:     string? CurrentConnectionStringRedacted { get; }
268: 
269: 
270: 
271: 
272:     void ForceRefresh();
273: }

 19: public sealed class RotationAwareHttpClientFactory : IHttpClientFactory, IDisposable
 20: {
 21:     private readonly ConcurrentDictionary<string, ClientEntry> _clients = new();
 22:     private readonly IOptionsMonitor<HttpClientCredentialOptions> _credentialOptions;
 23:     private readonly IOptionsMonitor<RotationOptions> _rotationOptions;
 24:     private readonly ILogger<RotationAwareHttpClientFactory> _logger;
 25:     private readonly IDisposable? _credentialChangeListener;
 26:     private readonly SemaphoreSlim _rotationSemaphore;
 27:     private readonly object _disposeLock = new();
 28:     private bool _disposed;
 29: 
 30: 
 31: 
 32: 
 33:     public RotationAwareHttpClientFactory(
 34:         IOptionsMonitor<HttpClientCredentialOptions> credentialOptions,
 35:         IOptionsMonitor<RotationOptions> rotationOptions,
 36:         ILogger<RotationAwareHttpClientFactory> logger)
 37:     {
 38:         _credentialOptions = credentialOptions ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(credentialOptions));
 39:         _rotationOptions = rotationOptions ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(rotationOptions));
 40:         _logger = logger ?? throw new ArgumentNullException(nameof(logger));
 41:         _rotationSemaphore = new SemaphoreSlim(rotationOptions.CurrentValue.MaxConcurrentRotations);
 42: 
 43: 
 44:         _credentialChangeListener = _credentialOptions.OnChange(OnCredentialsChanged);
 45: 
 46:         _logger.LogDebug("RotationAwareHttpClientFactory initialized");
 47:     }
 48: 
 49: 
 50: 
 51: 
 52: 
 53: 
 54:     public HttpClient CreateClient(string name)
 55:     {
 56:         ObjectDisposedException.ThrowIf(_disposed, this);
 57: 
 58:         var entry = _clients.GetOrAdd(name, CreateClientEntry);
 59:         return entry.Client;
 60:     }
 61: 
 62: 
 63: 
 64: 
 65:     public int ActiveClientCount => _clients.Count;
 66: 
 67: 
 68: 
 69: 
 70:     public bool HasClient(string name) => _clients.ContainsKey(name);
 71: 
 72:     private ClientEntry CreateClientEntry(string name)
 73:     {
 74:         var client = CreateHttpClientInternal(name);
 75:         _logger.LogDebug("Created new HTTP client for '{Name}'", name);
 76:         return new ClientEntry(client, DateTime.UtcNow);
 77:     }
 78: 
 79:     private HttpClient CreateHttpClientInternal(string name)
 80:     {
 81:         var client = new HttpClient();
 82:         var credentials = _credentialOptions.CurrentValue;
 83: 
 84:         if (credentials.Clients.TryGetValue(name, out var clientCred))
 85:         {
 86:             ApplyCredentials(client, clientCred, name);
 87:         }
 88: 
 89:         return client;
 90:     }
 91: 
 92:     private void ApplyCredentials(HttpClient client, HttpClientCredential credential, string name)
 93:     {
 94: 
 95:         if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(credential.BaseAddress))
 96:         {
 97:             client.BaseAddress = new Uri(credential.BaseAddress);
 98:         }
 99: 
100: 
101:         if (credential.Timeout.HasValue)
102:         {
103:             client.Timeout = credential.Timeout.Value;
104:         }
105: 
106: 
107:         if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(credential.BearerToken))
108:         {
109:             client.DefaultRequestHeaders.Authorization =
110:                 new System.Net.Http.Headers.AuthenticationHeaderValue("Bearer", credential.BearerToken);
111:         }
112: 
113: 
114:         if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(credential.ApiKey))
115:         {
116:             client.DefaultRequestHeaders.Add("X-API-Key", credential.ApiKey);
117:         }
118: 
119: 
120:         foreach (var header in credential.Headers)
121:         {
122:             if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(header.Value))
123:             {
124:                 client.DefaultRequestHeaders.TryAddWithoutValidation(header.Key, header.Value);
125:             }
126:         }
127: 
128:         _logger.LogDebug(
129:             "Applied credentials to HTTP client '{Name}' (BaseAddress: {BaseAddress})",
130:             name,
131:             credential.BaseAddress ?? "not set");
132:     }
133: 
134:     private void OnCredentialsChanged(HttpClientCredentialOptions newCredentials, string? name)
135:     {
136:         if (!_rotationOptions.CurrentValue.Enabled)
137:         {
138:             _logger.LogDebug("Credential rotation is disabled, ignoring change");
139:             return;
140:         }
141: 
142:         _logger.LogInformation("HTTP client credentials changed, initiating rotation");
143: 
144: 
145:         foreach (var clientName in newCredentials.Clients.Keys)
146:         {
147:             if (_clients.ContainsKey(clientName))
148:             {
149:                 _ = RotateClientAsync(clientName);
150:             }
151:         }
152:     }
153: 
154:     private async Task RotateClientAsync(string name)
155:     {
156:         try
157:         {
158: 
159:             if (!await _rotationSemaphore.WaitAsync(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(5)))
160:             {
161:                 _logger.LogWarning(
162:                     "Rotation for client '{Name}' skipped - too many concurrent rotations",
163:                     name);
164:                 return;
165:             }
166: 
167:             try
168:             {
169:                 await RotateClientInternalAsync(name);
170:             }
171:             finally
172:             {
173:                 _rotationSemaphore.Release();
174:             }
175:         }
176:         catch (Exception ex)
177:         {
178:             _logger.LogError(ex, "Failed to rotate HTTP client '{Name}'", name);
179:         }
180:     }
181: 
182:     private async Task RotateClientInternalAsync(string name)
183:     {
184:         var rotationOptions = _rotationOptions.CurrentValue;
185: 
186:         if (rotationOptions.LogRotationEvents)
187:         {
188:             _logger.LogInformation("Rotating HTTP client '{Name}'", name);
189:         }
190: 
191: 
192:         var newEntry = CreateClientEntry(name);
193: 
194: 
195:         if (_clients.TryGetValue(name, out var oldEntry))
196:         {
197:             _clients[name] = newEntry;
198: 
199:             if (rotationOptions.LogRotationEvents)
200:             {
201:                 _logger.LogDebug(
202:                     "Swapped HTTP client '{Name}', scheduling disposal after {GracePeriod}",
203:                     name,
204:                     rotationOptions.GracePeriod);
205:             }
206: 
207: 
208:             _ = DisposeAfterGracePeriodAsync(oldEntry.Client, name, rotationOptions.GracePeriod);
209:         }
210:         else
211:         {
212: 
213:             _clients[name] = newEntry;
214:         }
215: 
216:         await Task.CompletedTask;
217:     }
218: 
219:     private async Task DisposeAfterGracePeriodAsync(HttpClient client, string name, TimeSpan gracePeriod)
220:     {
221:         try
222:         {
223:             await Task.Delay(gracePeriod);
224:             client.Dispose();
225: 
226:             if (_rotationOptions.CurrentValue.LogRotationEvents)
227:             {
228:                 _logger.LogDebug(
229:                     "Disposed old HTTP client '{Name}' after grace period",
230:                     name);
231:             }
232:         }
233:         catch (Exception ex)
234:         {
235:             _logger.LogError(
236:                 ex,
237:                 "Error disposing old HTTP client '{Name}' after grace period",
238:                 name);
239:         }
240:     }
241: 
242: 
243: 
244: 
245: 
246:     public async Task ForceRotateAsync(string name)
247:     {
248:         ObjectDisposedException.ThrowIf(_disposed, this);
249: 
250:         if (!_clients.ContainsKey(name))
251:         {
252:             throw new ArgumentException($"No client with name '{name}' exists", nameof(name));
253:         }
254: 
255:         await RotateClientAsync(name);
256:     }
257: 
258: 
259: 
260: 
261:     public async Task ForceRotateAllAsync()
262:     {
263:         ObjectDisposedException.ThrowIf(_disposed, this);
264: 
265:         var tasks = _clients.Keys.Select(RotateClientAsync);
266:         await Task.WhenAll(tasks);
267:     }
268: 
269: 
270: 
271: 
272:     public void Dispose()
273:     {
274:         lock (_disposeLock)
275:         {
276:             if (_disposed)
277:             {
278:                 return;
279:             }
280: 
281:             _disposed = true;
282:         }
283: 
284:         _logger.LogDebug("Disposing RotationAwareHttpClientFactory");
285: 
286: 
287:         _credentialChangeListener?.Dispose();
288: 
289: 
290:         foreach (var entry in _clients.Values)
291:         {
292:             try
293:             {
294:                 entry.Client.Dispose();
295:             }
296:             catch (Exception ex)
297:             {
298:                 _logger.LogWarning(ex, "Error disposing HTTP client during factory disposal");
299:             }
300:         }
301: 
302:         _clients.Clear();
303:         _rotationSemaphore.Dispose();
304: 
305:         _logger.LogDebug("RotationAwareHttpClientFactory disposed");
306:     }
307: 
308: 
309: 
310: 
311:     private sealed record ClientEntry(HttpClient Client, DateTime CreatedAt);
312: }
````

## File: Explore.Secrets/Services/SecretRefreshService.cs
````csharp
  1: using Explore.Secrets.Abstractions;
  2: using Explore.Secrets.Configuration;
  3: using Explore.Secrets.Observability;
  4: using Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration;
  5: using Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting;
  6: using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
  7: using Microsoft.Extensions.Options;
  8: 
  9: namespace Explore.Secrets.Services;
 10: 
 11: 
 12: 
 13: 
 14: 
 15: public sealed class SecretRefreshService : BackgroundService
 16: {
 17:     private readonly ISecretProvider _secretProvider;
 18:     private readonly IConfigurationRoot? _configuration;
 19:     private readonly SecretRefreshOptions _options;
 20:     private readonly SecretRefreshMetrics _metrics;
 21:     private readonly ILogger<SecretRefreshService> _logger;
 22: 
 23:     private int _consecutiveFailures;
 24:     private DateTime? _lastSuccessfulRefresh;
 25: 
 26:     public SecretRefreshService(
 27:         ISecretProvider secretProvider,
 28:         IConfiguration configuration,
 29:         IOptions<SecretRefreshOptions> options,
 30:         SecretRefreshMetrics metrics,
 31:         ILogger<SecretRefreshService> logger)
 32:     {
 33:         _secretProvider = secretProvider;
 34:         _configuration = configuration as IConfigurationRoot;
 35:         _options = options.Value;
 36:         _metrics = metrics;
 37:         _logger = logger;
 38:     }
 39: 
 40: 
 41: 
 42: 
 43:     public int ConsecutiveFailures => _consecutiveFailures;
 44: 
 45: 
 46: 
 47: 
 48:     public DateTime? LastSuccessfulRefresh => _lastSuccessfulRefresh;
 49: 
 50:     protected override async Task ExecuteAsync(CancellationToken stoppingToken)
 51:     {
 52:         if (!_options.Enabled)
 53:         {
 54:             _logger.LogInformation("Secret refresh service is disabled");
 55:             return;
 56:         }
 57: 
 58:         if (!_secretProvider.SupportsRefresh)
 59:         {
 60:             _logger.LogInformation(
 61:                 "Secret provider {Provider} does not support refresh, service will not run",
 62:                 _secretProvider.ProviderType);
 63:             return;
 64:         }
 65: 
 66:         _logger.LogInformation(
 67:             "Secret refresh service starting with interval {Interval}",
 68:             _options.RefreshInterval);
 69: 
 70: 
 71:         var initialDelay = _options.AddJitter(_options.InitialDelay);
 72:         _logger.LogDebug("Waiting {Delay} before first refresh", initialDelay);
 73: 
 74:         try
 75:         {
 76:             await Task.Delay(initialDelay, stoppingToken);
 77:         }
 78:         catch (OperationCanceledException)
 79:         {
 80:             return;
 81:         }
 82: 
 83: 
 84:         using var timer = new PeriodicTimer(_options.RefreshInterval);
 85: 
 86:         while (!stoppingToken.IsCancellationRequested)
 87:         {
 88:             await RefreshSecretsAsync(stoppingToken);
 89: 
 90:             try
 91:             {
 92: 
 93:                 var waitTime = CalculateNextWaitTime();
 94: 
 95:                 if (waitTime != _options.RefreshInterval)
 96:                 {
 97: 
 98:                     await Task.Delay(waitTime, stoppingToken);
 99:                 }
100:                 else
101:                 {
102: 
103:                     await timer.WaitForNextTickAsync(stoppingToken);
104:                 }
105:             }
106:             catch (OperationCanceledException)
107:             {
108:                 break;
109:             }
110:         }
111: 
112:         _logger.LogInformation("Secret refresh service stopped");
113:     }
114: 
115:     private async Task RefreshSecretsAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken)
116:     {
117:         using var operation = _metrics.StartRefreshOperation(_secretProvider.ProviderType);
118: 
119:         try
120:         {
121:             _logger.LogDebug(
122:                 "Starting secret refresh (consecutive failures: {Failures})",
123:                 _consecutiveFailures);
124: 
125:             await _secretProvider.RefreshAsync(cancellationToken);
126: 
127: 
128:             if (_configuration is not null)
129:             {
130:                 _configuration.Reload();
131:                 _logger.LogDebug("Configuration reloaded after secret refresh");
132:             }
133: 
134:             _consecutiveFailures = 0;
135:             _lastSuccessfulRefresh = DateTime.UtcNow;
136:             operation.Complete();
137: 
138:             _logger.LogInformation("Secret refresh completed successfully");
139:         }
140:         catch (SecretProviderException ex) when (ex.IsTransient)
141:         {
142:             _consecutiveFailures++;
143:             operation.Fail("transient");
144: 
145:             _logger.LogWarning(
146:                 ex,
147:                 "Transient error during secret refresh (failures: {Failures}, operation: {Operation})",
148:                 _consecutiveFailures,
149:                 ex.Operation);
150:         }
151:         catch (SecretProviderException ex)
152:         {
153:             _consecutiveFailures++;
154:             operation.Fail("permanent");
155: 
156:             _logger.LogError(
157:                 ex,
158:                 "Permanent error during secret refresh (failures: {Failures}, operation: {Operation})",
159:                 _consecutiveFailures,
160:                 ex.Operation);
161:         }
162:         catch (OperationCanceledException)
163:         {
164: 
165:             _logger.LogDebug("Secret refresh cancelled");
166:             throw;
167:         }
168:         catch (Exception ex)
169:         {
170:             _consecutiveFailures++;
171:             operation.Fail("unknown");
172: 
173:             _logger.LogError(
174:                 ex,
175:                 "Unexpected error during secret refresh (failures: {Failures})",
176:                 _consecutiveFailures);
177:         }
178:     }
179: 
180:     private TimeSpan CalculateNextWaitTime()
181:     {
182:         if (_consecutiveFailures == 0)
183:         {
184: 
185:             return _options.AddJitter(_options.RefreshInterval);
186:         }
187: 
188: 
189:         var backoff = _options.CalculateBackoffDelay(_consecutiveFailures);
190: 
191:         _logger.LogDebug(
192:             "Using backoff delay {Delay} after {Failures} consecutive failures",
193:             backoff,
194:             _consecutiveFailures);
195: 
196:         return backoff;
197:     }
198: 
199:     public override async Task StopAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken)
200:     {
201:         _logger.LogInformation(
202:             "Secret refresh service stopping (last success: {LastSuccess}, failures: {Failures})",
203:             _lastSuccessfulRefresh,
204:             _consecutiveFailures);
205: 
206:         await base.StopAsync(cancellationToken);
207:     }
208: }
````

19: 
20: 
21: 
22: 
23:     private const LogLevel FailureLevel = LogLevel.Warning;

46:

49:         _logger.Log(
50:             logLevel: level,
51:             eventId: new EventId((int)entry.Operation, entry.Operation.ToString()),
52:             message: "SecretAudit: {Operation} on {ProviderType} {Status}. Key: {KeyPattern}",
53:             args:
54:             [
55:                 entry.Operation.ToString(),
56:                 entry.ProviderType.ToString(),
57:                 entry.Success ? "succeeded" : "failed",
58:                 entry.KeyPattern ?? "(none)"
59:             ]);
60: 
61: 
62:         if (_logger.IsEnabled(LogLevel.Debug))
63:         {
64:             _logger.LogDebug(
65:                 "SecretAudit details - Operation: {Operation}, Provider: {ProviderType}, " +
66:                 "Key: {KeyPattern}, Success: {Success}, UserId: {UserId}, " +
67:                 "CorrelationId: {CorrelationId}, Timestamp: {Timestamp}, Error: {ErrorMessage}",
68:                 entry.Operation,
69:                 entry.ProviderType,
70:                 entry.KeyPattern,
71:                 entry.Success,
72:                 entry.UserId ?? "anonymous",
73:                 entry.CorrelationId ?? "none",
74:                 entry.Timestamp.ToString("O"),
75:                 entry.ErrorMessage ?? "none");
76:         }
77: 
78: 
79:         if (!entry.Success && !string.IsNullOrEmpty(entry.ErrorMessage))
80:         {
81:             _logger.LogWarning(
82:                 "SecretAudit FAILURE - Operation: {Operation}, Provider: {ProviderType}, " +
83:                 "Error: {ErrorMessage}, CorrelationId: {CorrelationId}",
84:                 entry.Operation,
85:                 entry.ProviderType,
86:                 entry.ErrorMessage,
87:                 entry.CorrelationId ?? "none");
88:         }

90: }

## File: Explore.Secrets/Validation/RequiredSecretsValidator.cs
````csharp
  1: using Explore.Secrets.Abstractions;
  2: using Explore.Secrets.Configuration;
  3: using Microsoft.Extensions.Options;
  4: 
  5: namespace Explore.Secrets.Validation;
  6:

 10: 
 11: public sealed class SecretProviderOptionsValidator : IValidateOptions<SecretProviderOptions>
 12: {
 13: 
 14:     public ValidateOptionsResult Validate(string? name, SecretProviderOptions options)
 15:     {
 16:         var errors = new List<string>();
 17: 
 18:         switch (options.Provider)
 19:         {
 20:             case SecretProviderType.None:
 21: 
 22:                 break;
 23: 
 24:             case SecretProviderType.Infisical:
 25:                 ValidateInfisicalOptions(options.Infisical, errors);
 26:                 break;
 27: 
 28:             case SecretProviderType.Vault:
 29:                 ValidateVaultOptions(options.Vault, errors);
 30:                 break;
 31: 
 32:             case SecretProviderType.AzureKeyVault:
 33:                 ValidateAzureKeyVaultOptions(options.AzureKeyVault, errors);
 34:                 break;
 35: 
 36:             case SecretProviderType.AwsSecretsManager:
 37:                 ValidateAwsSecretsManagerOptions(options.AwsSecretsManager, errors);
 38:                 break;
 39: 
 40:             default:
 41:                 errors.Add($"Unknown secret provider type: {options.Provider}");
 42:                 break;
 43:         }
 44: 
 45:         return errors.Count > 0
 46:             ? ValidateOptionsResult.Fail(errors)
 47:             : ValidateOptionsResult.Success;
 48:     }
 49: 
 50:     private static void ValidateInfisicalOptions(InfisicalOptions options, List<string> errors)
 51:     {
 52:         if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(options.Url))
 53:             errors.Add("Infisical URL is required (SecretProvider:Infisical:Url)");
 54: 
 55:         if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(options.ProjectId))
 56:             errors.Add("Infisical Project ID is required (SecretProvider:Infisical:ProjectId)");
 57: 
 58:         if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(options.ClientId))
 59:             errors.Add("Infisical Client ID is required (SecretProvider:Infisical:ClientId)");
 60: 
 61:         if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(options.ClientSecret))
 62:             errors.Add("Infisical Client Secret is required (SecretProvider:Infisical:ClientSecret)");
 63: 
 64:         if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(options.Environment))
 65:             errors.Add("Infisical Environment is required (SecretProvider:Infisical:Environment)");
 66: 
 67:         if (!Uri.TryCreate(options.Url, UriKind.Absolute, out var uri) ||
 68:             (uri.Scheme != "http" && uri.Scheme != "https"))
 69:         {
 70:             errors.Add("Infisical URL must be a valid HTTP/HTTPS URL");
 71:         }
 72:     }
 73: 
 74:     private static void ValidateVaultOptions(VaultOptions options, List<string> errors)
 75:     {
 76:         if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(options.Url))
 77:             errors.Add("Vault URL is required (SecretProvider:Vault:Url)");
 78: 
 79:         if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(options.RoleId))
 80:             errors.Add("Vault Role ID is required (SecretProvider:Vault:RoleId)");
 81: 
 82:         if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(options.SecretId))
 83:             errors.Add("Vault Secret ID is required (SecretProvider:Vault:SecretId)");
 84: 
 85:         if (!Uri.TryCreate(options.Url, UriKind.Absolute, out var uri) ||
 86:             (uri.Scheme != "http" && uri.Scheme != "https"))
 87:         {
 88:             errors.Add("Vault URL must be a valid HTTP/HTTPS URL");
 89:         }
 90: 
 91:         if (options.Paths.Count == 0)
 92:             errors.Add("At least one Vault secret path is required (SecretProvider:Vault:Paths)");
 93:     }
 94: 
 95:     private static void ValidateAzureKeyVaultOptions(AzureKeyVaultOptions options, List<string> errors)
 96:     {
 97:         if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(options.VaultUrl))
 98:             errors.Add("Azure Key Vault URL is required (SecretProvider:AzureKeyVault:VaultUrl)");
 99: 
100:         if (!Uri.TryCreate(options.VaultUrl, UriKind.Absolute, out var uri) ||
101:             uri.Scheme != "https" ||
102:             !uri.Host.EndsWith(".vault.azure.net", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
103:         {
104:             errors.Add("Azure Key Vault URL must be a valid HTTPS URL ending in .vault.azure.net");
105:         }
106: 
107: 
108:         var hasServicePrincipal = !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(options.ClientId);
109:         if (hasServicePrincipal)
110:         {
111:             if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(options.TenantId))
112:                 errors.Add("Azure AD Tenant ID is required when using Service Principal auth");
113:             if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(options.ClientSecret))
114:                 errors.Add("Azure AD Client Secret is required when using Service Principal auth");
115:         }
116:     }
117: 
118:     private static void ValidateAwsSecretsManagerOptions(AwsSecretsManagerOptions options, List<string> errors)
119:     {
120:         if (string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(options.Region))
121:             errors.Add("AWS Region is required (SecretProvider:AwsSecretsManager:Region)");
122: 
123:         if (options.SecretNames.Count == 0)
124:             errors.Add("At least one AWS secret name is required (SecretProvider:AwsSecretsManager:SecretNames)");
125: 
126: 
127:         var hasExplicitCredentials = !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(options.AccessKeyId);
128:         if (hasExplicitCredentials && string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(options.SecretAccessKey))
129:         {
130:             errors.Add("AWS Secret Access Key is required when Access Key ID is provided");
131:         }
132:     }
133: }

## File: .claude/skills/auth-patterns/resources/user-id-extraction.md
````markdown
  1: # User ID Extraction Pattern
  2: 
  3: This document details the **CRITICAL** pattern for safely and consistently extracting the user ID from JWT claims within the ISLAMU Event platform. This pattern accounts for various claim types and provides a robust fallback mechanism.
  4: 
  5: ---
  6: 
  7: ## 1. The Fallback Pattern (ASP.NET Core)
  8: 
  9: Always use this specific fallback logic when attempting to retrieve the authenticated user's ID from a `ClaimsPrincipal` (e.g., `HttpContext.User`).
 10: 
 11: ```csharp
 12: using System.Security.Claims; // Required for ClaimTypes
 13: 
 14: // Access the ClaimsPrincipal from HttpContext or another source
 15: // Example from an ASP.NET Core Controller:
 16: var claimsPrincipal = HttpContext.User;
 17: 
 18: var userId = claimsPrincipal.FindFirst("sub")?.Value // 1. Standard OIDC subject claim (preferred)
 19:     ?? claimsPrincipal.FindFirst("http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/nameidentifier")?.Value // 2. Legacy .NET nameidentifier claim (fallback)
 20:     ?? claimsPrincipal.FindFirst("sid")?.Value; // 3. Session ID (last resort, less common for user ID)
 21: 
 22: if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(userId))
 23: {
 24:     // Handle the case where no user ID could be extracted.
 25:     // This typically indicates a misconfigured token or an unauthenticated request
 26:     // that reached an [Authorize] endpoint without a valid user context.
 27:     // Depending on context (e.g., API controller), you might return Unauthorized.
 28:     // In a Blazor component, you might redirect to login.
 29:     throw new UnauthorizedAccessException("User ID claim could not be found in the token.");
 30: }
 31: 
 32: // At this point, userId contains the extracted user ID
 33: Console.WriteLine($"Extracted User ID: {userId}");
 34: ```
 35: 
 36: ### Claim Priority Explained:
 37: 
 38: 1.  **`sub` (Subject)**: This is the **standard and preferred** claim for a unique identifier of the user (or "subject") in OpenID Connect (OIDC) and OAuth 2.0. Keycloak typically populates this.
 39: 2.  **`http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/nameidentifier`**: This is the .NET Framework's default claim type for `NameIdentifier` (User ID). It's a common fallback, especially when dealing with older identity providers or configurations.
 40: 3.  **`sid` (Session ID)**: This is the session ID claim. While it's a unique identifier for a session, it's generally **less preferred** for identifying the user directly across different sessions or systems. It's included as a last resort fallback if `sub` and `nameidentifier` are absent, but its usage as a primary user ID should be carefully evaluated based on the specific requirements.
 41: 
 42: ---
 43: 
 44: ## 2. Using the Pattern in MediatR Handlers
 45: 
 46: When performing authorization checks or data filtering based on the current user in MediatR handlers, the user ID typically needs to be passed from the controller (where `HttpContext` is available) to the handler.
 47: 
 48: ```csharp
 49: // File: Explore.API/Controllers/EventController.cs
 50: using MediatR;
 51: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;
 52: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;
 53: using System.Security.Claims; // For ClaimsPrincipal and ClaimTypes
 54: 
 55: [Authorize]
 56: [HttpPost]
 57: public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<Guid>>> CreateEvent([FromBody] CreateEventDto dto)
 58: {
 59:     // ✅ Extract user ID using the fallback pattern
 60:     var userId = HttpContext.User.FindFirst("sub")?.Value
 61:         ?? HttpContext.User.FindFirst(ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier)?.Value // Using ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier constant
 62:         ?? HttpContext.User.FindFirst("sid")?.Value;
 63: 
 64:     if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(userId))
 65:     {
 66:         return Unauthorized(new { error = "User ID not found in token" });
 67:     }
 68: 
 69:     // Pass the extracted userId to the command
 70:     var command = new CreateEventCommand { EventDto = dto, UserId = userId }; // Assume CreateEventCommand has a UserId property
 71:     var response = await _mediator.Send(command);
 72:     return Ok(response);
 73: }
 74: 
 75: // File: Explore.Application/Features/Events/Requests/Commands/CreateEventCommand.cs
 76: public class CreateEventCommand : IRequest<BaseCommandResponse<Guid>>
 77: {
 78:     public CreateEventDto EventDto { get; set; }
 79:     public string UserId { get; set; } = string.Empty; // ✅ Property to receive the userId
 80: }
 81: 
 82: // File: Explore.Application/Features/Events/Handlers/Commands/CreateEventCommandHandler.cs
 83: public class CreateEventCommandHandler : IRequestHandler<CreateEventCommand, BaseCommandResponse<Guid>>
 84: {
 85:     // ... dependencies ...
 86: 
 87:     public async Task<BaseCommandResponse<Guid>> Handle(CreateEventCommand request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
 88:     {
 89:         // ... validation ...
 90:         
 91:         // ✅ Use request.UserId for ownership checks or data filtering
 92:         var isAuthorized = await _permissionService.HasPermission(request.UserId, "create_event");
 93:         if (!isAuthorized)
 94:         {
 95:             // Handle unauthorized access within the application layer
 96:             // For example, return a specific error in BaseCommandResponse
 97:         }
 98: 
 99:         // ... create event logic ...
100:     }
101: }
102: ```
103: 
104: ---
105: 
106: ## 3. Key Considerations
107: 
108: *   **Security**: Always perform server-side validation of user claims. Do not trust client-side assertions.
109: *   **Consistency**: Adhere strictly to this pattern across all services that require user ID extraction.
110: *   **Error Handling**: Ensure that `string.IsNullOrEmpty(userId)` is handled appropriately (e.g., returning `401 Unauthorized` from an API controller).
111: *   **Blazor vs. API**: In Blazor Server-side, `HttpContext.User` is directly available. In Blazor WebAssembly, you typically rely on the BFF pattern, where the server-side Blazor app handles authentication and potentially passes claims to the WASM client.
112: 
113: ---
114: 
115: **Related Skills**:
116: - [`auth-patterns`](../SKILL.md) - General authentication and authorization rules.
117: - [`blazor-bff-patterns`](../../blazor-bff-patterns/SKILL.md) - Blazor-specific authentication context.
118: - [`cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`](../../cqrs-mediatr-guidelines/SKILL.md) - How to pass user context to MediatR handlers.
````

## File: .claude/skills/cqrs-mediatr-guidelines/resources/api-endpoint-design.md
````markdown
 1: # API Endpoint Design for CQRS
 2: 
 3: Use this guide when wiring HTTP endpoints to MediatR commands/queries.
 4: 
 5: ## Core Rules
 6: 
 7: - Keep controllers transport-only: parse HTTP input, send request to MediatR, map result to HTTP status code.
 8: - Keep handlers application-only: business logic, validation, orchestration, repository usage.
 9: - Never return domain entities from API endpoints. Return DTOs or response envelopes.
10: 
11: ## Route and Method Conventions
12: 
13: - Collection read: `GET /api/{entities}` -> query request -> paginated DTO result.
14: - Item read: `GET /api/{entities}/{id}` -> query request -> item DTO or `404`.
15: - Create: `POST /api/{entities}` -> command -> `BaseCommandResponse<Guid>` and `201 Created`.
16: - Update: `PUT /api/{entities}/{id}` -> command -> `BaseCommandResponse<Guid>` and `200 OK`.
17: - Delete: `DELETE /api/{entities}/{id}` -> command -> `bool` and `204`/`404`.
18: 
19: Use route constraints for clarity (`{id:guid}`) where applicable.
20: 
21: ## HTTP Status Mapping
22: 
23: - Successful list/detail query: `200 OK`
24: - Successful create: `201 Created` with `Location` header
25: - Successful update: `200 OK`
26: - Successful delete: `204 NoContent`
27: - Validation failures: `400 BadRequest`
28: - Unauthenticated: `401 Unauthorized`
29: - Unauthorized: `403 Forbidden`
30: - Missing resource: `404 NotFound`
31: 
32: ## Controller Pattern
33: 
34: ```csharp
35: [HttpPost]
36: [Authorize]
37: public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<Guid>>> Create(
38:     [FromBody] CreateEntityDto dto,
39:     CancellationToken cancellationToken)
40: {
41:     var response = await _mediator.Send(new CreateEntityCommand { EntityDto = dto }, cancellationToken);
42: 
43:     if (!response.Success)
44:         return BadRequest(response);
45: 
46:     return CreatedAtRoute(
47:         RouteNames.GetEntityById,
48:         new { id = response.Id },
49:         response);
50: }
51: ```
52: 
53: ## Handler Pattern Boundary
54: 
55: - Handler receives typed request and `CancellationToken`.
56: - Handler manually instantiates validator (if required by project pattern).
57: - Handler maps DTO -> Entity, saves through repository, maps result to response envelope.
58: - Handler does not set HTTP status codes.
59: 
60: ## Pagination Pattern
61: 
62: - Query contracts should include at minimum `PageNumber` and `PageSize`.
63: - Return `PaginatedResult<TDto>` from query handlers.
64: - Controller adds any representation concerns (for example HATEOAS wrapping).
65: 
66: ## Security Placement
67: 
68: - Endpoint gate in controller with `[AllowAnonymous]`/`[Authorize]`/`[Authorize(Roles = "...")]`.
69: - Resource ownership and business permission checks in handlers or authorization behaviors.
````

## File: .claude/skills/error-tracking/resources/api-error-responses.md
````markdown
 1: # API Error Response Contract
 2: 
 3: Define one consistent error contract for all API failures.
 4: 
 5: ## Standard Format
 6: 
 7: Use RFC 7807 `ProblemDetails` as the base envelope:
 8: 
 9: - `type`: canonical error category URI
10: - `title`: short summary
11: - `status`: HTTP status code
12: - `detail`: human-readable explanation
13: - `instance`: request path
14: 
15: Add extensions for operational tracing:
16: 
17: - `traceId`
18: - `correlationId` (if available)
19: - `errors` (validation dictionary for field-level issues)
20: 
21: ## Status Code Mapping
22: 
23: - `400`: validation and malformed request
24: - `401`: unauthenticated
25: - `403`: authenticated but not permitted
26: - `404`: missing resource
27: - `409`: conflict (for example duplicate unique values)
28: - `422`: semantically invalid payload when distinct from shape validation
29: - `500`: unexpected server error
30: 
31: ## Practical Rules
32: 
33: - Never return raw exception internals in production.
34: - Keep validation errors deterministic and field-addressable.
35: - Emit structured logs before writing response bodies.
36: - Include trace identifiers in both logs and response payload for incident triage.
37: 
38: ## Example
39: 
40: ```json
41: {
42:   "type": "https://httpstatuses.com/400",
43:   "title": "Validation failed",
44:   "status": 400,
45:   "detail": "One or more validation errors occurred.",
46:   "instance": "/api/events",
47:   "traceId": "00-1f6...",
48:   "errors": {
49:     "title": ["Title is required"],
50:     "eventTypeId": ["Event type not found"]
51:   }
52: }
53: ```
````

112: ## Decisions Made
113: 
114: | Decision | Rationale |
115: |----------|-----------|
116: | **Media type API versioning** (Accept header: `application/json;v=1.0`) | User explicit request. Keeps URLs clean (no `/` changes). Standard approach for APIs consumed by controlled clients. |
117: | ETag via response body hash (not entity version) | Works with OutputCache; no entity changes needed for Phase 3.2 |
118: | Idempotency via HybridCache + DB table | Survives restarts; HybridCache for fast lookup (deferred to future session) |
119: | Cursor pagination keyset-based (not token) | More efficient for PostgreSQL; no session state (deferred to future session) |
120: | Security headers as middleware (not filter) | Applies to all responses including non-controller (health, metrics) |
121: | Rate limiting via built-in ASP.NET Core | Already partially implemented; no external dependency needed |
122: | **Token bucket for global rate limiter** | Better burst tolerance than fixed window; configurable replenish rate |
123: | **No-op rate limiter in Testing environment** | Prevents 429s during parallel test execution in `WebApplicationFactory` |
124: | **Loopback IP bypass in global limiter** | `IPAddress.IsLoopback` -> NoLimiter, supports local development |
125: | **X-Forwarded-For support** | Required for ngrok/Cloudflare reverse proxy deployments |
126: | **Rate limiting defaults are config-driven** | `appsettings.json` section `RateLimiting:*` with sensible defaults baked into code |

## File: dev/active/api-improvement/api-improvement-plan.md
````markdown
  1: # Plan: Enterprise-Grade API Improvement
  2: 
  3: **Last Updated**: 2026-02-18 (plan created) | Implementation started same day
  4: 
  5: ---
  6: 
  7: ## Executive Summary
  8: 
  9: The ISLAMU Event API (`Explore.API`) is already a strong implementation with Clean Architecture, CQRS, HATEOAS/HAL+JSON, dual-layer caching (OutputCache + HybridCache), Cerbos authorization, OpenTelemetry observability, and response compression. This plan identifies the remaining gaps to bring the API to a fully enterprise-grade, highly scalable implementation following best practices for .NET 10.
 10: 
 11: The improvements are categorized into 6 phases, ordered by impact and dependency. The plan prioritizes hardening, performance, and developer experience while respecting YAGNI and the repo's existing conventions.
 12: 
 13: ---
 14: 
 15: ## Current State Analysis
 16: 
 17: ### Already Implemented (Strengths)
 18: 
 19: | Feature | Status | Notes |
 20: |---------|--------|-------|
 21: | Clean Architecture + CQRS | Complete | MediatR, AutoMapper, strict layer separation |
 22: | Keycloak JWT + BFF | Complete | Multi-audience validation, BFF pattern |
 23: | Cerbos Authorization | Complete | `AuthorizationBehavior`, dual-provider with circuit breaker fallback |
 24: | HATEOAS/HAL+JSON | Complete | 17 assemblers, 17 link policies, `Prefer: return=minimal` |
 25: | OutputCache (3 policies) | Complete | Lookup 1h, List 30s, Detail 60s |
 26: | HybridCache (L1+L2) | Complete | Used in ~15+ handlers, stampede protection |
 27: | Response Compression | Complete | Brotli + Gzip |
 28: | OpenTelemetry | Complete | Traces, metrics, logs, Prometheus, OTLP |
 29: | Health Checks | Complete | Database, secrets, shutdown-aware |
 30: | RFC 7807 ProblemDetails | Complete | Global + validation exception handlers |
 31: | Specification Pattern | Complete | Composable filters/sorts for events |
 32: | Graceful Shutdown | Complete | 25s SIGTERM grace period |
 33: | Pagination | Complete | Offset-based, max 100, HATEOAS nav links |
 34: | Architecture Tests | Complete | NetArchTest layer validation |
 35: 
 36: ### Gaps Identified
 37: 
 38: | Gap | Impact | Effort |
 39: |-----|--------|--------|
 40: | No API versioning (hardcoded `v1`) | High | M |
 41: | No security headers (CSP, X-Content-Type-Options, etc.) | High | S |
 42: | Rate limiting only on 1 endpoint | High | M |
 43: | No ETag / conditional requests | Medium | M |
 44: | No idempotency keys for POST/PUT | Medium | L |
 45: | No structured request/response logging middleware | Medium | S |
 46: | Correlation ID only outgoing, not incoming | Medium | S |
 47: | No compiled queries on hot paths | Medium | M |
 48: | CORS policies overly permissive | Medium | S |
 49: | No cursor-based pagination option | Low | M |
 50: | No request timeout per endpoint | Low | S |
 51: | No API changelog / versioned docs | Low | S |
 52: 
 53: ---
 54: 
 55: ## Proposed Future State
 56: 
 57: A fully enterprise-grade API with:
 58: - **Formal API versioning** via `Asp.Versioning` with **media type strategy** (`Accept: application/json;v=1.0`) — *changed from URL path per user request*
 59: - **Comprehensive security headers** via middleware
 60: - **Tiered rate limiting** (global, per-user, per-endpoint)
 61: - **ETag-based conditional requests** for bandwidth optimization on GET endpoints
 62: - **Idempotency keys** for safe POST/PUT retries
 63: - **Structured request logging** with correlation ID propagation through Serilog
 64: - **Compiled EF Core queries** on hot-path repository methods
 65: - **Production-hardened CORS** with explicit origin allowlists
 66: - **Cursor-based pagination** as an alternative for real-time feeds
 67: - **Per-endpoint request timeouts** for long-running operations
 68: 
 69: ---
 70: 
 71: ## Phase 1: Security Hardening (Week 1)
 72: **Priority: Critical** | **Risk: Low** | **Dependencies: None**
 73: 
 74: ### Task 1.1: Add Security Headers Middleware
 75: - **File**: `Explore.API/Middleware/SecurityHeadersMiddleware.cs`
 76: - **Action**: Create middleware that adds `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, `Permissions-Policy`, `Content-Security-Policy` (for API: `default-src 'none'`)
 77: - **Register**: In `Program.cs` pipeline before `UseRouting()`
 78: - **Acceptance Criteria**:
 79:   - [ ] All responses include security headers
 80:   - [ ] CSP configured appropriately for API (not Blazor)
 81:   - [ ] Integration test verifying headers present
 82: - **Effort**: S
 83: - **Related Skill**: `error-tracking`
 84: 
 85: ### Task 1.2: Harden CORS Policies
 86: - **File**: `Explore.API/Program.cs` (CORS section)
 87: - **Action**: Replace `AllowAnyOrigin` on `InternalAppPolicy` and `ExternalAppPolicy` with explicit origin allowlists from configuration. Keep `DevPolicy` permissive for development only.
 88: - **Acceptance Criteria**:
 89:   - [ ] Dev policy remains permissive
 90:   - [ ] Internal/External policies use `WithOrigins()` from config
 91:   - [ ] Configuration section `Cors:AllowedOrigins` added to `appsettings.json`
 92:   - [ ] Integration test verifying CORS behavior
 93: - **Effort**: S
 94: - **Related Skill**: `auth-patterns`
 95: 
 96: ### Task 1.3: Tiered Rate Limiting
 97: - **Files**: `Explore.API/Program.cs`, new `Explore.API/RateLimiting/` directory
 98: - **Action**: Add tiered rate limiting:
 99:   - **Global**: Fixed window, 1000 req/min per IP (configurable)
100:   - **Authenticated**: Token bucket, 200 req/min per user
101:   - **Write**: Fixed window, 30 req/min per user for POST/PUT/DELETE
102:   - **Admin**: Separate higher limits
103: - **Configuration**: `appsettings.json` section `RateLimiting:*`
104: - **Acceptance Criteria**:
105:   - [ ] Global rate limit on all endpoints
106:   - [ ] Per-user rate limit on authenticated endpoints
107:   - [ ] Stricter limit on write operations
108:   - [ ] 429 Too Many Requests with `Retry-After` header
109:   - [ ] Rate limit headers (`X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`)
110:   - [ ] Integration test for rate limiting behavior
111: - **Effort**: M

113: 
114: ---
115: 
116: ## Phase 2: Observability & Debugging (Week 1-2)
117: **Priority: High** | **Risk: Low** | **Dependencies: None**
118: 
119: ### Task 2.1: Structured Request/Response Logging Middleware
120: - **File**: `Explore.API/Middleware/RequestLoggingMiddleware.cs`
121: - **Action**: Create middleware that logs every request with: HTTP method, path, status code, duration (ms), request size, response size, user ID (if authenticated), tenant ID, correlation ID. Use Serilog structured logging.
122: - **Register**: In `Program.cs` pipeline early (after exception handler)
123: - **Acceptance Criteria**:
124:   - [ ] All requests logged with structured properties
125:   - [ ] Sensitive data (auth headers, body) NOT logged
126:   - [ ] Duration measured accurately
127:   - [ ] Correlation ID included in log context
128:   - [ ] Unit test for middleware behavior
129: - **Effort**: S
130: - **Related Skill**: `error-tracking`
131: 
132: ### Task 2.2: Correlation ID Propagation (Incoming + Outgoing)
133: - **File**: `Explore.API/Middleware/CorrelationIdMiddleware.cs`
134: - **Action**: Create middleware that:
135:   1. Reads `X-Correlation-ID` or `X-Request-ID` from incoming request headers
136:   2. Generates a new one if absent (using `Activity.Current?.Id ?? Guid.NewGuid()`)
137:   3. Pushes to Serilog `LogContext` as `CorrelationId`
138:   4. Adds to response headers
139:   5. Existing `CorrelationIdDelegatingHandler` continues to propagate on outgoing HTTP
140: - **Acceptance Criteria**:
141:   - [ ] Incoming correlation ID respected
142:   - [ ] New ID generated when absent
143:   - [ ] All Serilog logs include CorrelationId property
144:   - [ ] Response includes `X-Correlation-ID` header
145:   - [ ] Integration test verifying propagation

192: - **Action**:

194:   - Handle `If-None-Match` header → return 304 Not Modified when match
195:   - Apply only to `GET` requests returning `application/json` or `application/hal+json`

204: ### Task 3.3: Idempotency Keys for Write Operations

206: - **Action**:

388: ### Task 6.4: API Changelog
389: - **File**: `docs/API_CHANGELOG.md`
390: - **Action**:
391:   - Create API changelog documenting all breaking/non-breaking changes

393:   - Include current v1 API as baseline entry
394:   - Add section in OpenAPI description linking to changelog
395: - **Acceptance Criteria**:

397:   - [ ] Format follows Keep a Changelog
398:   - [ ] Linked from Scalar/Swagger UI
399: - **Effort**: S
400: 
401: ---
402: 
403: ## Risk Assessment and Mitigation
404: 
405: | Risk | Probability | Impact | Mitigation |
406: |------|-------------|--------|------------|
407: | API versioning breaks existing clients | Medium | High | Apply `[ApiVersion("1.0")]` only; existing URLs unchanged |
408: | ETag computation adds latency | Low | Medium | Use efficient hashing; OutputCache handles most cases |
409: | Idempotency table grows unbounded | Medium | Medium | TTL cleanup + background job to purge expired records |
410: | Compiled queries reduce flexibility | Low | Medium | Keep non-compiled versions for dynamic/specification queries |
411: | Rate limiting blocks legitimate traffic | Medium | High | Start with generous limits; monitor before tightening |
412: | Concurrency tokens break existing updates | Medium | High | Make `RowVersion` optional in DTOs initially; gradual adoption |
413: 
414: ---
415: 
416: ## Success Metrics
417: 
418: | Metric | Current | Target |
419: |--------|---------|--------|
420: | Security headers score (securityheaders.com) | D/F | A |
421: | P95 API response time (hot path) | ~50ms (estimated) | <30ms |
422: | Cache hit ratio (HybridCache) | Unknown | >80% |
423: | 304 Not Modified ratio | 0% | >30% of repeated GETs |
424: | Rate limit false positive rate | N/A | <0.1% |
425: | Test coverage for middleware | 0% | >90% |
426: | Architecture test violations | 0 | 0 (maintained) |
427: 
428: ---
429: 
430: ## Effort Estimates Summary
431: 
432: | Phase | Effort | Duration |
433: |-------|--------|----------|
434: | Phase 1: Security Hardening | S+S+M = M | ~3-4 days |
435: | Phase 2: Observability & Debugging | S+S+M = M | ~3-4 days |
436: | Phase 3: API Design & Contract | M+M+L+M = XL | ~8-10 days |
437: | Phase 4: Performance Optimization | M+S+M = M | ~4-5 days |
438: | Phase 5: Resilience & Reliability | S+M+M = M | ~4-5 days |
439: | Phase 6: Testing & Documentation | M+L+S+S = L | ~6-7 days |
440: | **Total** | | **~28-35 days** |
441: 
442: ---
443: 
444: ## Critique: Potential Risks & Unknowns
445: 
446: **Most likely failure point**: **Task 3.3 (Idempotency Keys)** is the highest-complexity task. The interaction between `IdempotencyMiddleware`, `HybridCache`, and the database persistence layer is non-trivial. Edge cases include: partial failures (request processed but response not cached), concurrent identical requests racing, and serialization of diverse response types. The TTL cleanup also needs a background service. **Recommendation**: Start with a simpler in-memory-only idempotency check (using `HybridCache` alone, no DB table) and add persistence later if needed.
447: 
448: **Second risk area**: **Task 3.1 (API Versioning)** has a deceptively large blast radius. Every controller file needs modification, and the route templates change from `[Route("api/[controller]")]` to `[Route("api/v{version:apiVersion}/[controller]")]`. This touches 40+ controllers. While the change is mechanical, any typo breaks the endpoint. **Mitigation**: Write the architecture test first (Task 6.3), then apply changes systematically.
449: 
450: **Third risk area**: **Task 5.2 (Optimistic Concurrency)** could break existing update flows if clients don't send the `RowVersion` back. PostgreSQL's `xmin` is auto-managed but requires EF Core-specific configuration with the Npgsql provider. This needs careful testing with the existing integration test suite.
451: 
452: **Unknown**: The compiled queries (Task 4.1) performance gain depends on query complexity. Simple key lookups may see <5% improvement. The benchmark suite (Task 6.1) should be completed first to identify the actual hot paths worth optimizing. Don't pre-optimize all queries.
````

## File: dev/active/harmonic-jumping-crescent.md
````markdown
   1: # Blazor Enterprise Refactoring - ISLAMU Event
   2: 
   3: ## Executive Summary
   4: 
   5: Transform the ISLAMU Event Blazor frontend into an enterprise-grade application that fully utilizes all API capabilities. This plan addresses critical architectural issues, implements missing features, and establishes production-ready patterns.
   6: 
   7: **Scope**: 45+ entities, 180+ DTOs, complete event lifecycle management, organization workflows, and advanced filtering.
   8: 
   9: **Timeline**: 40-60 hours of focused implementation.
  10: 
  11: **Outcome**: Production-ready, maintainable, enterprise-grade Blazor WASM+Server application.
  12: 
  13: ---
  14: 
  15: ## Critical Issues Identified
  16: 
  17: ### 🔴 High Priority (Breaks Core Functionality)
  18: 
  19: 1. **Event Editing Broken**
  20:    - Sessions not updated when editing event
  21:    - Categories/tags not persisted on update
  22:    - New sessions added in editor but ignored on save
  23:    - **Impact**: Cannot modify events after creation
  24: 
  25: 2. **Event Session Management**
  26:    - Sessions created AFTER event (not atomic)
  27:    - No rollback if session creation fails
  28:    - Cannot edit existing sessions in event edit flow
  29:    - **Impact**: Data inconsistency, orphaned events
  30: 
  31: 3. **Hard-coded TenantId**
  32:    - `Guid.Parse("00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001")` in CreateEvent
  33:    - Should come from authenticated user context
  34:    - **Impact**: Multi-tenancy broken, security issue
  35: 
  36: 4. **No State Management**
  37:    - UserId extracted multiple times
  38:    - TenantId hard-coded
  39:    - No global auth context
  40:    - **Impact**: Maintainability nightmare
  41: 
  42: ### 🟡 Medium Priority (Missing Features)
  43: 
  44: 5. **Organization Member Management**
  45:    - API has full invitation workflow
  46:    - No UI for invitations, member roles, positions
  47:    - **Impact**: Cannot manage organization teams
  48: 
  49: 6. **Advanced Event Filtering**
  50:    - API supports filtering by madhab, age, gender, language, location
  51:    - UI only implements basic filters
  52:    - **Impact**: Poor discovery experience
  53: 
  54: 7. **Lookup Table Management**
  55:    - No admin UI for EventTypes, Formats, Statuses, Languages, etc.
  56:    - **Impact**: Cannot configure system without DB access
  57: 
  58: 8. **Registration Flow Incomplete**
  59:    - Approval workflow not implemented
  60:    - No registration status tracking
  61:    - **Impact**: Manual events cannot use approval system
  62: 
  63: ### 🟢 Low Priority (Optimization)
  64: 
  65: 9. **HTTP Client Anti-Pattern**
  66:    - ImageStorageService creates new HttpClient per upload
  67:    - Should use IHttpClientFactory
  68:    - **Impact**: Socket exhaustion risk
  69: 
  70: 10. **Sequential Operations**
  71:     - Category/tag assignment loops sequentially
  72:     - Should parallelize after event creation
  73:     - **Impact**: Slow event creation
  74: 
  75: ---
  76: 
  77: ## MudBlazor 7 Best Practices Integration
  78: 
  79: Based on latest MudBlazor documentation, we'll follow these patterns:
  80: 
  81: **Form Validation**:
  82: ```razor
  83: <EditForm Model="@model" OnValidSubmit="OnValidSubmit">
  84:     <DataAnnotationsValidator/>
  85:     <MudTextField @bind-Value="model.Title" For="@(() => model.Title)" Label="Title" />
  86:     <ValidationSummary />
  87: </EditForm>
  88: ```
  89: 
  90: **Dialog Pattern**:
  91: ```csharp
  92: var parameters = new DialogParameters<MyDialog>
  93: {
  94:     { x => x.ContentText, "Dialog content" },
  95:     { x => x.Data, myData }
  96: };
  97: var dialog = await DialogService.ShowAsync<MyDialog>("Title", parameters);
  98: var result = await dialog.Result;
  99: ```
 100: 
 101: **Code-Behind Pattern** (Recommended for complex components):
 102: ```csharp
 103: // Component.razor
 104: @inherits ComponentBase
 105: @code { /* minimal inline code */ }
 106: 
 107: // Component.razor.cs
 108: public partial class Component : ComponentBase
 109: {
 110:     [Inject] private IService Service { get; set; }
 111:     // All logic here
 112: }
 113: ```
 114: 
 115: **EventCallback Usage**:
 116: ```csharp
 117: [Parameter] public EventCallback<T> OnDataChanged { get; set; }
 118: await OnDataChanged.InvokeAsync(data);
 119: ```
 120: 
 121: ---
 122: 
 123: ## Implementation Strategy
 124: 
 125: ### Phase 1: Foundation & Architecture (8-12 hours)
 126: 
 127: **Goal**: Fix critical architectural issues, establish enterprise patterns.
 128: 
 129: #### 1.1 State Management Foundation

 140:     private readonly IHttpContextAccessor _httpContextAccessor;
 141: 
 142:     public async Task<string> GetCurrentUserIdAsync()
 143:     {
 144:         // Fallback chain: sub → nameidentifier → sid
 145:         return userId ?? throw new UnauthorizedException();
 146:     }
 147: 
 148:     public async Task<Guid> GetCurrentTenantIdAsync()

 150:         // Extract from claims or tenant context

 153: }
