 42: ---
 43: 
 44: ## Key Decisions
 45: 
 46: ### D1: Tenant.IsActive -> Computed Property (Non-Breaking)
 47: **Decision**: Keep `IsActive` as a computed property from `TenantStatus.IsActiveState` to avoid breaking existing code.
 48: **Rationale**: `IsActive` is referenced in query filters, Cerbos attributes, and Blazor conditionals. Making it a computed navigation keeps backward compatibility.
 49: 
 50: ### D2: Email Integration Deferred
 51: **Decision**: Invitation system generates tokens + copy-link only. Email delivery is a separate feature.
 52: **Rationale**: Email service (SMTP abstraction) is a separate work item in `dev/active/email-smtp-abstraction/`. This plan focuses on the invitation data model and API.
 53: 
 54: ### D3: 4-Step Wizard (Not More)
 55: **Decision**: Onboarding wizard has exactly 4 steps: Identity, Policies, Branding & Domain, Review & Complete.
 56: **Rationale**: Enterprise SaaS research shows minimal required steps + checklist for optional steps. More than 4 steps causes abandonment.
 57: 
 58: ### D4: TenantProvisioningService (Shared Logic)
 59: **Decision**: Extract tenant provisioning into a shared service used by both admin-created and self-service flows.
 60: **Rationale**: DRY principle. Both flows create the same resources (tenant, settings, onboarding state, capabilities, first member).
 61: 
 62: ### D5: Phase 0 First (Critical Auth Fix)
 63: **Decision**: Fix authorization bug before any other work.
 64: **Rationale**: Any tenant member can currently complete onboarding. This is a security vulnerability that must be fixed immediately.
 65: 
 66: ### D6: TenantStatus as Lookup Table (Not Enum)
 67: **Decision**: TenantStatus is a database lookup table entity with Id(int), MasterCode, FullName, Description, IsActiveState(bool).
 68: **Rationale**: Matches existing `ApprovalStatus`/`Madhab`/`AnalyticsProvider` pattern. Provides referential integrity, metadata support (DisplayName, Description), and can be extended without code changes. Cybertec PostgreSQL analysis confirms lookup tables > enums for lifecycle management.
 69: **Pattern reference**: `Explore.Domain/ApprovalStatus.cs`, `Explore.Persistence/Configurations/Entities/ApprovalStatusConfiguration.cs`
 70: 
 71: ### D7: TenantLifecycleLog for Status Transition Audit
 72: **Decision**: New `TenantLifecycleLog` entity tracks every status change: OldStatusId -> NewStatusId, TransitionedByUserId, Reason, TransitionedAt.
 73: **Rationale**: IAuditableEntity only tracks last update (CreatedBy/UpdatedBy). Lifecycle transitions need full history with actor, reason, and before/after state. Follows WorkOS/Infisical audit log patterns.
 74: **Pattern reference**: `Explore.Domain/ConfigurationChangeLog.cs` (OldValue/NewValue, Scope, ActionType pattern)
 75: 
 76: ### D8: Transactional Provisioning (Explicit Transaction)
 77: **Decision**: `ITenantProvisioningService` wraps all provisioning steps in explicit `BeginTransactionAsync()`/`CommitAsync()`/`RollbackAsync()`.
 78: **Rationale**: Current `CompleteInstanceOnboardingCommandHandler` creates 5 records without explicit transaction -- a failure mid-way leaves orphaned records. Stripe-style idempotency check (slug exists?) before creating.
 79: **Pattern reference**: `Explore.Persistence/Repositories/AppSettingRepository.cs` (BulkUpdateAsync)
 80: 
 81: ### D9: Advanced Invitation Security
 82: **Decision**: TenantInvitation gets `AllowedDomain` field for domain whitelisting + role ceiling enforcement (inviter role >= invitee role) + one-time token hardening (accept + invalidate in same transaction).
 83: **Rationale**: Clerk verified domains pattern. Prevents privilege escalation (TenantAdmin inviting TenantOwner). Token must be invalidated atomically with accept to prevent race conditions.
 84: 
 85: ### D10: Onboarding Funnel Analytics via Existing IAnalyticsProvider
 86: **Decision**: Track wizard step completions and lifecycle transitions using existing `IAnalyticsProvider.TrackAsync()`. No new analytics infrastructure needed.
 87: **Rationale**: `RuntimeAnalyticsProvider` supports runtime switching across None/Posthog/Plausible/Rybbit/RudderStack with fire-and-forget behavior. Events: `onboarding.step_completed` (step_name, step_index), `tenant.status_changed` (old, new, reason).
 88: **Pattern reference**: `Explore.Application/Contracts/Infrastructure/IAnalyticsProvider.cs`, `Explore.Infrastructure/Analytics/RuntimeAnalyticsProvider.cs`
 89: 
 90: ### D11: Backend Lock Enforcement (Not UI-Only)
 91: **Decision**: `UpdateTenantPolicySettingsCommandHandler` must check `SystemSetting.IsLocked` and throw `ValidationException` if a locked setting is being modified.
 92: **Rationale**: UI currently hides locked fields but the handler doesn't validate. Backend enforcement is mandatory -- UI hiding is insufficient for security.
 93: 
 94: ### D12: Tenant White-Labeling Requires Platform Toggle + Multi-Tenant Mode
 95: **Decision**: Tenant branding overrides are only enabled when both conditions are true: (1) instance deployment mode is `MultiTenant`, and (2) platform admin enabled `tenants.white_labeling_enabled`.
 96: **Rationale**: White-labeling is a tenant capability, not a guaranteed default. Enforcing dual gating avoids accidental tenant-brand drift in single-tenant deployments and keeps platform-admin governance explicit.
 97: 
 98: ### D13: Instance Onboarding Redirect Behavior (Single vs Multi-Tenant)
 99: **Decision**: After completing instance onboarding, do not redirect to tenant onboarding. Instead:
100: - **SingleTenant**: route to the instance-level preferred home page (LandingPage or EventList), then allow tenant admins to override in tenant onboarding when available.
101: - **MultiTenant**: route to instance admin area (platform management pages), not tenant onboarding.
102: **Rationale**: Aligns with enterprise onboarding expectations; single-tenant acts as unified admin, while multi-tenant continues in platform admin area.

202: ## Analytics Integration Notes
203: 
204: The existing analytics abstraction is fully implemented and ready to use for onboarding funnel tracking:
205: 
206: - **Interface**: `IAnalyticsProvider` with `TrackAsync(eventName, properties)`, `IdentifyAsync`, `PageViewAsync`
207: - **Runtime switching**: `RuntimeAnalyticsProvider` resolves active provider at runtime (None/Posthog/Plausible/Rybbit/RudderStack)
208: - **Pattern**: Fire-and-forget with try/catch -- never blocks business logic
209: - **Events to track**:
210:   - `onboarding.step_completed` -- properties: `{ step_name, step_index, tenant_id }`
211:   - `onboarding.completed` -- properties: `{ tenant_id, total_time_seconds }`
212:   - `tenant.status_changed` -- properties: `{ old_status, new_status, reason, tenant_id }`
213:   - `tenant.invitation_sent` -- properties: `{ tenant_id, role }`
214:   - `tenant.invitation_accepted` -- properties: `{ tenant_id, role }`
215: 
216: No new analytics infrastructure needed -- just inject `IAnalyticsProvider` in handlers and call `TrackAsync`.
217: 
218: ### Session Note (2026-02-17)
219: - Analytics naming/conventions were updated globally: enum is now `AnalyticsProviderEnum`, provider selection key is `analytics.provider` (string), and lookup values include `none`, `posthog`, `plausible`, `rybbit`, `rudderstack`.
220: 
221: ---
222: 
223: ## Technical Constraints
224: 
225: 1. **Blazor BFF Separation**: Blazor.Client can ONLY communicate with API via YARP proxy. No direct access to Application/Infrastructure layers.
226: 2. **Named Query Filters (EF Core 10)**: Use `.HasQueryFilter(name: "SoftDelete", ...)` pattern for new entities.
227: 3. **ABOUTME Comments**: Every new file must start with 2-line ABOUTME comment.
228: 4. **File-Scoped Namespaces**: All new files use `namespace Explore.Domain;` (not block style).
229: 5. **Repositories Return Entities**: Never DTOs. Map in handlers.
230: 6. **Commands Return BaseCommandResponse<Guid>**: Not just Guid.
231: 7. **TDD Required**: Write failing test first, then implementation.
232: 8. **No Default Values in Domain Entities**: Set in handlers.
233: 9. **Validators Use Manual Instantiation**: `var validator = new Validator(repo1, repo2);` (not DI).
234: 10. **Lookup Table Pattern**: ValueGeneratedNever(), MaxLength(500), idempotent seeding via LookupTableSeeder.
235: 11. **FK Pattern**: `[ForeignKey("TenantStatus")] public int TenantStatusId` + `public required TenantStatus TenantStatus { get; set; }`
236: 12. **Explicit Transactions**: BeginTransactionAsync/CommitAsync/RollbackAsync for multi-step operations.
237:

````markdown
  1: # Enterprise Tenant Onboarding - Implementation Plan
  2: 
  3: **Last Updated: 2026-02-17**
  4: 
  5: ---
  6: 
  7: ## Executive Summary
  8: 
  9: Transform the tenant admin onboarding experience from a minimal flat form into an enterprise-grade, wizard-based flow that supports both self-service and admin-provisioned tenant creation. The platform currently has a binary onboarding state (complete/not), no invitation system, and critical authorization gaps. This plan addresses all of these while following Clean Architecture principles and maintaining the existing cascading governance model.
 10: 
 11: ### Key Deliverables
 12: 1. **Fix critical authorization gap** — Only TenantAdmin/TenantOwner/InstanceAdmin can complete onboarding (not any member)
 13: 2. **Tenant lifecycle management** — TenantStatus lookup table (Provisioning → Active → Suspended → Archived → Purged) with lifecycle audit log
 14: 3. **Tenant creation handler** — Missing `CreateTenantCommandHandler` with idempotent, transactional provisioning
 15: 4. **Invitation system** — Entity, tokens, domain whitelisting, role ceiling, email templates
 16: 5. **Self-service registration** — Implement the dead `TenantSelfServiceRegistration` flag
 17: 6. **Onboarding wizard with checklist** — Multi-step stepper with progress tracking and funnel analytics
 18: 7. **Single-tenant identity** — Enforce instance admin = tenant admin in single-tenant mode
 19: 8. **Configuration lock enforcement** — Backend-enforced lock pattern, not UI-only
 20: 9. **Instance onboarding routing** — Post-completion routing based on deployment mode and preferred home page
 21: 
 22: ### Enterprise SaaS Patterns Applied
 23: - **Stripe**: Progressive checklist, idempotency keys for provisioning
 24: - **Vercel**: SSO-aware invite flow, simplified team onboarding
 25: - **Clerk**: Verified domains for auto-association, domain-based access constraints
 26: - **WorkOS**: Domain verification (DNS TXT), tenant-scoped audit logs, self-service Admin Portal
 27: - **Supabase**: Organization-first structure with plan selection upfront
 28: - **AWS SaaS Lens**: Tenant-aware logs/metrics during onboarding, centralized provisioning orchestration
 29: 
 30: ### Enterprise Enhancements (v2 — from Altice Informatics Feedback)
 31: | # | Enhancement | Rationale |
 32: |---|-------------|-----------|
 33: | 1 | **TenantStatus Lookup Table** (not enum) | Referential integrity, metadata support (DisplayName, Description, IsActiveState), matches existing ApprovalStatus/Madhab pattern |
 34: | 2 | **TenantLifecycleLog Table** | Full audit trail: OldStatus → NewStatus, ActorId, Reason, Timestamp. IAuditableEntity overwrite is insufficient. |
 35: | 3 | **Transactional Provisioning** | Explicit `BeginTransactionAsync()` + idempotency checks. Prevents orphaned tenants if any step fails. |
 36: | 4 | **Advanced Invitation Security** | Domain whitelisting, one-time token hardening (invalidate in same transaction), role ceiling enforcement |
 37: | 5 | **Onboarding Funnel Analytics** | Track wizard step completions via existing `IAnalyticsProvider` abstraction (None/Posthog/Plausible/Rybbit/RudderStack) |
 38: | 6 | **Backend Lock Enforcement** | `UpdateTenantPolicySettingsCommandHandler` must validate `IsLocked` on SystemSetting — not UI-only |
 39: | 7 | **Table Summary** | TenantStatus lookup, TenantLifecycleLog, enhanced TenantInvitation |
 40: 
 41: ---
 42: 
 43: ## Current State Analysis
 44: 
 45: ### What Exists (Verified)
 46: 
 47: | Component | File | Status |
 48: |-----------|------|--------|
 49: | Tenant entity | `Explore.Domain/Tenant.cs` | ⚠️ Minimal (Id, FullName, Slug, IsActive, NavigationLinks, NOT IAuditableEntity) |

 85: ## Proposed Future State
 86: 
 87: ### Tenant Lifecycle (with Audit Trail)
 88: 
 89: ```
 90: ┌─────────────┐     ┌──────────┐     ┌───────────┐     ┌──────────┐     ┌────────┐
 91: │ Provisioning│────▶│  Active   │────▶│ Suspended  │────▶│ Archived  │────▶│ Purged  │
 92: └─────────────┘     └──────────┘     └───────────┘     └──────────┘     └────────┘
 93:        │                  ▲                  │                                   
 94:        │                  └──────────────────┘                                   
 95:        │              (Reactivate)                                               
 96:        ▼                                                                          
 97:   [Auto-created resources — wrapped in explicit transaction]                     
 98:   - TenantSettings, TenantOnboardingState, TenantCapability, TenantMember       
 99:                                                                                   
100:   [Every transition creates a TenantLifecycleLog entry]                          
101:   - OldStatusId → NewStatusId, TransitionedByUserId, Reason, Timestamp           
102: ```
103: 
104: ### Data Model Changes
105: 
106: ```
107: TenantStatuses (Lookup Table — NEW)
108: ├── Id (int, PK, ValueGeneratedNever)
109: ├── MasterCode (string, required)
110: ├── FullName (string, required)
111: ├── Description (string?)
112: └── IsActiveState (bool)
113: 
114: Tenants (updated)
115: ├── TenantStatusId (int, FK → TenantStatuses — NEW)
116: ├── Description (string? — NEW)
117: ├── IsActive (COMPUTED from TenantStatus.IsActiveState)
118: └── + IAuditableEntity fields
119: 
120: TenantLifecycleLogs (NEW)
121: ├── Id (Guid, UUIDv7)
122: ├── TenantId (Guid, FK → Tenants)
123: ├── OldStatusId (int, FK → TenantStatuses)
124: ├── NewStatusId (int, FK → TenantStatuses)
125: ├── TransitionedByUserId (Guid)
126: ├── Reason (string?)
127: ├── TransitionedAt (DateTime)
128: └── + IAuditableEntity fields
129: 
130: TenantInvitations (NEW — enhanced)
131: ├── AllowedDomain (string? — domain whitelisting)
132: ├── RoleId (int — role ceiling enforced in handler)
133: └── Token (invalidated atomically on accept)
134: ```

281: ## Risk Assessment
282: 
283: | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
284: |------|-----------|--------|------------|
285: | Breaking Tenant.IsActive | High | High | Computed property from TenantStatus.IsActiveState. Grep all IsActive assignments. |
286: | Orphaned tenants | Medium | High | Explicit transaction in TenantProvisioningService |
287: | Domain whitelist bypass | Low | High | Backend validation in handler, not UI-only |
288: | Locked setting override | Medium | High | Backend ValidationException in handler |
289: | Migration on existing data | Low | Medium | Existing tenants default to TenantStatusId=2 (Active) |
290: | Analytics overhead | Low | Low | IAnalyticsProvider is fire-and-forget with try/catch |

100: 
101: ## Important Decisions Made
102: 
103: ### 1. TUnit Assertions (KEEP)
104: **Decision:** Do not migrate to FluentAssertions. Entire codebase uses `await Assert.That(...)` consistently. Migration would create inconsistency with zero behavioral benefit.
105: 
106: ### 2. Received() Policy
107: **Decision:** Remove `Received()` on read operations. Keep ONLY for:
108: - Write operations where the side-effect IS the behavior
109: - Retry logic verification
110: - Error logging verification
111: 
112: ### 3. Separate Tests vs Parameterized
113: **Decision:** Keep separate null/exception tests. Each documents a distinct contract even if current implementation is identical. They guard against future divergence.
114: 
115: ### 4. Test Execution Order
116: **Decision:** Architecture tests first (fast, catches structure issues), then unit tests (fast, pure logic), then integration tests (slow, external deps).
117: 
118: ### 5. In-Memory DB vs TestContainers for API Tests
119: **Observation:** API tests use in-memory EF Core. Persistence tests use TestContainers PostgreSQL. Both approaches coexist. Consider migrating API tests to TestContainers long-term for schema validation, but not in this sprint.
120: 
121: ---
122: 
123: ## Technical Constraints
124: 
125: 1. **NSwag-generated client** (`EventApiClient.g.cs`) — DO NOT MODIFY, ~28k lines
126: 2. **Domain entities** in `Explore.Domain/` — DO NOT MODIFY (per user constraint)
127: 3. **TUnit runs as exe** — use `dotnet run --project <TestProject>` not `dotnet test`
128: 4. **French-locale Windows** — `findstr /i` unreliable, use exact case
129: 5. **HAL response mocking** — Must set `MasterCode` on `CategoryDto` (Required.Always in NSwag)
130: 6. **NSubstitute + ILogger** — Cannot mock `LogError()` directly (extension method); must mock `Log()` with verbose signature
131: 7. **CancellationToken mocking** — NSwag methods have optional CancellationToken; must mock BOTH `Method(arg, Arg.Any<CancellationToken>())` AND `Method(arg)` for NSubstitute to match
132: 
133: ---
134: 
135: ## Anti-Pattern Inventory (from audit)
136: 
137: ### Blazor Client Tests
138: - ~40 instances of `Received()` on read operations
139: - Logger mocked but never verified in error paths
140: - 38% service coverage (11/29)
141: 
142: ### Application Unit Tests
143: - IMapper mocked everywhere (mapping logic untested)
144: - `Received(1)` on repository calls (brittle)
145: - Only 4.8% handler coverage (10/207)
146: - HybridCache compilation errors (pre-existing)
147: 
148: ### API Integration Tests
149: - No test data seeding (in-memory DB starts empty)
150: - `SharedType.PerAssembly` — no test isolation
151: - No multi-role auth testing (always Admin)
152: - Only status code assertions (no body validation)
153: - 21% controller coverage (9/43)
154: 
155: ### Persistence Integration Tests
156: - Only 2 tests for 1 repository
157: - No Update/Delete/Filter/Paginate tests
158: - Uses `EnsureCreated()` instead of `Migrate()`
159: 
160: ### Domain Unit Tests
161: - 0% coverage — placeholder only
162:

## File: docs/API_CHANGELOG.md
````markdown
 1: # API Changelog
 2: 
 3: All notable changes to the Explore API are documented in this file.
 4: 
 5: The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/).
 6: 
 7: ---
 8: 
 9: ## [1.0.0] - 2026-02-18
10: 
11: ### Added
12: 
13: #### Security
14: - **Security headers** on all responses: `X-Content-Type-Options`, `X-Frame-Options`, `Referrer-Policy`, `Permissions-Policy`, `Content-Security-Policy`
15: - **Tiered rate limiting** with `Retry-After` and `X-RateLimit-*` response headers:
16:   - Global: 200 requests/IP (token bucket, configurable)
17:   - Authenticated: 200 requests/min/user (sliding window)
18:   - Write operations: 30 requests/min/user (fixed window)
19: - **Hardened CORS policies** with configurable origin allowlists (replaced `AllowAnyOrigin`)
20: 
21: #### API Versioning
22: - **Media type versioning** via `Accept` header: `application/json;v=1.0`
23: - Default version 1.0 assumed when no version specified
24: - All controllers annotated with `[ApiVersion("1.0")]`
25: 
26: #### Performance
27: - **ETag / conditional requests** on all GET endpoints returning JSON
28:   - Responses include `ETag` header (weak validator, SHA256 body hash)
29:   - Send `If-None-Match` header to receive `304 Not Modified` when content unchanged
30: - **Request timeouts** per endpoint category:
31:   - Default: 30 seconds
32:   - Lookup endpoints: 10 seconds
33:   - Complex operations: 60 seconds
34: 
35: #### Observability
36: - **Correlation ID propagation** via `X-Correlation-ID` / `X-Request-ID` headers
37:   - Send a correlation ID in the request; it will be echoed in the response
38:   - If no correlation ID is sent, one is auto-generated
39: - **Structured request logging** with method, path, status, duration, user, and tenant
40: - **Business metrics** via OpenTelemetry: `events.created`, `registrations.created`, `organizations.created`, `authorization.decisions`
41: 
42: ### Usage
43: 
44: #### Media Type Versioning
45: ```http
46: GET /api/event HTTP/1.1
47: Accept: application/json;v=1.0
48: ```
49: 
50: When no version is specified, the API defaults to version 1.0.
51: 
52: #### Conditional Requests (ETag)
53: ```http
54: GET /api/category HTTP/1.1
55: 
56: HTTP/1.1 200 OK
57: ETag: W/"abc123..."
58: 
59: GET /api/category HTTP/1.1
60: If-None-Match: W/"abc123..."
61: 
62: HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
63: ```
64: 
65: #### Correlation ID
66: ```http
67: GET /api/event HTTP/1.1
68: X-Correlation-ID: my-trace-id-123
69: 
70: HTTP/1.1 200 OK
71: X-Correlation-ID: my-trace-id-123
72: ```
73: 
74: ---
75: 
76: ## [0.1.0] - 2025-01-01
77: 
78: ### Initial Release
79: - REST API with Clean Architecture + CQRS (MediatR)
80: - HATEOAS/HAL+JSON with RFC 7240 `Prefer: return=minimal` support
81: - Keycloak JWT authentication with BFF pattern
82: - Cerbos authorization with fallback provider
83: - OutputCache (Lookup 1h, List 30s, Detail 60s) + HybridCache (L1+L2)
84: - Response compression (Brotli + Gzip)
85: - OpenTelemetry traces, metrics, and logs
86: - RFC 7807 ProblemDetails error responses
87: - Offset-based pagination with HATEOAS navigation links
88: - Graceful shutdown with 25-second SIGTERM grace period
````

## File: docs/CODEBASE_INSIGHTS.md
````markdown
  1: # Codebase Insights
  2: 
  3: > Non-intuitive patterns, hidden knowledge, and things requiring deep analysis.
  4: > This document captures what you cannot guess from reading ARCHITECTURE.md alone.
  5: > Last Updated: February 2026
  6: 
  7: ---
  8: 
  9: ## 1. Multi-Tenancy Deep Mechanics
 10: 
 11: ### How Tenant Isolation Actually Works
 12: 
 13: Multi-tenancy is **not middleware-based** — it uses EF Core global query filters injected via the DbContext. The flow:
 14: 
 15: 1. **TenantContext** (API service) resolves the tenant from the HTTP request
 16: 2. **ExploreDbContext** receives TenantContext via **property injection** (not constructor injection) because the DbContext uses pooling
 17: 3. **Named query filters** on every tenant-scoped entity automatically filter by `TenantId`
 18: 4. The filter expression is: `TenantContext == null || e.TenantId == TenantContext.TenantId` — the null check allows migrations and seeding to bypass tenant filtering
 19: 
 20: ### Tenant Resolution Priority
 21: 
 22: TenantContext resolves the tenant in this order:
 23: 1. `X-Tenant-Id` HTTP header (explicit selection)
 24: 2. Custom domain lookup (checks `TenantSetting` for matching domain)
 25: 3. Subdomain extraction (extracts from host, looks up tenant by subdomain or slug)
 26: 4. Default tenant (from configuration or hardcoded fallback)
 27: 
 28: ### Runtime vs Static Deployment Mode
 29: 
 30: The system checks deployment mode (SingleTenant/MultiTenant) **at runtime from the database** (`SystemSettings` table), not just from `appsettings.json`. This means a running instance can be switched between modes without redeployment. The static config is only a fallback when the DB is unreachable.
 31: 
 32: ### Not All Entities Are Tenant-Scoped
 33: 
 34: - **Tenant-scoped** (implement `ITenantEntity`): Event, Organization, Actor, Location, StorageObject, Category, Tag, and their junction tables
 35: - **Global** (no tenant filter): User, lookup tables (EventType, Language, etc.), SystemSetting, ModuleDefinition, InstanceAdministrator
 36: - **Soft-delete only** (no tenant, has `ISoftDeletable`): User
 37: 
 38: ### The TenantSetting vs TenantSettings Distinction
 39: 
 40: There are **two different entities** for tenant settings:
 41: - `TenantSetting` — Individual key-value pairs per tenant (governance overrides, used by `SettingsResolver`)
 42: - `TenantSettings` — A snapshot entity with explicit properties per tenant (display name, theme, etc.)
 43: 
 44: The DbSet names reflect this: `TenantSettingOverrides` for `TenantSetting`, `TenantSettings` for `TenantSettings`.
 45: 
 46: ---
 47: 
 48: ## 2. DbContext Pooling and Property Injection
 49: 
 50: The `ExploreDbContext` uses **pooled DbContext factory** for performance. This has a critical implication:
 51: 
 52: - The constructor **cannot** accept scoped services (TenantContext, CurrentUserService)
 53: - Instead, these are set via **property injection** after the context is created from the pool
 54: - The scoped registration in `PersistenceServicesRegistration.cs` creates the context from the factory, then sets the properties
 55: 
 56: This means:
 57: - `TenantContext` and `CurrentUserService` can be `null` (during migrations, seeding, or background services)
 58: - All query filters and audit logic must handle null gracefully
 59: - If you add a new scoped dependency to DbContext, it must follow this property injection pattern
 60: 
 61: ---
 62: 
 63: ## 3. Soft Delete Interception in SaveChanges
 64: 
 65: When you call `Delete()` on an entity that implements `ISoftDeletable`, the `GenericRepository` sets `EntityState.Deleted`. But the entity is **never actually deleted** from the database. Here's what happens:
 66: 
 67: 1. `GenericRepository.Delete()` marks entity as `EntityState.Deleted`
 68: 2. `ExploreDbContext.SaveChangesAsync()` intercepts the Deleted state
 69: 3. Changes it to `EntityState.Modified` instead
 70: 4. Sets `IsDeleted = true`, `DeletedAt = now`, `DeletedBy = userId`
 71: 5. Also updates `UpdatedAt`/`UpdatedBy` if entity is `IAuditableEntity`
 72: 
 73: For entities that don't implement `ISoftDeletable`, `Delete()` performs a real hard delete.
 74: 
 75: `HardDelete()` method exists for admin operations that need permanent removal regardless of `ISoftDeletable`.
 76: 
 77: ---
 78: 
 79: ## 4. Named Query Filters (EF Core 10+)
 80: 
 81: This project uses EF Core 10's **named query filters** feature. Each entity can have multiple independently-controllable filters:
 82: 
 83: - `QueryFilterNames.Tenant` — Tenant isolation filter
 84: - `QueryFilterNames.SoftDelete` — Soft delete filter
 85: 
 86: You can selectively disable one without the other:
 87: - `IgnoreQueryFilter("SoftDelete")` — Shows deleted records but still respects tenant isolation
 88: - `IgnoreQueryFilter("Tenant")` — Cross-tenant query (admin operations) but still hides deleted records
 89: - `IgnoreQueryFilters()` — Disables ALL filters (dangerous — cross-tenant + deleted)
 90: 
 91: Not all entities have both filters. Check `ExploreDbContext.ApplyGlobalQueryFilters()` for the exact mapping.
 92: 
 93: ---
 94: 
 95: ## 5. Blazor Server + WASM Hybrid Architecture
 96: 
 97: ### The Two-Project Structure
 98: 
 99: - `Explore.Blazor` — Blazor Server host. Handles SSR, OIDC authentication, serves the WASM app, and acts as a BFF proxy
100: - `Explore.Blazor.Client` — Blazor WebAssembly. Contains all interactive UI components, pages, and services
101: 
102: ### How Authentication Flows
103: 
104: 1. User accesses the Blazor Server host
105: 2. OIDC challenge redirects to Keycloak for login
106: 3. After login, the server stores tokens in a `CircuitAccessTokenService` (per-circuit lifetime)
107: 4. For WASM: Authentication state is serialized to the client using `AddAuthenticationStateDeserialization()`
108: 5. WASM makes API calls through the same origin (BFF pattern)
109: 6. `BrowserCredentialsMessageHandler` adds cookies to all WASM HttpClient requests
110: 7. `BffUnauthorizedHandler` intercepts 401 responses and triggers server-side re-login
111: 
112: ### The BFF Pattern
113: 
114: The Blazor Server host proxies API requests. WASM never calls the API directly — it goes through the BFF:
115: - WASM `HttpClient.BaseAddress` = same origin as Blazor Server
116: - Blazor Server proxies `/api/*` requests to the actual API
117: - Cookies (including auth tokens) travel automatically
118: 
119: ### S3 Image Upload Exception
120: 
121: Image uploads bypass the BFF. They go directly to S3-compatible storage (Hetzner) using presigned URLs:
122: - `ImageStorageService` gets a presigned URL from the API
123: - `S3UploadMessageHandler` configures CORS mode for cross-origin PUT
124: - Direct browser-to-S3 upload avoids server bottleneck
125: 
126: ---
127: 
128: ## 6. Module Governance System
129: 
130: ### What Modules Are
131: 
132: The system supports pluggable modules that add domain-specific behavior:
133: - **Core** — Always enabled. Basic event functionality
134: - **Islamic** — Madhab selection, prayer times, gender segregation awareness
135: - **Tech** — GitHub repositories, skill levels, live coding flags
136: 
137: ### How Modules Work
138: 
139: 1. `ModuleDefinition` table defines available modules (seeded)
140: 2. `TenantCapability` maps which modules each tenant has enabled
141: 3. `IModuleService` checks if a module is enabled for the current tenant
142: 4. `EventIslamicAspect` / `EventTechAspect` — Optional 1:1 extension tables that store module-specific fields
143: 5. `IEventStrategy` / `StrategyResolver` — Module-specific behavior dispatched at runtime via strategy pattern
144: 
145: ### The Strategy Pattern
146: 
147: When creating/updating events, the `StrategyResolver` picks the right strategy based on enabled modules:
148: - `IslamicEventStrategy` — Handles Islamic-specific validation and field population
149: - `TechEventStrategy` — Handles tech-specific validation and field population
150: 
151: ---
152: 
153: ## 7. Lookup Table Dual-Track System
154: 
155: Lookup tables are managed in **two synchronized places**:
156: 
157: ### Track 1: Domain Enums
158: `Explore.Domain/Enums/{EntityName}Enum.cs` — Defines the int IDs and names. Used in code for type-safe references.
159: 
160: ### Track 2: EF Core HasData Seeding
161: `Explore.Persistence/Configurations/Entities/{EntityName}Configuration.cs` — Uses `HasData()` to seed the database with matching values.
162: 
163: ### The Synchronization Rule
164: 
165: The enum values and HasData seed values **must always match**. If you add a new enum value, you must also add a matching `HasData()` entry. The `LookupTableSeeder` class helps ensure runtime synchronization.
166: 
167: ### Which ID Type for What
168: 
169: - **Lookup tables** use `int` PK (EventType, Language, etc.)
170: - **Main entities** use `Guid` PK (Event, Organization, etc.)
171: - **Link tables** use composite keys (EventId + CategoryId, etc.)
172: - Never use `long` except for file sizes or pagination cursors
173: 
174: ---
175: 
176: ## 8. Seed Data Architecture
177: 
178: ### Two Seeding Mechanisms
179: 
180: 1. **EF Configuration HasData()** — Lookup tables are seeded via entity configurations. This creates migration-tracked seed data. Used for: EventType, EventStatus, EventFormat, AudienceAge, etc.
181: 
182: 2. **Runtime DatabaseSeeder** — Called at startup via `DatabaseSeeder.cs`. Seeds main entities (Tenant, User, Organization, Actor, StorageObject, Event). Uses `SeedIds.cs` for deterministic GUIDs.
183: 
184: ### SeedIds and UUIDv7
185: 
186: All seed GUIDs use **UUIDv7** format (`018e4e5c-xxxx-7xxx-8xxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx`) for:
187: - Time-ordered insertion (better index performance)
188: - Deterministic values (same GUIDs every run, prevents duplicates)
189: - Range-separated by entity type (different `xxxx` ranges for tenants vs users vs organizations)
190: 
191: **Critical rule:** Never change seed IDs after they've been used in production migrations.
192: 
193: ---
194: 
195: ## 9. HATEOAS Implementation
196: 
197: The API implements **HAL (Hypertext Application Language)** for hypermedia:
198: 
199: - `HalResource<T>` wraps response DTOs with `_links` section
200: - `HalCollectionResource<T>` wraps lists with pagination links
201: - `ResourceAssemblerBase<T>` generates links per entity type
202: - `HateoasLinkGenerator` resolves URLs from route names
203: - OpenAPI schema is transformed by `HalSchemaTransformer` to show HAL structure
204: 
205: The `PreferHeaderMiddleware` handles content negotiation: clients can request HAL format via `Prefer: return=representation` header.
206: 
207: ---
208: 
209: ## 10. The Actors System (Federation/ATProto)
210: 
211: ### What Actors Are
212: 
213: `Actor` is the federation identity concept from ATProto/ActivityPub:
214: - Every user gets a personal Actor
215: - Every organization gets an Actor
216: - Actors have DIDs (Decentralized Identifiers), key pairs, and can federate
217: 
218: ### Actor ↔ User/Organization Relationship
219: 
220: - An `Actor` has an `ActorType` (Personal, Organization, Bot, Service)
221: - A `User` owns one or more Actors
222: - An `Organization` is linked to exactly one Actor
223: - `ActorKeyStore` stores signing keys for federated operations
224: - `DidCustodyType` tracks who controls the DID (self, server, external)
225: 
226: ### Federation Sync
227: 
228: - `PdsSyncOutbox` — Outbox pattern for syncing changes to ATProto PDS
229: - `PdsSyncWorker` — Background service that processes the outbox
230: - `IndexedDid` / `SyncState` / `AtprotoRecord` — Firehose indexer state
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## 11. Settings Resolution Chain
235: 
236: The governance settings system has a three-tier resolution:
237: 
238: 1. **SystemSetting** (instance-wide defaults) — e.g., "require event approval = true"
239: 2. **TenantSetting** (per-tenant overrides) — e.g., Tenant A overrides to "false"
240: 3. **PlatformDefaults** (code-level fallback) — if neither DB value exists
241: 
242: `SettingsResolver` implements this cascade. Settings values are stored as **JSON-serialized strings** in the database. The `TenantContext.cs` file shows the deserialization pattern: `JsonSerializer.Deserialize<T>(rawValue)` with fallback to raw parsing.
243: 
244: ### GovernanceSettingKeys
245: 
246: Setting keys are string constants in `GovernanceSettingKeys.cs`. They use dot-separated hierarchical naming:
247: - `Deployment.Mode`
248: - `Events.MaxSessionsPerEvent`
249: - `Modules.Islamic.Enabled`
250: - `Domains.InstanceBaseDomain`
251: - `Domains.AllowTenantCustomDomain`
252: 
253: ---
254: 
255: ## 12. AutoMapper Profile Organization
256: 
257: All mappings live in a **single file**: `Explore.Application/Profiles/MappingProfile.cs`. This file maps every entity to every DTO. When adding a new entity/DTO pair, the mapping goes here — not in a separate profile file.
258: 
259: ---
260: 
261: ## 13. API Client Generation
262: 
263: The Blazor client uses an **NSwag-generated API client**:
264: 
265: - `EventApiClient.cs` — Hand-written interface (`IEventApiClient`) with additional methods
266: - `EventApiClient.g.cs` — Auto-generated code from `swagger.json`
267: - The generated client is registered in WASM `Program.cs` with the BFF HttpClient
268: 
269: To regenerate: update `swagger.json` from the API, then run the NSwag generator.
270: 
271: ---
272: 
273: ## 14. Exception Handling Flow
274: 
275: ### API Side
276: `ExceptionMiddleware` catches all unhandled exceptions and maps them to HTTP responses:
277: - `NotFoundException` → 404
278: - `BadRequestException` → 400
279: - `ValidationException` → 400 with error details
280: - Unhandled → 500
281: 
282: ### Command Response Pattern
283: Commands don't throw for validation failures. They return `BaseCommandResponse<TKey>`:
284: - `Success = true/false`
285: - `Errors` list with validation messages
286: - Controllers return `Ok(response)` or `BadRequest(response)` based on `Success`
287: 
288: ### Client Side
289: `ServiceResult<T>` wraps API responses in the Blazor client, providing a consistent error handling pattern.
290: 
291: ---
292: 
293: ## 15. BlockInSingleTenant Filter
294: 
295: The `BlockInSingleTenantAttribute` action filter prevents certain endpoints from being called in single-tenant mode. This is used for multi-tenant management endpoints that don't make sense in single-tenant deployments.
296: 
297: ---
298: 
299: ## 16. DI Registration Locations
300: 
301: Services are registered in multiple places — knowing where to add yours is critical:
302: 
303: | What | Where | Method |
304: |---|---|---|
305: | Repositories | `Explore.Persistence/PersistenceServicesRegistration.cs` | `CongfigurePersistenceServices()` |
306: | Infrastructure services | `Explore.Infrastructure/InfrastructureServicesRegistration.cs` | `ConfigureInfrastructureServices()` |
307: | API-layer services | `Explore.API/Program.cs` | Direct registration |
308: | MediatR handlers | Auto-registered via `AddMediatR()` in `Program.cs` | Assembly scanning |
309: | AutoMapper profiles | Auto-registered via `AddAutoMapper()` | Assembly scanning |
310: | Blazor WASM services | `Explore.Blazor.Client/Program.cs` | Direct registration |
311: | Blazor Server services | `Explore.Blazor/Program.cs` | Direct registration |
312: | Secrets | `Explore.Secrets/Extensions/ServiceCollectionExtensions.cs` | `AddSecrets()` |
313: 
314: **Note:** There is a typo in `CongfigurePersistenceServices` (missing `i` in "Configure"). This is existing and intentional — do not rename it without updating all call sites.
315: 
316: ---
317: 
318: ## 17. Aspire Integration
319: 
320: The project uses **.NET Aspire** for local development orchestration:
321: 
322: - `Explore.AppHost` — Defines the service topology (API + Blazor + PostgreSQL + dependencies)
323: - `Explore.ServiceDefaults` — Shared configuration (OpenTelemetry, health checks, resilience)
324: - Database connection is configured via Aspire's `AddNpgsqlDbContext` in the API project, while `PersistenceServicesRegistration` uses `AddPooledDbContextFactory` for production
325: 
326: The Aspire integration is intentionally **not** in the Persistence project to avoid an ASP.NET Core dependency in the persistence layer.
327: 
328: ---
329: 
330: ## 18. Migration Service
331: 
332: `Event.MigrationService` is a **worker service** that applies EF Core migrations at startup:
333: - Runs as a separate process in the Aspire topology
334: - Applies pending migrations to the database
335: - Calls `DatabaseSeeder` to ensure seed data exists
336: - Exits after completion
337: 
338: This decouples migration execution from the API startup, allowing the API to assume the database is ready.
339: 
340: ---
341: 
342: ## 19. Image Storage Flow
343: 
344: Images are stored in **S3-compatible object storage** (Hetzner):
345: 
346: 1. Client requests a presigned upload URL from the API (`StorageObjectController`)
347: 2. API generates presigned URL via `ObjectStorageService` and creates a `StorageObject` record
348: 3. Client uploads directly to S3 using the presigned URL (bypasses BFF)
349: 4. `S3Image.razor` component renders images using the S3 URL
350: 5. `StorageObject` entity tracks: bucket, key, content type, size, and owner (via `OwnerType`)
351: 
352: ---
353: 
354: ## 20. Organization Review System
355: 
356: Organization reviews use a slightly different CQRS structure:
357: 
358: - `OrganizationReviews/Commands/` and `OrganizationReviews/Queries/` (flattened, no `Handlers/Requests` split)
359: - This is the only feature that uses this alternative structure — all others use the standard nested pattern
360: 
361: ---
362: 
363: ## 21. ABOUTME File Comments
364: 
365: Every file should start with a two-line comment:
366: ```
367: // ABOUTME: Brief description of what this file does.
368: // ABOUTME: Second line with additional context.
369: ```
370: 
371: Not all files have this yet, but it's the convention. Add it when modifying a file.
372: 
373: ---
374: 
375: ## 22. Client-Side Lookup Caching
376: 
377: `LookupCacheService` caches lookup table data (EventTypes, AudienceAges, Languages, etc.) in the WASM client to avoid repeated API calls. When adding a new lookup table:
378: 
379: 1. Add the API call to the relevant service
380: 2. Add caching in `LookupCacheService`
381: 3. Use the cached version in page components
382: 
383: ---
384: 
385: ## 23. Route Guards (Blazouter)
386: 
387: The Blazor client uses **Blazouter** library for client-side routing with guards:
388: 
389: - `AuthenticatedRouteGuard` — Requires authentication
390: - `AdminRouteGuard` — Requires admin role
391: 
392: Guards are registered in `Program.cs` and applied via Blazouter's routing configuration.
393: 
394: ---
395: 
396: ## 25. Specification Pattern Implementation
397: 
398: The application uses a custom **Specification Pattern** to handle complex filtering logic, particularly for the `Event` entity which has modular aspects.
399: 
400: ### Core Components
401: - **`IQuerySpecification<T>`**: Interface defining the contract for query specifications.
402: - **`EventQuerySpecification`**: The main specification for event retrieval. It orchestrates sub-filters.
403: - **`IFilterSpecification<T>`**: Interface for individual filter components.
404: 
405: ### Modular Filtering Strategy
406: Instead of a massive `Where()` clause in the repository, filters are broken down into small, reusable classes:
407: 
408: 1.  **`EventFilter`**: Handles core fields (Date, Location, Category).
409: 2.  **`AspectPresenceFilter`**: Handles "HasIslamicAspect" / "HasTechAspect" flags.
410: 3.  **`IslamicAspectFilter`**: Handles Islamic-specific fields (Madhab, GenderMode).
411: 4.  **`TechAspectFilter`**: Handles Tech-specific fields (SkillLevel, Stack).
412: 
413: The `EventQuerySpecification` applies these filters sequentially to the `IQueryable<Event>`. This allows module-specific filters to be applied only when relevant.
414: 
415: ---
416: 
417: ## 26. Hybrid Caching Strategy (L1 + L2)
418: 
419: We use **.NET 9+ HybridCache** for application-level caching, which provides L1 (In-Memory) + L2 (Redis) caching with built-in stampede protection.
420: 
421: ### Usage Pattern
422: HybridCache is injected into **MediatR Handlers**, not Controllers.
423: 
424: **Read-Through (Query Handlers):**
425: ```csharp
426: return await _cache.GetOrCreateAsync(
427:     key: $"event:{request.Id}",
428:     factory: async cancel => await _repo.GetById(request.Id),
429:     options: new HybridCacheEntryOptions { Expiration = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10) }
430: );
431: ```
432: 
433: **Invalidation (Command Handlers):**
434: ```csharp
435: // In Create/Update/Delete handlers
436: await _cache.RemoveAsync($"event:{request.Id}");
437: ```
438: 
439: **Key Distinction:**
440: - **OutputCache**: Caches the *HTTP response* (Controllers). Good for anonymous public lists.
441: - **HybridCache**: Caches the *Domain Entity/DTO* (Handlers). Good for shared data, authenticated views, and internal logic.
442: 
443: ---
444: 
445: ## 27. Validation Architecture
446: 
447: ### The "Manual Instantiation" Rule
448: Validators are **never** injected via DI. They are manually instantiated in the Handler.
449: 
450: **Why?**
451: Our validators often require database access (e.g., "Does this CategoryId exist?", "Is this User an Admin?"). Injecting Repositories into Validators via DI can cause lifetime issues and circular dependencies if not careful.
452: 
453: **The Pattern:**
454: ```csharp
455: public class CreateEventCommandHandler : IRequestHandler<...>
456: {
457:     public CreateEventCommandHandler(
458:         IEventRepository eventRepo,
459:         IOrganizationRepository orgRepo) // Inject repos into Handler
460:     { ... }
461: 
462:     public async Task<Response> Handle(...)
463:     {
464:         // Pass repos to Validator constructor manually
465:         var validator = new CreateEventDtoValidator(_eventRepo, _orgRepo);
466:         var result = await validator.ValidateAsync(request.Dto);
467:         // ...
468:     }
469: }
470: ```
471: 
472: This ensures the validator uses the same repository instances (and DbContext) as the handler transaction.
````

 23: 
 24: ## Executive Summary
 25: 
 26: Research into documentation best practices from leading open source projects (Kubernetes, PostgreSQL, Stripe, Twilio, Microsoft, Google) reveals consistent patterns that drive developer engagement and reduce time-to-value:
 27: 
 28: ### Key Findings
 29: 
 30: 1. **Structure Matters**: The Diátaxis framework (tutorials, how-to guides, reference, explanations) is widely adopted
 31: 2. **Interactivity Drives Engagement**: Code playgrounds, interactive API consoles, and live examples significantly improve comprehension
 32: 3. **Consistency is Critical**: Style guides, terminology standards, and formatting rules prevent cognitive overhead
 33: 4. **Multi-Modal Learning**: Diagrams, code examples in multiple languages, and visual aids accelerate understanding
 34: 5. **Maintenance is Ongoing**: Documentation requires continuous updates, clear changelogs, and dedicated ownership
 35: 
 36: ---
 37: 
 38: ## Industry Best Practices
 39: 
 40: ### 1. The Diátaxis Framework
 41: 
 42: **Source**: Widely adopted by Django, Divio, and numerous high-quality OSS projects
 43: 
 44: The Diátaxis framework organizes documentation into four distinct categories based on user needs:
 45: 
 46: | Category | Purpose | When to Use | Example |
 47: |----------|---------|-------------|---------|
 48: | **Tutorials** | Learning-oriented | User wants to get started | "Build Your First Event Platform in 15 Minutes" |
 49: | **How-To Guides** | Task-oriented | User has a specific problem to solve | "How to Configure Multi-Tenancy" |
 50: | **Reference** | Information-oriented | User needs to look up specific details | "API Endpoint Reference", "Configuration Options" |
 51: | **Explanation** | Understanding-oriented | User wants to understand concepts | "Understanding the BFF Pattern", "Multi-Tenancy Architecture" |
 52: 
 53: **Key Principle**: Each document should fit into ONE category. Mixing categories creates confusion.
 54: 
 55: **Current ISLAMU Status**: 
 56: - ✅ Good reference documentation (API.md, DOMAIN.md)
 57: - ✅ Good explanations (ARCHITECTURE.md, MULTI_TENANCY.md)
 58: - ⚠️ Limited tutorials (need more "Getting Started" guides)
 59: - ⚠️ Limited how-to guides (need more task-specific documentation)

 61: ---

 63: ### 2. Interactive Documentation
 64: 
 65: **Leading Examples**: Stripe, Twilio, Postman, GitHub API Explorer
 66: 
 67: **Key Features**:
 68: - **Live API Console**: Execute API calls directly in documentation
 69: - **Code Playgrounds**: Interactive code examples with instant feedback
 70: - **Request/Response Examples**: Real-time examples in multiple languages
 71: - **Try-It-Now Buttons**: Immediate experimentation without setup
 72: 
 73: **Benefits**:
 74: - Reduces barrier to entry
 75: - Validates understanding in real-time
 76: - Builds confidence before production use

 79: **Recommendation for ISLAMU**:

 85: 
 86: ### 3. Style Guide and Consistency
 87: 
 88: **Leading Examples**: Google Developer Documentation Style Guide, Microsoft Writing Style Guide

 90: **Critical Elements**:
 91: 
 92: 1. **Terminology Standards**
 93:    - Define domain-specific terms once, use consistently
 94:    - Example: "Event" vs "Event Instance" vs "Occurrence" - pick ONE
 95:    - Avoid synonyms that create confusion
 96: 
 97: 2. **Voice and Tone**
 98:    - **Active Voice**: "Configure the tenant" (not "The tenant can be configured")
 99:    - **Second Person**: "You can create events" (not "Users can create events")
100:    - **Present Tense**: "The API returns a response" (not "The API will return")
101: 
102: 3. **Formatting Conventions**
103:    - Code: `inline code`, ```code blocks```
104:    - UI Elements: **Bold** (e.g., "Click **Save**")
105:    - File Paths: `C:\path\to\file`
106:    - Environment Variables: `ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT`

369: 
370: ## Technical Writing Principles
371: 
372: ### The 5 C's of Technical Writing
373: 
374: 1. **Clear**: Unambiguous language, simple sentences
375: 2. **Concise**: No unnecessary words, get to the point
376: 3. **Consistent**: Same terms, same style throughout
377: 4. **Complete**: All necessary information provided
378: 5. **Correct**: Technically accurate, tested examples
379: 
380: ### Writing Style Guidelines
381: 
382: **Do**:
383: - Use active voice: "Configure the tenant" vs "The tenant is configured"
384: - Write in present tense: "The API returns" vs "The API will return"
385: - Use second person: "You can create" vs "Users can create"
386: - Be specific: "Set timeout to 30 seconds" vs "Set reasonable timeout"
387: - Provide context: Explain WHY before HOW
388: 
389: **Don't**:
390: - Use jargon without explanation
391: - Assume prior knowledge
392: - Mix conceptual and procedural content
393: - Write long paragraphs (break into bullets/sections)
394: - Forget to proofread and test examples
395: 
396: ### Accessibility Considerations
397: 
398: - **Screen readers**: Use semantic HTML, alt text for images
399: - **Color contrast**: Ensure sufficient contrast ratios
400: - **Code blocks**: Provide syntax highlighting for readability
401: - **Navigation**: Logical heading hierarchy (H1 > H2 > H3)
402: - **Links**: Descriptive link text (not "click here")
403: 
404: ---

## File: docs/MULTI_TENANCY.md
````markdown
  1: # Multi-Tenancy Architecture
  2: 
  3: > **Conceptual Guide for Multi-Tenant System Design**
  4: >
  5: > This document describes the multi-tenancy model, authority hierarchy, and data isolation patterns.
  6: > For implementation details and code patterns, see the relevant skills in `.claude/skills/`.
  7: 
  8: **Last Updated**: January 2026
  9: 
 10: ---
 11: 
 12: ## Overview
 13: 
 14: The platform operates as a **multi-tenant system** where multiple independent organizations (tenants) share the same application infrastructure while maintaining complete data isolation. The architecture supports both dedicated single-tenant deployments and shared multi-tenant SaaS models.
 15: 
 16: ---
 17: 
 18: ## Hierarchy of Authority
 19: 
 20: ### Two-Tier Administration Model
 21: 
 22: The system distinguishes between two fundamentally different administrative roles:
 23: 
 24: | Tier | Role | Scope | Typical Use Case |
 25: |------|------|-------|------------------|
 26: | **Tier 1** | Instance Administrator | Infrastructure, global policies, module enablement | SaaS provider, IT department |
 27: | **Tier 2** | Tenant Administrator | Community data, local configuration, user management | Organization leader, community admin |
 28: 
 29: ### Instance Administrator (Super Admin)
 30: 
 31: **Responsibilities:**
 32: - Physical server and infrastructure management
 33: - Global resource limits and quotas
 34: - Module enablement/disablement at platform level
 35: - Enforcement policies that cannot be overridden
 36: - Tenant provisioning and lifecycle management
 37: - System-wide security policies
 38: 
 39: **Cannot Do:**
 40: - Access tenant-specific business data
 41: - Make decisions on behalf of tenants
 42: - Override tenant preferences within allowed bounds
 43: 
 44: ### Tenant Administrator (Customer)
 45: 
 46: **Responsibilities:**
 47: - Community-specific configuration
 48: - User management within their tenant
 49: - Branding and customization
 50: - Local business rules and workflows
 51: - Content moderation policies
 52: 
 53: **Constrained By:**
 54: - Instance-level enforcement policies
 55: - Module availability set by Instance Admin
 56: - Resource quotas and limits
 57: 
 58: ---
 59: 
 60: ## Cascading Configuration Engine
 61: 
 62: ### Resolution Strategy
 63: 
 64: Settings are resolved at runtime using a **fall-through strategy**:
 65: 
 66: 1. **Check Tenant Override** → Does the tenant have a specific value?
 67: 2. **Check Instance Enforcement** → Is this setting locked by the Instance Admin?
 68: 3. **Fall to Default** → Use the system default value
 69: 
 70: ### Setting Types
 71: 
 72: | Type | Behavior | Example |
 73: |------|----------|---------|
 74: | **Locked** | Tenant cannot override | Security policies, payment provider |
 75: | **Delegated** | Tenant may customize | Theme colors, notification preferences |
 76: | **Default-Only** | System default, no UI exposed | Internal technical settings |
 77: 
 78: ### Enforcement Scenarios
 79: 
 80: **Scenario: Render Mode Control**
 81: - Instance Admin sets `RenderMode = Auto` with `IsLocked = false`
 82: - Tenant Admin sees a dropdown and can change to `Server` or `WebAssembly`
 83: - If Instance Admin sets `IsLocked = true`, dropdown is disabled/hidden
 84: 
 85: **Scenario: Module Restriction**
 86: - Instance Admin configures `AllowedModules = ["Core", "Islamic"]`
 87: - Tenant Admin cannot enable "Tech" module even if code exists
 88: - Tenant only sees modules within their allowed set
 89: 
 90: ---
 91: 
 92: ## Data Isolation
 93: 
 94: ### Tenant Boundary Enforcement
 95: 
 96: Every tenant-scoped entity implements `ITenantEntity`:
 97: - Contains `TenantId` property
 98: - Automatically filtered in all queries via global query filters
 99: - Cannot be accidentally accessed across tenant boundaries
100: 
101: ### Isolation Guarantees
102: 
103: | Layer | Mechanism |
104: |-------|-----------|
105: | **Database** | Global query filters on `TenantId` |
106: | **Application** | Tenant context injected per-request |
107: | **API** | Middleware validates tenant claims |
108: | **UI** | Routes scoped to tenant context |
109: 
110: ### Cross-Tenant Operations
111: 
112: Cross-tenant operations are **explicitly forbidden** except:
113: - Instance Admin reporting and analytics
114: - System-wide notifications (opt-in)
115: - Federation sync (ATProto/ActivityPub)
116: 
117: ---
118: 
119: ## Tenant Lifecycle
120: 
121: ### Provisioning Flow
122: 
123: 1. **Request** → Tenant Admin requests new tenant (or Instance Admin creates)
124: 2. **Validation** → Check quotas, naming conflicts, policy compliance
125: 3. **Creation** → Database schema initialized with tenant seed data
126: 4. **Configuration** → Module selection, initial settings
127: 5. **Activation** → Tenant becomes operational
128: 
129: ### Tenant States
130: 
131: | State | Description | Operations Allowed |
132: |-------|-------------|-------------------|
133: | **Pending** | Created but not activated | Configuration only |
134: | **Active** | Fully operational | All operations |
135: | **Suspended** | Temporarily disabled | Read-only access |
136: | **Archived** | Soft-deleted | None (data retained) |
137: | **Purged** | Permanently deleted | None (data removed) |
138: 
139: ---
140: 
141: ## Single-Tenant vs Multi-Tenant Deployment
142: 
143: ### Virtual Tenant Strategy
144: 
145: The codebase is **always multi-tenant internally** to avoid maintaining separate codebases. Single-tenant mode is achieved through a "Virtual Tenant" that masks the complexity.
146: 
147: | Mode | Behavior |
148: |------|----------|
149: | **Single-Tenant** | `TenantId` hardcoded to `Default`; tenant management UI hidden |
150: | **Multi-Tenant** | `TenantId` resolved from subdomain/header; full tenant management |
151: 
152: ### Runtime Mode Switching
153: 
154: The deployment mode can be changed at runtime without application restart:
155: 1. Instance Admin toggles setting in dashboard
156: 2. Database updated, cache invalidated
157: 3. Next request uses new mode
158: 4. UI adapts automatically (tenant menu appears/disappears)
159: 
160: ---
161: 
162: ## Onboarding Patterns
163: 
164: ### Instance Admin First-Run
165: 
166: When the platform is first installed:
167: 1. First user becomes Instance Admin
168: 2. Wizard asks deployment purpose (Dedicated vs. SaaS)
169: 3. Module selection for the instance
170: 4. Default tenant configuration
171: 
172: ### Tenant Registration Policies
173: 
174: | Policy | Description |
175: |--------|-------------|
176: | **Open** | Self-service registration via public form |
177: | **Invite-Only** | Instance Admin sends invitation link |
178: | **Sales-Gated** | Request must be approved by sales team |
179: | **Closed** | No new tenants (maintenance mode) |
180: 
181: ---
182: 
183: ## Tenant Branding & Customization
184: 
185: ### Navigation Customization
186: 
187: Tenants can define custom external navigation links to seamlessly integrate the event platform with their main website.
188: 
189: - **Entity**: `TenantNavigationLink`
190: - **Management**: Tenant Admins via Admin Portal (`/admin/tenant/navigation`)
191: - **Features**:
192:   - Custom Label and URL
193:   - Ordering support
194:   - "Open in New Tab" option
195:   - Icon selection (MudBlazor icons)
196: 
197: These links are rendered dynamically in the main application sidebar, appearing below standard navigation items. This reduces friction for end-users by providing easy access back to the organization's main site.
198: 
199: ---
200: 
201: ## Related Documentation
202: 
203: - **[ADMIN_HIERARCHY.md](ADMIN_HIERARCHY.md)** - Detailed authority model
204: - **[DEPLOYMENT_MODES.md](DEPLOYMENT_MODES.md)** - Single vs multi-tenant deployment
205: - **[EXTENSIBILITY.md](EXTENSIBILITY.md)** - Module and aspect architecture
206: - **[ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md)** - Overall system architecture
207: 
208: ## Implementation Reference
209: 
210: For code patterns and implementation details:
211: - **`dotnet-efcore-guidelines`** skill - Tenant query filters
212: - **`auth-patterns`** skill - Tenant context extraction
213: - **`clean-architecture-rules`** skill - Layer boundaries
````

## File: docs/semantic_versioning/v0.1.0.md
````markdown
  1: # v0.1.0 - First Public Release (Beta)
  2: **Released:** TBD
  3: 
  4: ## Summary
  5: The first publicly-available release of the **ISLAMU Event Platform** — a multi-tenant, federated event discovery system built with .NET 10, Clean Architecture, and enterprise-grade security. This version represents the **MVP baseline** ready for beta testing and early adopter feedback, featuring complete event management, organization workflows, advanced filtering with modular aspects, HATEOAS REST API, and a full Blazor frontend.
  6: 
  7: **⚠️ Pre-1.0 Notice**: Major version zero (0.y.z) indicates initial development. The public API may change at any time and should not be considered stable. This release is intended for beta testing, early adopters, and feedback gathering.
  8: 
  9: ---
 10: 
 11: ## 🎯 Platform Overview
 12: 
 13: ### What is ISLAMU Event?
 14: A **culturally-aware event discovery platform** designed for Muslim communities and tech meetups, enabling:
 15: - **Event discovery** with advanced filtering (age, gender, madhab, skill level, location, language)
 16: - **Two-tier verification system** (user-submitted vs. verified organizations)
 17: - **Multi-tenant SaaS** architecture (single-tenant and multi-tenant deployment modes)
 18: - **Modular event types** (Islamic events module, Tech events module) with per-tenant enablement
 19: - **Federation readiness** (ATProto/ActivityPub data models — Phase 1 complete, protocol endpoints planned)
 20: 
 21: ### Technology Stack
 22: - **Runtime**: .NET 10.0
 23: - **Architecture**: Clean Architecture + CQRS (MediatR)
 24: - **Frontend**: Blazor Server + WebAssembly (InteractiveAuto hybrid rendering)
 25: - **UI Components**: MudBlazor (Material Design)
 26: - **Database**: PostgreSQL + PostGIS (spatial queries)
 27: - **Authentication**: Keycloak (OIDC/OAuth 2.0) with Backend-for-Frontend (BFF) pattern
 28: - **Authorization**: Cerbos (Policy Decision Point) + ASP.NET Core
 29: - **Secrets Management**: Infisical (with environment variable fallback)
 30: - **API Documentation**: Scalar + Swagger/NSwag
 31: - **Observability**: Serilog + OpenTelemetry (Prometheus + Loki + Grafana)
 32: - **Orchestration**: .NET Aspire (development), Docker (production)
 33: 
 34: ---
 35: 
 36: ## 🚀 Core Features
 37: 
 38: ### 1. Event Management System
 39: **Complete event lifecycle management with advanced capabilities:**
 40: 
 41: - **Event Creation & Editing**: Rich event forms with title, subtitle, description, type, format, status, pricing
 42: - **Event Sessions**: Multiple sessions per event with date/time, location, speakers, agenda items
 43: - **Event Registration**: RSVP system with approval workflow, registration limits, waitlist support
 44: - **Event Discovery**: Public event listing with search, filtering, sorting, and pagination
 45: - **Event Types**: Workshop, Lecture, Social, Conference, Seminar, Training, Networking, Fundraiser, Hackathon
 46: - **Event Formats**: In-Person, Online, Hybrid
 47: - **Event Status**: Draft, Published, Canceled, Archived
 48: - **Visibility Control**: Public, Private, Draft-Only
 49: - **Session Management**: Multiple sessions with speakers, languages, agenda breakdowns
 50: - **Advanced Query System**: 33 query parameters via `EventQuerySpecification` fluent builder:
 51:   - Core filters: Title search, type, format, status, date range, organization, featured flag
 52:   - Islamic aspect filters: Gender segregation mode, madhab, prayer time, audience age/gender
 53:   - Tech aspect filters: Skill level, tech stack, session format
 54:   - Subquery filters: Category IDs and Tag IDs (junction table queries)
 55:   - Sorting: Date, relevance, view count
 56: 
 57: ### 2. Organization Management
 58: **Verified organization workflows with member roles:**
 59: 
 60: - **Organization Creation**: Registration form with approval workflow (Open/Approval Required/Invite Only policies)
 61: - **Organization Profiles**: Name, description, website, logo, social links, verification status
 62: - **Member Management**: Invite members, assign roles (Owner, Admin, Editor, Viewer), update permissions
 63: - **Role-Based Access**: Fine-grained permissions per organization role
 64: - **Organization Reviews**: User ratings and reviews for verified organizations
 65: - **Organization Positions**: Job title lookup for member profiles
 66: 
 67: ### 3. Multi-Tenancy & Admin Hierarchy
 68: **Enterprise SaaS architecture with flexible deployment modes:**
 69: 
 70: - **Deployment Modes**:
 71:   - **Single-Tenant**: Multi-tenancy disabled, feels like traditional app (TenantId = Default)
 72:   - **Multi-Tenant (SaaS)**: Multiple isolated organizations, subdomain-based routing
 73: - **Tenant Management**: Isolated workspaces with custom branding, navigation links, settings
 74: - **Tenant Resolution**: Header (`X-Tenant-Id`) → JWT claim → Subdomain → Path segment → Default
 75: - **Admin Hierarchy**:
 76:   - **Instance Admins**: System-level configuration (deployment mode, modules, federation, S3, SMTP)
 77:   - **Tenant Admins**: Tenant-level settings (policies, member management, branding)
 78:   - **Organization Admins**: Organization-level operations (events, members, reviews)
 79: - **Cascading Configuration**: Instance → Tenant → Feature override hierarchy with lock/unlock mechanism
 80: - **Module Governance**: System-level gates for module availability (Islamic, Tech) across all tenants
 81: 
 82: ### 4. Modular Event Aspects
 83: **Plugin-style event extensions with per-tenant enablement:**
 84: 
 85: - **Islamic Events Module** (`EventIslamicAspect`):
 86:   - **Gender Segregation Mode**: Male-only, Female-only, Segregated, Mixed
 87:   - **Madhab Targeting**: Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, Hanbali
 88:   - **Prayer Time Scheduling**: Event times relative to prayer times (liturgical temporal engine)
 89:   - **Audience Filtering**: Age ranges (Children, Teens, Adults, Seniors), Gender designation
 90: - **Tech Events Module** (`EventTechAspect`):
 91:   - **Skill Level**: Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced, Expert
 92:   - **Tech Stack**: Technologies used (e.g., .NET, JavaScript, Python, Docker)
 93:   - **Session Format**: Hands-on, Lecture, Workshop, Q&A
 94: - **Module-Conditional Queries**: Aspect filters only applied when module enabled for tenant
 95: - **Module Service**: `IModuleService` for runtime module availability checking
 96: 
 97: ### 5. Security & Authentication
 98: **Enterprise-grade security with BFF pattern and fine-grained authorization:**
 99: 
100: - **Backend-for-Frontend (BFF)**: Blazor Server proxies all API requests
101:   - Tokens **never** exposed to browser JavaScript
102:   - Secure HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookies
103:   - YARP reverse proxy forwards `/api/*` requests with Bearer tokens
104: - **Authentication**: Keycloak (OIDC/OAuth 2.0)
105:   - Authorization Code flow with PKCE
106:   - Claims mapping with fallback: `sub` → `nameidentifier` → `sid`
107:   - Token refresh handling
108: - **Authorization**:
109:   - **Endpoint-Level**: `GET = [AllowAnonymous]`, `Write = [Authorize]`, `Admin = [Authorize(Roles="Admin")]`
110:   - **Resource-Level**: Cerbos Policy Decision Point (PDP) for fine-grained checks
111:     - `[CerbosAuthorize("event", CerbosPermissionAction.Update)]` attribute on commands
112:     - `AuthorizationBehavior` MediatR pipeline enforces policies before handler execution
113:     - YAML policy definitions in `cerbos/policies/` (tenant_settings, organization, instance_settings)
114:     - Derived roles (e.g., "owner" when `userId == resource.ownerId`)
115:     - Batch Cerbos checks for HATEOAS link filtering
116:   - **Link-Level**: `HateoasAuthorizationEvaluator` filters visible actions in HAL+JSON responses
117: - **Secrets Management**: Infisical provider with health checks, auto-refresh, audit logging, environment variable fallback
118: 
119: ### 6. REST API (Level 3 - HATEOAS)
120: **Hypermedia-driven API with HAL+JSON:**
121: 
122: - **43 REST Controllers** covering all domain entities
123: - **HATEOAS Implementation**:
124:   - HAL+JSON format (`application/hal+json`)
125:   - 18 link policies (Event, Organization, User, Actor, Session, Registration, TenantSettings, etc.)
126:   - `HateoasLinkGenerator` central service with fluent `LinkDefinition` API
127:   - `ResourceAssemblerBase<T>` for consistent resource assembly
128:   - `PreferHeaderMiddleware` for content negotiation (JSON vs HAL)
129:   - Authorization-aware link filtering — clients only see permitted actions
130: - **API Documentation**: Scalar + Swagger with OpenAPI 3.0 specs
131:   - `[EndpointSummary]` and `[EndpointDescription]` on all endpoints
132:   - `[ProducesResponseType]` for success/failure codes
133: - **NSwag Client Generation**: Auto-generated `EventApiClient` for Blazor frontend
134: - **Response Compression**: Brotli + Gzip for optimized payloads
135: 
136: ### 7. Blazor Frontend (MVP)
137: **44 pages covering complete event and organization workflows:**
138: 
139: #### Event Pages
140: - **EventList**: Browse/search events with advanced filtering (13 core + 5 Islamic + 6 Tech filters)
141: - **EventDetail**: Event overview with sessions, speakers, registration
142: - **CreateEvent**: Multi-step event creation form
143: - **EventEdit**: Update existing events
144: - **MyEvents**: User's event dashboard
145: - **EventCreated**: Confirmation page
146: 
147: #### Organization Pages
148: - **CreateOrganization**: Multi-step wizard with `MudStepper`
149: - **MyOrganizations**: User's organizations
150: - **OrganizationProfile**: Public org view
151: - **OrganizationDetails**: Full org info
152: - **OrganizationMembers**: Member management with role assignment
153: - **OrganizationReviews**: User reviews display
154: - **InviteMemberDialog**: Modal for member invitations
155: - **EditMemberRoleDialog**: Role management dialog
156: 
157: #### User Pages
158: - **UserProfile**: User identity and settings
159: - **MyRegistrations**: Registration history
160: - **MyReviews**: User-submitted reviews
161: - **Settings**: User preferences
162: 
163: #### Admin Pages
164: - **AdminList**: Admin dashboard
165: - **LookupTables**: Manage reference data (Categories, Tags, Madhabs, Locations, Languages, EventTypes, etc.)
166: - **TenantAdminSettings**: Tenant configuration
167: - **TenantPolicySettings**: Tenant policies
168: - **InstanceAdminSettings**: Instance-level settings
169: - **InstanceSettings**: System configuration
170: 
171: #### Landing Pages
172: - **LandingPageForUsers**: Authenticated home
173: - **LandingPageForNonUsers**: Public home
174: 
175: #### Layout & Reusable Components
176: - **MainLayout**: App shell with CSS isolation (BEM methodology)
177: - **NavMenu**: Navigation sidebar (CSS isolated)
178: - **AnnouncementBar**: Alert banner (CSS isolated)
179: - **Footer**: Page footer (CSS isolated)
180: - **EventFilterBar**: Reusable filter component with module-aware rendering
181: - **S3Image**: Reactive image component with presigned URLs
182: - **ImageUpload**: File upload with progress (CSS isolated)
183: 
184: #### Client Services
185: - **EventService**: Event operations consuming NSwag client
186: - **OrganizationService**: Organization operations
187: - **InstanceOnboardingService**: Setup flows
188: - **ImageStorageService**: S3 storage management
189: - **PublicExperienceService**: Anonymous endpoint access
190: 
191: ### 8. Advanced Filtering & Query System
192: **EventQuerySpecification fluent builder with 33 parameters:**
193: 
194: - **Immutable Builder Pattern**: Fluent API for complex queries with cache key generation
195: - **Core Filters**: Title search, event type, format, status, date range, organization, featured flag
196: - **Islamic Aspect Filters**: Gender mode, madhab, prayer time, audience age, audience gender
197: - **Tech Aspect Filters**: Skill level, tech stack, session format
198: - **Aspect Presence Filters**: Filter by presence/absence of Islamic or Tech aspects
199: - **Subquery Filters**: Category IDs and Tag IDs via junction table queries
200: - **Sorting**: Date, relevance, view count
201: - **Module-Conditional Composition**: Aspect filters only applied when module enabled
202: - **Blazor Integration**: `EventFilterBar` component with 24+ filter parameters, module-aware rendering
203: 
204: ### 9. Object Storage & File Management
205: **S3-compatible storage with multi-tenant resolution:**
206: 
207: - **Presigned URLs**: Direct browser-to-S3 upload/download (no server proxy)
208: - **File Metadata Tracking**: `StorageObject` entity with S3 keys, content types, sizes
209: - **Multi-Tenant Resolution**: `S3ConfigResolver` with cascading settings (Instance → Tenant)
210: - **Instance Admin Lock/Unlock**: Control tenant override permissions
211: - **Blazor Components**: `S3Image` (reactive display), `ImageUpload` (progress tracking)
212: - **Supported Providers**: AWS S3, MinIO, DigitalOcean Spaces, any S3-compatible service
213: 
214: ### 10. Email Service
215: **Production-grade SMTP with resilience:**
216: 
217: - **Provider-Agnostic**: MailKit supporting any SMTP server (Gmail, SendGrid, custom)
218: - **Multi-Tenant Configuration**: `SmtpConfigResolver` with cascading resolution (Instance → Tenant)
219: - **Resilience Patterns**: Polly pipelines with exponential backoff, circuit breaker, timeouts
220: - **Connection Validation**: Health checks for SMTP configuration
221: - **Structured Logging**: Serilog output for debugging and monitoring
222: 
223: ### 11. Observability & Monitoring
224: **PLG stack (Prometheus + Loki + Grafana):**
225: 
226: - **Structured Logging**: Serilog with JSON output
227: - **Distributed Tracing**: OpenTelemetry traces and metrics
228: - **Metrics Endpoint**: `/metrics` for Prometheus scraping (HTTP duration, DB queries, MediatR execution, exceptions)
229: - **Log Aggregation**: Logs shipped to Loki via `GrafanaLoki` sink
230: - **Dashboards**: Grafana for unified observability
231: - **Aspire Dashboard**: Local development observability (.NET Aspire)
232: - **Health Checks**: Liveness and readiness endpoints for Database, Keycloak, Cerbos, S3, SMTP
233: 
234: ### 12. Caching Strategy (Multi-Level)
235: **Optimized performance with hybrid caching:**
236: 
237: - **Output Caching**: Response-level caching with named policies:
238:   - `LookupData` — 1-hour expiration (reference data)
239:   - `ListData` — 30-second expiration (paginated lists)
240:   - `DetailData` — 60-second expiration (individual records)
241: - **HybridCache** (.NET 9+): L1 in-memory (5-minute local) + optional L2 distributed
242:   - 10MB payload limit, 512-character key limit, 30-minute default expiration
243: - **Cache Invalidation**: Tag-based invalidation via `OutputCacheInvalidationService`
244: - **Query Specification Caching**: `ToCacheKeySuffix()` for specification-based keys
245: 
246: ### 13. Federation Foundation (Phase 1)
247: **ATProto/ActivityPub data models — protocol endpoints planned for Phase 2:**
248: 
249: - **Implemented** ✅:
250:   - **Actor Entity**: Polymorphic identity (User OR Organization) with DID, Handle, PDS host
251:   - **ActorKeyStore**: Cryptographic key material storage
252:   - **AtprotoRecord**: ATProto record storage (`ngo.islamu.event.*` namespace)
253:   - **IndexedDid**: DID resolution caching
254:   - **SyncState**: Outbound federation tracking
255:   - **Enums**: `ActorType` (User, Organization, Bot), `DidCustodyType` (SelfHosted, PLCServer)
256: - **Not Yet Implemented** ⏳:
257:   - HTTP endpoints (WebFinger, Actor endpoints, Inbox/Outbox)
258:   - ATProto PDS server
259:   - ATProto AppView indexing
260:   - ActivityPub ↔ ATProto bridge/gateway
261:   - DID resolution (PLC/DNS-based)
262:   - HTTP Signatures
263:   - Collections (Followers, Following, Liked)
264: 
265: ---
266: 
267: ## 🏗️ Architecture & Design
268: 
269: ### Clean Architecture + CQRS
270: **4-layer separation with strict dependency rules:**
271: 
272: ```
273: Presentation Layer (Explore.API, Explore.Blazor)
274:     ↓ depends on
275: Application Layer (Explore.Application)
276:     ↓ depends on
277: Domain Layer (Explore.Domain) ← no external dependencies
278:     ↑ implemented by
279: Infrastructure Layer (Explore.Persistence, Explore.Infrastructure)
280: ```
281: 
282: - **Domain Layer**: 62 entities, 18 enums, 3 core interfaces (ITenantEntity, IAuditableEntity, ISoftDeletable)
283: - **Application Layer**: 48 feature modules, CQRS handlers (MediatR), DTOs with FluentValidation
284: - **Infrastructure Layer**: EF Core repositories, Keycloak integration, Cerbos service, Infisical provider, S3 storage, SMTP email
285: - **Presentation Layer**: 43 REST controllers, 44 Blazor pages
286: 
287: ### Domain Model Highlights
288: **Triple Interface Pattern on all entities:**
289: - **ITenantEntity**: `TenantId` for multi-tenant isolation
290: - **IAuditableEntity**: `CreatedAt`, `CreatedBy`, `UpdatedAt`, `UpdatedBy`
291: - **ISoftDeletable**: `IsDeleted`, `DeletedAt`, `DeletedBy` (soft delete with full audit trail)
292: 
293: **Key Entities**:
294: - Event aggregate: `Event`, `EventSession`, `EventSessionSpeaker`, `EventSessionAgendaItem`, `EventRegistration`
295: - Event aspects: `EventIslamicAspect`, `EventTechAspect` (module-conditional)
296: - Organization: `Organization`, `OrganizationMember`, `OrganizationReview`
297: - Identity: `User`, `Actor`, `ActorKeyStore`
298: - Lookups: 18+ reference tables (EventType, Category, Tag, Madhab, Language, Location, etc.)
299: - Federation: `AtprotoRecord`, `IndexedDid`, `SyncState`
300: - Settings: `TenantSetting`, `AppSetting`, `ConfigurationChangeLog`
301: 
302: ### Repository Pattern
303: - **GenericRepository<T, TId>**: Base repository with CRUD + soft delete
304: - **Specification Pattern**: `IQuerySpecification<T>` for complex queries
305: - **EF Core Optimizations**:
306:   - `AsNoTracking()` for simple read-only queries
307:   - `AsNoTrackingWithIdentityResolution()` for complex queries with shared navigation properties
308: - **Named Query Filters** (EF Core 10):
309:   - `"Tenant"` — Always-active tenant isolation
310:   - `"SoftDelete"` — Can be selectively bypassed with `IgnoreQueryFilter("SoftDelete")`
311: 
312: ### Authorization Pipeline
313: **Three-level authorization enforcement:**
314: 
315: 1. **Endpoint-Level**: `[AllowAnonymous]` / `[Authorize]` / `[Authorize(Roles="Admin")]`
316: 2. **Resource-Level**: MediatR `AuthorizationBehavior` → Cerbos policy checks before handler execution
317: 3. **Link-Level**: `HateoasAuthorizationEvaluator` → Batch Cerbos checks filter visible actions in HAL responses
318: 
319: ### BFF Security Model
320: **No tokens in browser JavaScript:**
321: 
322: ```
323: Browser (Blazor WASM)
324:     ↓ HTTPS session cookie (HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict)
325: Blazor Server (BFF)
326:     ↓ HTTPS Bearer token (JWT)
327: API (JWT validation)
328: ```
329: 
330: - `Explore.Blazor` (Server) manages Keycloak OIDC flow, stores tokens server-side
331: - `Explore.Blazor.Client` (WASM) sends session cookie automatically
332: - YARP proxy attaches JWT to `/api/*` requests transparently
333:

396: ## 🔒 Security Considerations
397: 
398: ### Authentication & Authorization
399: - ✅ BFF pattern prevents token exposure to browser
400: - ✅ Secure HttpOnly cookies with SameSite=Strict
401: - ✅ Keycloak OIDC Authorization Code flow with PKCE
402: - ✅ Fine-grained authorization via Cerbos (policy-based)
403: - ✅ Resource-level checks in MediatR pipeline
404: - ✅ HATEOAS link filtering based on permissions
405: 
406: ### Data Protection
407: - ✅ Multi-tenancy with global query filters
408: - ✅ Soft delete with full audit trail (who deleted, when)
409: - ✅ Auditing fields on all entities (created, updated, deleted)
410: - ✅ Secrets management via Infisical (never in source control)
411: - ✅ Database credentials encrypted at rest
412: - ✅ S3 presigned URLs for direct upload (no server proxy)

475: ## 🎓 Getting Started
476: 
477: ### Prerequisites
478: - .NET 10 SDK
479: - Docker Desktop (for Keycloak, PostgreSQL, MinIO)
480: - PostgreSQL 16+ with PostGIS extension
481: - Node.js 20+ (for NSwag client generation)
482: 
483: ### Quick Start (Development)
484: ```bash
485: # Clone repository
486: git clone https://github.com/islamu/explore.git
487: cd explore
488: 
489: # Start infrastructure with Docker Compose
490: docker compose up -d keycloak postgres minio
491: 
492: # Run database migrations
493: dotnet ef database update --project Event.MigrationService
494: 
495: # Start API
496: dotnet run --project Explore.API
497: 
498: # Start Blazor (separate terminal)
499: dotnet run --project Explore.Blazor
500: 
501: # Access application
502: # Blazor: https://localhost:7001
503: # API: https://localhost:5001
504: # Scalar: https://localhost:5001/scalar/v1
505: ```
506: 
507: ### Quick Start (Production)
508: ```bash
509: # Build Docker images
510: docker build -t explore-api -f Explore.API/Dockerfile .
511: docker build -t explore-blazor -f Explore.Blazor/Dockerfile .
512: 
513: # Run with Docker Compose
514: docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d
515: 
516: # Access application
517: # Blazor: https://your-domain.com
518: # API: https://api.your-domain.com
519: ```
