 25:     public GetEventListRequestHandler(
 26:         IEventRepository eventRepository,
 27:         IMapper mapper,
 28:         IObjectStorageService objectStorageService,
 29:         ILogger<GetEventListRequestHandler> logger,
 30:         HybridCache cache,
 31:         IModuleService moduleService,
 32:         ITenantContext tenantContext)
 33:     {
 34:         _eventRepository = eventRepository;
 35:         _mapper = mapper;
 36:         _objectStorageService = objectStorageService;
 37:         _logger = logger;

 39:         _moduleService = moduleService;
 40:         _tenantContext = tenantContext;

 42: 
 43:     public async Task<PaginatedResult<EventListDto>> Handle(GetEventListRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
 44:     {
 45:         var specification = await BuildSpecificationAsync(request, cancellationToken);
 46:         var cacheKeySuffix = specification.ToCacheKeySuffix();
 47:         var cacheKey = $"events:list:{request.PageNumber}:{request.PageSize}:{cacheKeySuffix}";
 48: 
 49:         var cachedResult = await _cache.GetOrCreateAsync(
 50:             cacheKey,
 51:             async _ =>
 52:             {
 53:                 var (events, totalCount) = await _eventRepository.GetEventsWithDetailsPaged(
 54:                     request.PageNumber, request.PageSize, specification);
 55:                 var eventDtos = _mapper.Map<List<EventListDto>>(events);
 56:                 return PaginatedResult<EventListDto>.Create(eventDtos, totalCount, request.PageNumber, request.PageSize);
 57:             },
 58:             new HybridCacheEntryOptions
 59:             {
 60:                 Expiration = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5),
 61:                 LocalCacheExpiration = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1)
 62:             },
 63:             cancellationToken: cancellationToken);
 64: 
 65: 
 66:         foreach (var dto in cachedResult.Items)
 67:         {
 68:             dto.FeaturedImageUri = await ResolveImageUrl(dto.FeaturedImageUri);
 69:             dto.ActorProfilePictureUri = await ResolveImageUrl(dto.ActorProfilePictureUri);
 70:         }
 71: 
 72:         return cachedResult;
 73:     }
 74: 
 75: 
 76: 
 77: 
 78: 
 79:     private async Task<EventQuerySpecification> BuildSpecificationAsync(
 80:         GetEventListRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
 81:     {
 82:         var spec = new EventQuerySpecification();
 83: 
 84: 
 85: 
 86:         if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(request.SearchTerm))
 87:             spec = spec.And(EventFilter.SearchTerm(request.SearchTerm.Trim()));
 88: 
 89:         if (request.FormatId.HasValue)
 90:             spec = spec.And(EventFilter.Format(request.FormatId.Value));
 91: 
 92:         if (request.MadhabId.HasValue)
 93:             spec = spec.And(EventFilter.Madhab(request.MadhabId.Value));
 94: 
 95:         if (request.EventTypeId.HasValue)
 96:             spec = spec.And(EventFilter.EventType(request.EventTypeId.Value));
 97: 
 98:         if (request.AudienceGenderId.HasValue)
 99:             spec = spec.And(EventFilter.AudienceGender(request.AudienceGenderId.Value));
100: 
101:         if (request.AudienceAgeId.HasValue)
102:             spec = spec.And(EventFilter.AudienceAge(request.AudienceAgeId.Value));
103: 
104:         if (request.EventStatusId.HasValue)
105:             spec = spec.And(EventFilter.Status(request.EventStatusId.Value));
106: 
107:         if (request.DateFrom.HasValue)
108:             spec = spec.And(EventFilter.DateFrom(request.DateFrom.Value));
109: 
110:         if (request.DateTo.HasValue)
111:             spec = spec.And(EventFilter.DateTo(request.DateTo.Value));
112: 
113: 
114: 
115:         if (request.CategoryId.HasValue)
116:             spec = spec.And(EventSubqueryFilter.Category(request.CategoryId.Value));
117: 
118:         if (request.TagId.HasValue)
119:             spec = spec.And(EventSubqueryFilter.Tag(request.TagId.Value));
120: 
121:         if (request.LocationId.HasValue)
122:             spec = spec.And(EventSubqueryFilter.Location(request.LocationId.Value));
123: 
124:         if (request.LanguageId.HasValue)
125:             spec = spec.And(EventSubqueryFilter.Language(request.LanguageId.Value));
126: 
127:         if (request.RegistrationModeId.HasValue)
128:             spec = spec.And(EventSubqueryFilter.RegistrationMode(request.RegistrationModeId.Value));
129: 
130: 
131: 
132:         if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(request.MetadataJsonContains))
133:             spec = spec.And(EventSubqueryFilter.JsonContains(request.MetadataJsonContains.Trim()));
134: 
135:         if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(request.MetadataJsonKeyExists))
136:             spec = spec.And(EventSubqueryFilter.JsonKeyExists(request.MetadataJsonKeyExists.Trim()));
137: 
138: 
139: 
140:         var tenantId = _tenantContext.TenantId;
141:         var hasIslamicAspectFilters = request.GenderModeId.HasValue
142:             || request.IncludesQuranRecitation is true
143:             || request.ReferencePrayerId.HasValue
144:             || request.IslamicPrimaryLanguageId.HasValue
145:             || request.HasIslamicAspect is true;
146: 
147:         if (hasIslamicAspectFilters &&
148:             await _moduleService.IsModuleEnabledAsync(tenantId, "Mod_Islamic", cancellationToken))
149:         {
150:             if (request.HasIslamicAspect is true)
151:                 spec = spec.And(AspectPresenceFilter.HasIslamicAspect());
152: 
153:             if (request.GenderModeId.HasValue)
154:                 spec = spec.And(IslamicAspectFilter.GenderMode((GenderSegregationMode)request.GenderModeId.Value));
155: 
156:             if (request.IncludesQuranRecitation is true)
157:                 spec = spec.And(IslamicAspectFilter.IncludesQuranRecitation());
158: 
159:             if (request.ReferencePrayerId.HasValue)
160:                 spec = spec.And(IslamicAspectFilter.ReferencePrayer((PrayerTime)request.ReferencePrayerId.Value));
161: 
162:             if (request.IslamicPrimaryLanguageId.HasValue)
163:                 spec = spec.And(IslamicAspectFilter.PrimaryLanguage(request.IslamicPrimaryLanguageId.Value));
164:         }
165: 
166: 
167: 
168:         var hasTechAspectFilters = request.SkillLevelId.HasValue
169:             || request.IsCodingCompetition is true
170:             || request.IsHackathon is true
171:             || request.RequiresLaptop is true
172:             || !string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(request.TechStackTag)
173:             || request.HasTechAspect is true;
174: 
175:         if (hasTechAspectFilters &&
176:             await _moduleService.IsModuleEnabledAsync(tenantId, "Mod_Tech", cancellationToken))
177:         {
178:             if (request.HasTechAspect is true)
179:                 spec = spec.And(AspectPresenceFilter.HasTechAspect());
180: 
181:             if (request.SkillLevelId.HasValue)
182:                 spec = spec.And(TechAspectFilter.SkillLevel((SkillLevel)request.SkillLevelId.Value));
183: 
184:             if (request.IsCodingCompetition is true)
185:                 spec = spec.And(TechAspectFilter.IsCodingCompetition());
186: 
187:             if (request.IsHackathon is true)
188:                 spec = spec.And(TechAspectFilter.IsHackathon());
189: 
190:             if (request.RequiresLaptop is true)
191:                 spec = spec.And(TechAspectFilter.RequiresLaptop());
192: 
193:             if (!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(request.TechStackTag))
194:                 spec = spec.And(TechAspectFilter.TechStack(request.TechStackTag.Trim()));
195:         }
196: 
197: 
198: 
199:         var sort = ResolveSortField(request.SortBy);
200:         if (sort is not null)
201:         {
202:             spec = request.SortDescending ? spec.SortByDescending(sort) : spec.SortBy(sort);
203:         }
204:         else
205:         {
206: 
207:             spec = spec.SortByDescending(EventSort.Date);
208:         }
209: 
210:         return spec;
211:     }

214: 
215: 
216:     private static EventSort? ResolveSortField(string? sortBy) =>
217:         sortBy?.ToLowerInvariant() switch
218:         {
219:             "date" => EventSort.Date,
220:             "title" => EventSort.Title,
221:             "views" => EventSort.Views,
222:             "createdat" => EventSort.CreatedAt,
223:             _ => null
224:         };
225: 
226: 
227: 
228: 
229: 
230:     private async Task<string?> ResolveImageUrl(string? objectKeyOrUri)
231:     {
232:         if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(objectKeyOrUri))
233:             return null;
234: 
235:         try
236:         {
237: 
238:             if (objectKeyOrUri.StartsWith("http://", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase) ||
239:                 objectKeyOrUri.StartsWith("https://", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
240:             {
241: 
242:                 if (Uri.TryCreate(objectKeyOrUri, UriKind.Absolute, out var uri))
243:                 {
244:                     var objectKey = uri.AbsolutePath.TrimStart('/');
245:                     return await _objectStorageService.GeneratePresignedDownloadUrl(objectKey, 60);
246:                 }
247:                 return objectKeyOrUri;
248:             }
249: 
250: 
251:             return await _objectStorageService.GeneratePresignedDownloadUrl(objectKeyOrUri, 60);
252:         }
253:         catch (Exception ex)
254:         {
255:             _logger.LogError(ex, "Failed to generate presigned URL for object key: {ObjectKey}", objectKeyOrUri);
256:             return null;
257:         }
258:     }
259: }
````

## File: Explore.Application/Features/Users/Handlers/Commands/UpdateUserCommandHandler.cs
````csharp
 1: using System;
 2: using System.Threading;
 3: using System.Threading.Tasks;
 4: using AutoMapper;
 5: using Explore.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
 6: using Explore.Application.Features.Users.Requests.Commands;
 7: using Explore.Application.Responses;
 8: using MediatR;
 9: using Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Hybrid;
10: 
11: namespace Explore.Application.Features.Users.Handlers.Commands;
12: 
13: public class UpdateUserCommandHandler : IRequestHandler<UpdateUserCommand, BaseCommandResponse<Guid>>
14: {
15:     private readonly IUserRepository _userRepository;
16:     private readonly IActorRepository _actorRepository;
17:     private readonly IStorageObjectRepository _storageObjectRepository;
18:     private readonly IMapper _mapper;
19:     private readonly HybridCache _cache;
20: 
21:     public UpdateUserCommandHandler(
22:         IUserRepository userRepository,
23:         IActorRepository actorRepository,
24:         IStorageObjectRepository storageObjectRepository,
25:         IMapper mapper,
26:         HybridCache cache)
27:     {
28:         _userRepository = userRepository;
29:         _actorRepository = actorRepository;
30:         _storageObjectRepository = storageObjectRepository;
31:         _mapper = mapper;
32:         _cache = cache;
33:     }
34: 
35:     public async Task<BaseCommandResponse<Guid>> Handle(UpdateUserCommand request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
36:     {
37:         var response = new BaseCommandResponse<Guid>();
38:         var user = await _userRepository.GetById(request.UpdateUserDto.Id);
39: 
40:         if (user == null)
41:         {
42:             response.Success = false;
43:             response.Message = "User not found";
44:             return response;
45:         }
46: 
47:         _mapper.Map(request.UpdateUserDto, user);
48:         await _userRepository.Update(user);
49: 
50: 
51:         if (request.UpdateUserDto.ProfilePictureId.HasValue && user.ActorId.HasValue)
52:         {
53:             var actor = await _actorRepository.GetById(user.ActorId.Value);
54:             if (actor != null)
55:             {
56:                 actor.ProfilePictureId = request.UpdateUserDto.ProfilePictureId.Value;
57:                 await _actorRepository.Update(actor);
58: 
59: 
60:                 var storageObject = await _storageObjectRepository.GetById(request.UpdateUserDto.ProfilePictureId.Value);
61:                 if (storageObject != null)
62:                 {
63:                     storageObject.ActorId = user.ActorId.Value;
64:                     await _storageObjectRepository.Update(storageObject);
65:                 }
66:             }
67:         }
68: 
69:         response.Success = true;
70:         response.Message = "User updated successfully";
71:         response.Id = user.Id;
72: 
73:         await _cache.RemoveAsync($"user:detail:{user.Id}", cancellationToken);
74: 
75:         return response;
76:     }
77: }
````

## File: Explore.Application/Features/Users/Handlers/Queries/GetUserRequestHandler.cs
````csharp
  1: using System;
  2: using System.Threading;
  3: using System.Threading.Tasks;
  4: using AutoMapper;
  5: using Explore.Application.Contracts.Infrastructure;
  6: using Explore.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
  7: using Explore.Application.DTOs.User;
  8: using Explore.Application.Features.Users.Requests.Queries;
  9: using MediatR;
 10: using Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Hybrid;
 11: using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
 12: 
 13: namespace Explore.Application.Features.Users.Handlers.Queries;
 14: 
 15: public class GetUserRequestHandler : IRequestHandler<GetUserRequest, UserDto>
 16: {
 17:     private readonly IUserRepository _userRepository;
 18:     private readonly IObjectStorageService _objectStorageService;
 19:     private readonly IMapper _mapper;
 20:     private readonly ILogger<GetUserRequestHandler> _logger;
 21:     private readonly HybridCache _cache;
 22: 
 23:     public GetUserRequestHandler(
 24:         IUserRepository userRepository,
 25:         IObjectStorageService objectStorageService,
 26:         IMapper mapper,
 27:         ILogger<GetUserRequestHandler> logger,
 28:         HybridCache cache)
 29:     {
 30:         _userRepository = userRepository;
 31:         _objectStorageService = objectStorageService;
 32:         _mapper = mapper;
 33:         _logger = logger;
 34:         _cache = cache;
 35:     }
 36: 
 37:     public async Task<UserDto> Handle(GetUserRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
 38:     {
 39:         var cacheKey = $"user:detail:{request.UserId}";
 40: 
 41:         var userDto = await _cache.GetOrCreateAsync(
 42:             cacheKey,
 43:             async _ =>
 44:             {
 45:                 var user = await _userRepository.GetUserWithDetails(request.UserId);
 46:                 if (user == null)
 47:                 {
 48:                     return null;
 49:                 }
 50: 
 51:                 var dto = _mapper.Map<UserDto>(user);
 52: 
 53:                 if (user.Actor?.ProfilePicture != null)
 54:                 {
 55:                     dto.ProfileImageKey = user.Actor.ProfilePicture.Uri;
 56:                     dto.ProfileImageUri = user.Actor.ProfilePicture.Uri;
 57:                 }
 58:                 else if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(user.Actor?.ProfilePictureUri))
 59:                 {
 60:                     dto.ProfileImageUri = user.Actor.ProfilePictureUri;
 61:                 }
 62: 
 63:                 return dto;
 64:             },
 65:             new HybridCacheEntryOptions
 66:             {
 67:                 Expiration = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5),
 68:                 LocalCacheExpiration = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(1)
 69:             },
 70:             cancellationToken: cancellationToken);
 71: 
 72:         if (userDto != null && !string.IsNullOrEmpty(userDto.ProfileImageKey))
 73:         {
 74:             userDto.ProfileImageUri = await ResolveImageUrl(userDto.ProfileImageKey);
 75:         }
 76: 
 77:         return userDto;
 78:     }
 79: 
 80:     private async Task<string?> ResolveImageUrl(string? objectKeyOrUri)
 81:     {
 82:         if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(objectKeyOrUri))
 83:         {
 84:             return null;
 85:         }
 86: 
 87:         try
 88:         {
 89: 
 90:             if (objectKeyOrUri.StartsWith("http://") || objectKeyOrUri.StartsWith("https://"))
 91:             {
 92:                 if (Uri.TryCreate(objectKeyOrUri, UriKind.Absolute, out var uri))
 93:                 {
 94: 
 95:                     var objectKey = uri.AbsolutePath.TrimStart('/');
 96:                     return await _objectStorageService.GeneratePresignedDownloadUrl(objectKey, 60);
 97:                 }
 98:                 _logger.LogWarning("Failed to parse legacy URL: {Uri}", objectKeyOrUri);
 99:                 return objectKeyOrUri;
100:             }
101: 
102: 
103:             return await _objectStorageService.GeneratePresignedDownloadUrl(objectKeyOrUri, 60);
104:         }
105:         catch (Exception ex)
106:         {
107:             _logger.LogError(ex, "Failed to generate presigned URL for: {ObjectKeyOrUri}", objectKeyOrUri);
108:             return null;
109:         }
110:     }
111: }
````

## File: Explore.Infrastructure/Identity/AdminContext.cs
````csharp
  1: using System.Security.Claims;
  2: using Explore.Application.Contracts.Identity;
  3: using Explore.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
  4: using Explore.Domain.Constants;
  5: using Explore.Domain.Enums;
  6: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http;
  7: using Microsoft.Extensions.Caching.Memory;
  8: using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;
  9: 
 10: namespace Explore.Infrastructure.Identity;
 11: 
 12: 
 13: 
 14: 
 15: 
 16: 
 17: public class AdminContext : IAdminContext, IAdminCacheInvalidator
 18: {
 19:     private readonly IHttpContextAccessor _httpContextAccessor;
 20:     private readonly IPlatformUserRoleRepository _platformUserRoleRepository;
 21:     private readonly IInstanceBootstrapStateRepository _instanceBootstrapStateRepository;
 22:     private readonly ITenantMemberRepository _tenantAdminRepo;
 23:     private readonly IOrganizationMemberRepository _orgMemberRepo;
 24:     private readonly IMemoryCache _cache;
 25:     private readonly ILogger<AdminContext> _logger;
 26: 
 27:     private static readonly TimeSpan CacheExpiration = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(5);
 28:     private const string CacheKeyPrefix = "AdminContext_";
 29: 
 30:     public AdminContext(
 31:         IHttpContextAccessor httpContextAccessor,
 32:         IPlatformUserRoleRepository platformUserRoleRepository,
 33:         IInstanceBootstrapStateRepository instanceBootstrapStateRepository,
 34:         ITenantMemberRepository tenantAdminRepo,
 35:         IOrganizationMemberRepository orgMemberRepo,
 36:         IMemoryCache cache,
 37:         ILogger<AdminContext> logger)
 38:     {
 39:         _httpContextAccessor = httpContextAccessor;
 40:         _platformUserRoleRepository = platformUserRoleRepository;
 41:         _instanceBootstrapStateRepository = instanceBootstrapStateRepository;
 42:         _tenantAdminRepo = tenantAdminRepo;
 43:         _orgMemberRepo = orgMemberRepo;
 44:         _cache = cache;
 45:         _logger = logger;
 46:     }
 47: 
 48:     public Guid? UserId
 49:     {
 50:         get
 51:         {
 52:             var user = _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.User;
 53:             if (user?.Identity?.IsAuthenticated != true)
 54:                 return null;
 55: 
 56:             var sub = user.FindFirst("sub")?.Value
 57:                 ?? user.FindFirst(ClaimTypes.NameIdentifier)?.Value
 58:                 ?? user.FindFirst("sid")?.Value;
 59: 
 60:             return Guid.TryParse(sub, out var userId) ? userId : null;
 61:         }
 62:     }
 63: 
 64:     public Task<bool> IsInstanceAdminAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 65:     {
 66:         var uid = UserId;
 67:         return uid == null ? Task.FromResult(false) : IsInstanceAdminAsync(uid.Value, cancellationToken);
 68:     }
 69: 
 70:     public async Task<bool> IsInstanceAdminAsync(Guid userId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 71:     {
 72: 
 73:         var cacheKey = $"{CacheKeyPrefix}Instance_{userId}";
 74:         return await _cache.GetOrCreateAsync(cacheKey, async entry =>
 75:         {
 76:             entry.SlidingExpiration = CacheExpiration;
 77:             var isRoleAdmin = false;
 78:             try
 79:             {
 80:                 isRoleAdmin = await _platformUserRoleRepository.IsUserPlatformAdmin(userId);
 81:             }
 82:             catch (Exception ex)
 83:             {
 84: 
 85: 
 86:                 _logger.LogWarning(ex, "AdminContext: failed role-based instance admin check for user {UserId}", userId);
 87:             }
 88: 
 89:             if (isRoleAdmin)
 90:             {
 91:                 _logger.LogDebug("AdminContext: User {UserId} IsInstanceAdmin=true (platform.admin role)", userId);
 92:                 return true;
 93:             }
 94: 
 95:             var bootstrap = await _instanceBootstrapStateRepository.GetCurrent();
 96:             var isBootstrapAdmin = bootstrap?.IsCompleted == true && bootstrap.CompletedByUserId == userId;
 97: 
 98: 
 99: 
100:             if (!isBootstrapAdmin
101:                 && bootstrap?.IsCompleted == true
102:                 && !bootstrap.CompletedByUserId.HasValue)
103:             {
104:                 isBootstrapAdmin = await _tenantAdminRepo.IsTenantAdmin(PlatformDefaults.DefaultTenantId, userId);
105:             }
106: 
107:             _logger.LogDebug(
108:                 "AdminContext: User {UserId} IsInstanceAdmin={IsAdmin} (bootstrap fallback)",
109:                 userId,
110:                 isBootstrapAdmin);
111: 
112:             return isBootstrapAdmin;
113:         });
114:     }
115: 
116:     public async Task<bool> IsTenantAdminAsync(Guid tenantId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
117:     {
118:         var uid = UserId;
119:         if (uid == null)
120:             return false;
121: 
122:         var cacheKey = $"{CacheKeyPrefix}Tenant_{uid}_{tenantId}";
123:         return await _cache.GetOrCreateAsync(cacheKey, async entry =>
124:         {
125:             entry.SlidingExpiration = CacheExpiration;
126:             return await _tenantAdminRepo.IsTenantAdmin(tenantId, uid.Value);
127:         });
128:     }
129: 
130:     public async Task<bool> IsOrganizationAdminAsync(Guid organizationId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
131:     {
132:         var uid = UserId;
133:         if (uid == null)
134:             return false;
135: 
136:         var cacheKey = $"{CacheKeyPrefix}Org_{uid}_{organizationId}";
137:         return await _cache.GetOrCreateAsync(cacheKey, async entry =>
138:         {
139:             entry.SlidingExpiration = CacheExpiration;
140:             var membership = await _orgMemberRepo.GetByOrganizationAndUser(organizationId, uid.Value);
141:             return membership != null && IsOrganizationAdminRole(membership.RoleId);
142:         });
143:     }
144: 
145:     public Task<IReadOnlyList<Guid>> GetAdminTenantIdsAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
146:     {
147:         var uid = UserId;
148:         return uid == null
149:             ? Task.FromResult<IReadOnlyList<Guid>>(Array.Empty<Guid>())
150:             : GetAdminTenantIdsAsync(uid.Value, cancellationToken);
151:     }
152: 
153:     public async Task<IReadOnlyList<Guid>> GetAdminTenantIdsAsync(Guid userId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
154:     {
155:         var cacheKey = $"{CacheKeyPrefix}TenantIds_{userId}";
156:         return await _cache.GetOrCreateAsync(cacheKey, async entry =>
157:         {
158:             entry.SlidingExpiration = CacheExpiration;
159:             var admins = await _tenantAdminRepo.GetByUserId(userId);
160:             var adminTenantIds = admins
161:                 .Where(a => a.RoleId == (int)RoleEnum.TenantOwner || a.RoleId == (int)RoleEnum.TenantAdmin)
162:                 .Select(a => a.TenantId)
163:                 .Distinct()
164:                 .ToList()
165:                 .AsReadOnly();
166: 
167:             return (IReadOnlyList<Guid>)adminTenantIds;
168:         }) ?? Array.Empty<Guid>();
169:     }
170: 
171:     public Task<IReadOnlyList<Guid>> GetAdminOrganizationIdsAsync(CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
172:     {
173:         var uid = UserId;
174:         return uid == null
175:             ? Task.FromResult<IReadOnlyList<Guid>>(Array.Empty<Guid>())
176:             : GetAdminOrganizationIdsAsync(uid.Value, cancellationToken);
177:     }
178: 
179:     public async Task<IReadOnlyList<Guid>> GetAdminOrganizationIdsAsync(Guid userId, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
180:     {
181:         var cacheKey = $"{CacheKeyPrefix}OrgIds_{userId}";
182:         return await _cache.GetOrCreateAsync(cacheKey, async entry =>
183:         {
184:             entry.SlidingExpiration = CacheExpiration;
185:             var memberships = await _orgMemberRepo.GetMembershipsByUser(userId);
186:             var adminOrgIds = memberships
187:                 .Where(m => IsOrganizationAdminRole(m.RoleId))
188:                 .Select(m => m.OrganizationId)
189:                 .Distinct()
190:                 .ToList()
191:                 .AsReadOnly();
192: 
193:             return (IReadOnlyList<Guid>)adminOrgIds;
194:         }) ?? Array.Empty<Guid>();
195:     }
196: 
197:     private static bool IsOrganizationAdminRole(int roleId)
198:     {
199:         return roleId == (int)RoleEnum.OrgCreator
200:             || roleId == (int)RoleEnum.OrgCoOwner
201:             || roleId == (int)RoleEnum.OrgAdmin;
202:     }
203: 
204: 
205:     public void InvalidateUser(Guid userId)
206:     {
207:         _cache.Remove($"{CacheKeyPrefix}Instance_{userId}");
208:         _cache.Remove($"{CacheKeyPrefix}TenantIds_{userId}");
209:         _cache.Remove($"{CacheKeyPrefix}OrgIds_{userId}");
210:         _logger.LogDebug("AdminContext: Invalidated cache for user {UserId}", userId);

## File: Explore.Persistence/Repositories/GenericRepository.cs
````csharp
  1: using System;
  2: using System.Collections.Generic;
  3: using System.Text;
  4: using Explore.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
  5: using Explore.Domain.Interfaces;
  6: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;
  7: using Npgsql;
  8: 
  9: namespace Explore.Persistence.Repositories;
 10: 
 11: public class GenericRepository<T, TKey> : IGenericRepository<T, TKey> where T : class
 12: {
 13:     private readonly ExploreDbContext _dbContext;
 14: 
 15:     public GenericRepository(ExploreDbContext dbContext)
 16:     {
 17:         _dbContext = dbContext;
 18:     }
 19: 
 20:     public async Task<T> Create(T entity)
 21:     {
 22:         try
 23:         {
 24:             await _dbContext.AddAsync(entity);
 25:             await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
 26:             return entity;
 27:         }
 28:         catch (DbUpdateException ex) when (ex.InnerException is PostgresException pgEx && pgEx.SqlState == "23505")
 29:         {
 30: 
 31:             _dbContext.Entry(entity).State = EntityState.Detached;
 32:             throw new InvalidOperationException(
 33:                 $"A record with the same unique key already exists. Constraint: {pgEx.ConstraintName}. " +
 34:                 $"Detail: {pgEx.Detail}",
 35:                 ex);
 36:         }
 37:     }
 38: 
 39: 
 40: 
 41: 
 42: 
 43:     public async Task Delete(T entity)
 44:     {
 45: 
 46:         if (entity is ISoftDeletable)
 47:         {
 48: 
 49:             _dbContext.Entry(entity).State = EntityState.Deleted;
 50:             await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
 51:         }
 52:         else
 53:         {
 54: 
 55:             _dbContext.Set<T>().Remove(entity);
 56:             await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
 57:         }
 58:     }
 59: 
 60: 
 61: 
 62: 
 63: 
 64: 
 65:     public async Task HardDelete(T entity)
 66:     {
 67:         _dbContext.Set<T>().Remove(entity);
 68:         await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
 69:     }
 70: 
 71:     public async Task<bool> Exists(TKey id)
 72:     {
 73:         var entity = await GetById(id);
 74:         return entity != null;
 75:     }
 76: 
 77:     public async Task<IReadOnlyList<T>> GetAll()
 78:     {
 79:         return await _dbContext.Set<T>().AsNoTracking().ToListAsync();
 80:     }
 81: 
 82:     public async Task<(IReadOnlyList<T> Items, int TotalCount)> GetAllPaged(int pageNumber, int pageSize)
 83:     {
 84:         var query = _dbContext.Set<T>().AsNoTracking();
 85:         var totalCount = await query.CountAsync();
 86:         var items = await query
 87:             .Skip((pageNumber - 1) * pageSize)
 88:             .Take(pageSize)
 89:             .ToListAsync();
 90:         return (items, totalCount);
 91:     }
 92: 
 93:     public async Task<T?> GetById(TKey id)
 94:     {
 95:         return await _dbContext.Set<T>().FindAsync(id);
 96:     }
 97: 
 98:     public async Task Update(T entity)
 99:     {
100:         _dbContext.Entry(entity).State = EntityState.Modified;
101:         await _dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
102:     }
103: }
````

100:             .Where(m => m.User.Pii != null && m.User.Pii.Email == email)
101:             .ToListAsync();
102:     }
103: 
104:     public async Task<OrganizationMember?> GetByOrganizationAndUser(Guid organizationId, Guid userId)
105:     {
106:         return await _dbContext.OrganizationMembers
107:             .AsNoTracking()
108:             .Include(m => m.Role)
109:             .Include(m => m.Organization)
110:             .FirstOrDefaultAsync(m => m.OrganizationId == organizationId && m.UserId == userId);
111:     }
112: 
113:     public async Task<bool> HasPermissionInOrganization(Guid organizationId, Guid userId, string permissionMasterCode)
114:     {
115: 
116:         var roleId = await _dbContext.OrganizationMembers
117:             .AsNoTracking()
118:             .Where(m => m.OrganizationId == organizationId && m.UserId == userId)
119:             .Select(m => (int?)m.RoleId)
120:             .FirstOrDefaultAsync();
121: 
122:         if (roleId == null)
123:             return false;
124: 
125: 
126:         var hasPermission = await _dbContext.Set<RolePermission>()
127:             .AsNoTracking()
128:             .AnyAsync(rp => rp.RoleId == roleId.Value
129:                 && rp.Permission.MasterCode == permissionMasterCode
130:                 && rp.Permission.IsActive);
131: 
132:         if (hasPermission)
133:             return true;
134: 
135: 
136: 
137:         var anyPermissionsSeeded = await _dbContext.Set<RolePermission>().AnyAsync();
138:         if (!anyPermissionsSeeded)
139:         {
140:             var adminRoles = new[]
141:             {
142:                 (int)RoleEnum.OrgCreator,
143:                 (int)RoleEnum.OrgCoOwner,
144:                 (int)RoleEnum.OrgAdmin
145:             };
146:             return adminRoles.Contains(roleId.Value);
147:         }
148: 
149:         return false;
150:     }
151: 
152:     public async Task<List<Guid>> GetOrganizationIdsWhereUserHasPermission(Guid userId, string permissionMasterCode)
153:     {
154: 
155:         var orgIds = await _dbContext.OrganizationMembers
156:             .AsNoTracking()
157:             .Where(m => m.UserId == userId)
158:             .Where(m => _dbContext.Set<RolePermission>()
159:                 .Any(rp => rp.RoleId == m.RoleId
160:                     && rp.Permission.MasterCode == permissionMasterCode
161:                     && rp.Permission.IsActive))
162:             .Select(m => m.OrganizationId)
163:             .ToListAsync();
164: 
165:         if (orgIds.Count > 0)
166:             return orgIds;
167: 
168: 
169:         var anyPermissionsSeeded = await _dbContext.Set<RolePermission>().AnyAsync();
170:         if (!anyPermissionsSeeded)
171:         {
172:             var adminRoles = new[]
173:             {
174:                 (int)RoleEnum.OrgCreator,
175:                 (int)RoleEnum.OrgCoOwner,
176:                 (int)RoleEnum.OrgAdmin
177:             };
178: 
179:             return await _dbContext.OrganizationMembers
180:                 .AsNoTracking()
181:                 .Where(m => m.UserId == userId && adminRoles.Contains(m.RoleId))
182:                 .Select(m => m.OrganizationId)
183:                 .ToListAsync();
184:         }
185: 
186:         return orgIds;
187:     }
188: }
````

12:     {
13:         _dbContext = dbContext;
14:     }
15: 
16:     public async Task<List<OrganizationReview>> GetByOrganizationId(Guid organizationId)
17:     {
18:         return await _dbContext.Set<OrganizationReview>()
19:             .AsNoTracking()
20:             .Where(r => r.OrganizationId == organizationId)
21:             .OrderByDescending(r => r.CreatedAt)
22:             .ToListAsync();
23:     }
24: 
25:     public async Task<List<OrganizationReview>> GetByUserId(Guid userId)
26:     {
27:         return await _dbContext.Set<OrganizationReview>()
28:             .AsNoTracking()
29:             .Include(r => r.Event)
30:             .Where(r => r.UserId == userId)
31:             .OrderByDescending(r => r.CreatedAt)
32:             .ToListAsync();
33:     }
34: 
35:     public async Task<bool> HasUserReviewedProgram(Guid userId, Guid programId)
36:     {
37:         return await _dbContext.Set<OrganizationReview>()
38:             .AsNoTracking()
39:             .AnyAsync(r => r.UserId == userId && r.EventId == programId);
40:     }
41: }
````

  6: 
  7: # Event Platform & Management System — v0.1.0 Beta

 29: 
 30: ## ℹ About ISLAMU Event
 31: 
 32: ISLAMU Event is a **self-hostable event discovery and management platform** that helps communities find, organize, and promote events. Built with advanced filtering, verification workflows, and cultural intelligence to serve diverse communities worldwide.
 33: 
 34: > **v0.1.0 Beta** — First public release ready for beta testing. [See what's included →](docs/semantic_versioning/v0.1.0.md)
 35: 
 36: > Give us a Star ⭐️
 37: 
 38: ### Platform Flexibility
 39: - **The software is general-purpose**: Adaptable for any kind of events, communities, and organizations (tech meetups, conferences, workshops, community gatherings)
 40: - **The ISLAMU-hosted instance is Islamic-focused**: Our public instance at [event.openislamu.org](https://event.openislamu.org) is curated for Islamic events and community needs
 41: - **White-label ready**: Rebrand and customize the platform for your specific use case with full control over branding, policies, and features
 42: 
 43: ## ✨ Why ISLAMU Event
 44: 
 45: ### Key Differentiators
 46: 
 47: - **🔐 Security-First:** BFF pattern (no tokens in browser), Cerbos fine-grained authorization, Infisical secrets management
 48: - **🛡️ Verified Organizations:** Two-tier verification system for trust and quality
 49: - **⚡ Multi-Tenancy:** Runtime mode switching (Single-tenant ↔ Multi-tenant) without code changes
 50: - **🔧 Modular Events:** Plugin-style aspects (Islamic, Tech) with per-tenant enablement
 51: - **🎯 Cultural Intelligence:** Advanced filtering based on enabled modules. filter by madhab, gender, age, prayer times, skill level...
 52: - **🏗️ Enterprise Architecture:** Clean Architecture + CQRS with MediatR, REST Level 3 (HATEOAS)
 53: - **🌍 Federation-Ready:** ATProto/ActivityPub data models complete (Phase 1), protocol endpoints planned for 1.0.0
 54: - **🧪 Test Coverage:** 7 test projects (TUnit, bUnit, architecture tests)
 55: - **📖 Open Source:** AGPL-3.0 licensed for transparency and community ownership
 56: 
 57: ---
 58: 
 59: ## 🎯 Core Features (v0.1.0)
 60: 
 61: ### For Event Seekers
 62: 
 63: - **🔍 Advanced Discovery:** 33 query parameters including title search, date range, location radius, categories, tags, and more
 64: - **👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Culturally-Aware Filters:** Age ranges, gender segregation modes, madhab targeting, prayer-relative timing (for instances that enable these modules)
 65: - **🌐 Multi-Language Support:** Event sessions with multiple language options
 66: - **📱 Responsive Design:** Mobile-friendly Blazor UI with MudBlazor components
 67: - **✅ RSVP & Registration:** Waitlists, approval workflows, registration limits per session
 68: 
 69: ### For Event Organizers
 70: 
 71: - **📅 Multi-Session Events:** Conferences, seminars, recurring programs with speakers, agendas, and language variants
 72: - **🛡️ Organization Verification:** Two-tier system (user-submitted vs. verified organizations)
 73: - **👥 Member Management:** Invite members, assign roles (Owner, Admin, Editor, Viewer), track permissions
 74: - **⭐ Reviews & Ratings:** Users can review verified organizations to build trust
 75: - **🎯 Modular Event Types:** Enable Islamic or Tech aspects per event based on tenant configuration
 76: - **📊 Flexible Publishing:** Open registration, approval-required, or invite-only policies
 77: 
 78: ### For Platform Owners
 79: 
 80: - **🐳 Docker-Ready:** One-command deployment with `docker-compose up -d`
 81: - **💼 Multi-Tenancy:** Switch between single-tenant and SaaS modes at runtime without code changes
 82: - **🛠️ White-Label Control:** Custom branding, domains, logos, navigation links, policies per tenant
 83: - **🔧 Admin Hierarchy:** Instance admins, tenant admins, and organization admins with cascading settings
 84: - **🌍 Federation Foundation:** ATProto/ActivityPub data models complete (Phase 1), protocol endpoints planned for 1.0.0
 85: - **📚 Comprehensive Docs:** Architecture, deployment, configuration, troubleshooting, and API reference
 86: - **🔐 Enterprise Security:** BFF pattern, Cerbos authorization, Infisical secrets, HATEOAS REST API
 87: 
 88: ##  Deployment & Hosting Options
 89: 
 90: This platform is designed to be flexible and self-hostable for any organization.
 91: 
 92: - **Single-Instance Mode**: One organization or community per deployment
 93: - **Multi-Tenant SaaS Mode**: Multiple isolated tenants with custom domains and branding
 94: 
 95: See [Operations Guide][operations-doc] for full deployment details and examples.
 96: 
 97: ## 🎨 Branding & Customization
 98: 
 99: ISLAMU Event is built for white-label use:
100: 
101: - **Change instance name and domain**
102: - **Customize logos, colors, and UI**
103: - **Define your own categories, tags, and policies**
104: - **Decide who can publish events and how verification works**
105: 
106: See [Configuration Guide][configuration-doc] for full customization options.
107: 
108: ## 🛡️ Enterprise Security & Compliance
109: 
110: We treat security as a first-class citizen, not an afterthought.
111: 
112: * **Identity & Access:** Managed via **Keycloak**, supporting MFA, Social Login, and SAML/LDAP integration.
113: * **Authorization:** Fine-grained access control (FGAC) powered by **Cerbos**: Policy Decision Point that coordinates unified policy-based authorization, allowing for complex "Who can do what" logic with human readable yaml for non technical users.
114: * **Data Integrity:** All database interactions use **Parameterized EF Core queries** to eliminate SQL injection.
115: * **Secret Management:** Zero hardcoded credentials; all secrets are injected at runtime via **Infisical**.
116: * **Observability:** Integrated **OpenTelemetry** for distributed tracing and real-time security monitoring.
117: 
118: ### Security Features
119: 
120: - **🔒 HTTPS Enforcement:** All traffic encrypted with HSTS
121: - **🔐 Modern Authentication:** OAuth 2.0/OIDC via Keycloak
122: - **🗝️ Secret Management:** Infisical vault for credentials
123: - **🛡️ Authorization:** Policy-based access control via Cerbos
124: - **🔍 Input Validation:** FluentValidation + ASP.NET Core model binding
125: - **🚫 SQL Injection Prevention:** Parameterized queries (EF Core)
126: - **🌐 CORS:** Configurable origin whitelist
127: - **⏱️ Rate Limiting:** ASP.NET Core middleware
128: 
129: ### Extensibility Model
130: 
131: Events use **composition over inheritance**:
132: 
133: ```
134: Event (Core)
135:   ├── IslamicDetails (optional aspect)
136:   ├── TechDetails (optional aspect)
137:   └── EducationalDetails (optional aspect)
138: ```
139: 
140: A "Ramadan Tech Workshop" has both Islamic and Tech aspects. No class explosion.
141: 
142: See [EXTENSIBILITY.md](docs/EXTENSIBILITY.md) and [MODULAR_EVENTS.md](docs/MODULAR_EVENTS.md).

261: ## 🏗️ Technical Overview
262: 
263: ISLAMU Event is built on **Clean Architecture + CQRS** with a **BFF (Backend-for-Frontend)** pattern.
264: 
265: ### Technology Stack (v0.1.0)
266: 
267: | Component | Technology | Purpose |
268: |-----------|------------|---------|
269: | **Runtime** | .NET 10.0 | Latest LTS framework |
270: | **Architecture** | Clean Architecture + CQRS | Layer separation with MediatR |
271: | **Frontend** | Blazor Server + WASM | Hybrid rendering (InteractiveAuto) |
272: | **UI Components** | MudBlazor | Material Design components |
273: | **Database** | PostgreSQL + PostGIS | Relational + spatial queries |
274: | **ORM** | Entity Framework Core 10 | Data access with named query filters |
275: | **Authentication** | Keycloak (OIDC/OAuth 2.0) | Identity provider with BFF pattern |
276: | **Authorization** | Cerbos | Policy Decision Point (PDP) for FGAC |
277: | **Secrets** | Infisical | Vault with auto-refresh + health checks |
278: | **API Docs** | Scalar + Swagger/NSwag | OpenAPI 3.0 with HAL+JSON |
279: | **Logging** | Serilog | Structured logging to Loki |
280: | **Telemetry** | OpenTelemetry | Distributed tracing + Prometheus metrics |
281: | **Orchestration** | .NET Aspire (dev), Docker (prod) | Service orchestration |
282: | **Test Framework** | TUnit + bUnit | Unit + integration + component tests |
283: 
284: ### The Request Lifecycle (CQRS)
285: We utilize **MediatR** for a decoupled command/query pipeline. This ensures that our business logic is isolated from transport layers (API/Blazor).
286: 
287: ```mermaid
288: graph TD
289:     subgraph Client_Layer [Presentation]
290:         A[Blazor WASM / Mobile] -->|HTTPS/REST| B[ASP.NET Core API]
291:     end
292: 
293:     subgraph Application_Layer [Business Logic]
294:         B -->|Command/Query| C[MediatR Pipeline]
295:         C -->|Validation| D[FluentValidation]
296:         D -->|Execution| E[Domain Handler]
297:     end
298: 
299:     subgraph Infrastructure_Layer [Data & Services]
300:         E -->|EF Core| F[(PostgreSQL + PostGIS)]
301:         E -->|OIDC| G[Keycloak]
302:         E -->|Events| H[Svix Webhooks]
303:     end
304: 
305:     E -.->|Future| I[ATProto / ActivityPub Gateway]
306: ```
307: 
308: ```mermaid
309: graph LR
310:     A[Request] --> B[Controller]
311:     B --> C[MediatR]
312:     C --> D[Handler]
313:     D --> E[Repository]
314:     E --> F[(PostgreSQL)]
315:     D --> G[Response]
316: ```
317:

````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: Agents Documentation
  3: description: Documentation file - not an executable agent
  4: disabled: true
  5: ---
  6: 
  7: # Project Agents
  8: 
  9: > **Project-Agnostic Autonomous Agents for Complex Tasks**
 10: >
 11: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
 12: 
 13: Specialized autonomous agents for complex, multi-step tasks in Clean Architecture .NET projects.
 14: 
 15: ---
 16: 
 17: ## Overview
 18: 
 19: Agents are autonomous Claude instances that handle specific complex tasks. Unlike skills (which provide inline guidance), agents:
 20: 
 21: - Run as separate sub-tasks with focused objectives
 22: - Work autonomously with minimal supervision
 23: - Have specialized tool access for their domain
 24: - Return comprehensive reports upon completion
 25:

242: 
243: ## When to Use Agents vs Skills
244: 
245: | Use Agents When... | Use Skills When... |
246: |-------------------|-------------------|
247: | Task requires multiple autonomous steps | Need inline guidance while coding |
248: | Complex analysis is needed | Checking best practices |
249: | Clear end goal exists | Ongoing development work |
250: | Want comprehensive report | Want to maintain control |
251: | **Example**: "Review all controllers" | **Example**: "Creating a new route" |
252: 
253: **Complementary Usage**:
254: - Use a **skill** for patterns during development
255: - Use an **agent** to review the result when complete
256: 
257: ---
258: 
259: ## Creating Custom Agents
260: 
261: Agents are markdown files with YAML frontmatter:
262: 
263: ```markdown
264: ---
265: name: my-custom-agent
266: description: Brief description of the agent's purpose
267: tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob
268: ---
269: 
270: # Agent Name
271: 
272: ## Purpose
273: What this agent accomplishes
274: 
275: ## Instructions
276: Step-by-step instructions for autonomous execution
277: 
278: ## Tools Available
279: - Read: For reading files
280: - Edit: For modifying files
281: - Bash: For running commands
282: 
283: ## Expected Output
284: What format to return results in
285: ```
286: 
287: **Best Practices**:
288: - Be specific in instructions
289: - Break complex tasks into numbered steps
290: - Specify exactly what to return
291: - Include examples of good output
292: - List available tools explicitly
293: 
294: ---
295: 
296: ## Troubleshooting
297: 
298: ### Agent Not Found
299: 
300: Verify the agent file exists:
301: ```powershell
302: Get-ChildItem .claude\agents\agent-name.md
303: ```
304: 
305: ### Agent Fails with Path Errors
306: 
307: Check for hardcoded paths:
308: ```powershell
309: Select-String -Path ".claude\agents\agent-name.md" -Pattern "~/|/root/|/Users/"
310: ```
311: 
312: Fix by replacing with relative paths or `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR`.
313: 
314: ### Agent Returns Incomplete Results
315: 
316: - Ensure the task is well-defined
317: - Break complex tasks into smaller sub-tasks
318: - Provide more context in the initial prompt
319: 
320: ---
321: 
322: ## Related Documentation
323: 
324: - [`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) - System architecture overview
325: - [`docs/QUICK_REFERENCE.md`](../../docs/QUICK_REFERENCE.md) - Critical rules and patterns
326: - [`.claude/skills/`](../skills/) - Inline guidance skills
````

## File: .claude/agents/refactor-planner.md
````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: refactor-planner
  3: description: Creates strategic refactoring plans to modernize legacy code, clean up technical debt, and enforce Clean Architecture in {Project}.
  4: tools: All tools
  5: ---
  6: 
  7: > **Project-Agnostic Refactoring Strategy Agent**
  8: >
  9: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
 10: 
 11: You are a **Technical Strategist** for the {Project} platform. You create comprehensive refactoring plans that transform disorganized code into Clean Architecture-compliant structures without breaking the build.
 12: 
 13: ## Technology Stack
 14: 
 15: - **.NET**: 10.0
 16: - **Language**: C# 13
 17: - **Architecture**: Clean Architecture with CQRS
 18: - **Frontend**: Blazor Server + WebAssembly (Hybrid)
 19: - **Database**: Entity Framework Core + PostgreSQL
 20: 
 21: ## CRITICAL RULES (Must Enforce in Refactoring)
 22: 
 23: These rules are strictly enforced during any refactoring effort. Violations **MUST** be addressed. For detailed explanations and examples, refer to the respective skills.
 24: 
 25: 1.  **Repositories Return ENTITIES, Never DTOs**: Repositories **MUST** return domain entities. DTO mapping always happens in the Application layer handlers via AutoMapper.
 26:     -   **Reference**: `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` (repository return types), `dotnet-efcore-guidelines` (repository pattern).
 27: 2.  **Validators Use Manual Instantiation (NOT DI)**: Validators are instantiated manually within handlers, with all required dependencies passed to their constructor. They are **NOT** injected via Dependency Injection.
 28:     -   **Reference**: `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` (validation integration), `clean-architecture-rules` (manual validator instantiation).
 29: 3.  **Navigation Properties Are Readonly**: Navigation properties on link/mapping tables are **readonly for queries only**. Writes **MUST** go through the link table's repository directly.
 30:     -   **Reference**: `dotnet-efcore-guidelines` (key principles & conventions).
 31: 4.  **Use `int` Instead of `long`**: Unless explicitly required for large values (e.g., file sizes, pagination cursors), use `int` for lookup table IDs and `Guid` for main entities.
 32:     -   **Reference**: `dotnet-efcore-guidelines` (key principles & conventions).
 33: 5.  **No Default Values in Entities**: **DO NOT** add default values in domain entity property initializers. Defaults are set in application handlers or via `IEntityTypeConfiguration`.
 34:     -   **Reference**: `dotnet-efcore-guidelines` (key principles & conventions).
 35: 6.  **Commands Return `BaseCommandResponse<Guid>`**: All commands (write operations) **MUST** return `BaseCommandResponse<Guid>` (or `bool` for delete operations).
 36:     -   **Reference**: `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` (command patterns).
 37: 7.  **GET = AllowAnonymous, Write = Authorize**: **`GET`** endpoints should be `[AllowAnonymous]`. **`POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`** endpoints **MUST** be `[Authorize]`.
 38:     -   **Reference**: `auth-patterns` (controller endpoint authorization).
 39: 8.  **Extract User ID with Fallback**: When extracting the user ID from JWT claims, **ALWAYS** use the provided fallback pattern (`sub` → `nameidentifier` → `sid`).
 40:     -   **Reference**: `auth-patterns` (user ID extraction).
 41: 9.  **File-Scoped Namespaces**: All new C# files **SHOULD** use file-scoped namespaces for conciseness.
 42: 10. **Do Not Remove Using Statements**: Keep ALL `using` statements even if they appear unused, except for old references that are broken.
 43: 
 44: ## Refactoring Scope Analysis
 45: 
 46: The first step in planning any refactoring is to identify the current state and the desired target state, leveraging the established architectural patterns.
 47: 
 48: ### Identifying Problem Areas
 49: 
 50: Analyze the current codebase to pinpoint common architectural violations. For detailed identification strategies, refer to the `code-architecture-reviewer` agent.
 51: 
 52: -   **Fat Controllers**: Controllers containing significant business logic or direct `DbContext` access.
 53:     -   **Target State**: Thin controllers using MediatR. Refer to `clean-architecture-rules` (layer responsibilities) and `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` (controller usage).
 54: -   **Wrong Validator Pattern**: Validators injected via DI rather than manually instantiated.
 55:     -   **Target State**: Manual validator instantiation in handlers. Refer to `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` (validation integration) and `clean-architecture-rules` (manual validator instantiation).
 56: -   **Repository Returns DTOs**: Repositories performing mapping or returning DTOs instead of domain entities.
 57:     -   **Target State**: Repositories returning entities, handlers mapping to DTOs. Refer to `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` (repository usage) and `dotnet-efcore-guidelines` (repository pattern).
 58: -   **Missing Authorization**: Write endpoints lacking `[Authorize]` or proper resource-level checks.
 59:     -   **Target State**: Consistent endpoint authorization and handler-level resource checks. Refer to `auth-patterns`.
 60: 
 61: ## Phased Execution Plan
 62: 
 63: Refactoring should be approached incrementally to minimize risk and allow for continuous verification. Each phase should result in a stable, tested codebase.
 64: 
 65: ### Phase 1: Create Abstractions (Non-Breaking)
 66: 
 67: **Goal**: Introduce new Clean Architecture-compliant components without altering existing functionality.
 68: -   [ ] Create MediatR Commands/Queries for existing controller actions.
 69: -   [ ] Create Handlers for these Commands/Queries, ensuring manual validator instantiation.
 70: -   [ ] Ensure existing repository methods in `{Project}.Persistence` return domain entities.
 71: 
 72: **Risk Level**: 🟢 Low (focus on non-breaking additions)
 73: 
 74: ### Phase 2: Switch Implementation
 75: 
 76: **Goal**: Transition existing code to use the newly created abstractions.
 77: -   [ ] Update Controllers to use MediatR for handling requests.
 78: -   [ ] Apply `[AllowAnonymous]` to `GET` endpoints and `[Authorize]` to `POST`/`PUT`/`DELETE` endpoints.
 79: -   [ ] Implement user ID extraction with the fallback pattern in controllers or custom middleware.
 80: 
 81: **Risk Level**: 🟡 Medium (requires thorough testing)
 82: 
 83: ### Phase 3: Cleanup
 84: 
 85: **Goal**: Remove old, deprecated code after the new implementation is proven stable and thoroughly tested.
 86: -   [ ] Remove direct `DbContext` usage from controllers.
 87: -   [ ] Delete old service classes, repositories, or DTOs that have been replaced.
 88: -   [ ] Remove any unused DI registrations.
 89: 
 90: **Risk Level**: 🟢 Low (already tested in Phase 2)
 91: 
 92: ## Risk Assessment & Rollback Plan
 93: 
 94: Each refactoring plan should include a basic risk assessment and a clear rollback strategy.
 95: 
 96: ### Risk Assessment
 97: 
 98: Analyze potential risks associated with the refactoring. For each risk, propose mitigation strategies.
 99: 
100: | Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
101: |------|------------|--------|------------|
102: | **Breaking existing API clients** | Low | High | Ensure API contract remains unchanged (internal refactor only). |
103: | **Validation errors not caught** | Medium | High | Implement manual validators with full FK repo checks (refer `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`). |
104: | **Repository returning wrong type** | Medium | High | Review all repository methods return entities (refer `dotnet-efcore-guidelines`). |
105: | **Missing authorization** | Low | High | Add `[Authorize]` to all write endpoints (refer `auth-patterns`). |
106: | **UserId extraction fails** | Medium | Medium | Use fallback pattern (`sub` → `nameidentifier` → `sid`) (refer `auth-patterns`). |
107: | **Performance regression (N+1)** | Medium | High | Implement eager loading (`Include`) or projections (refer `dotnet-efcore-guidelines`). |
108: 
109: ### Rollback Plan (PowerShell Example)
110: 
111: In case a phase introduces critical issues, a quick rollback is essential.
112: 
113: ```powershell
114: # If Phase X fails, revert the last commit
115: git revert HEAD --no-edit
116: 
117: # Rebuild the solution
118: dotnet build {Project}.sln
119: 
120: # Re-run the application with Aspire
121: dotnet run --project {Project}.AppHost
122: ```
123: 
124: ## Testing Strategy
125: 
126: Each phase **MUST** be thoroughly tested.
127: 
128: -   **Unit Tests**: Verify individual components (handlers, validators) in isolation.
129: -   **Integration Tests**: Test the full flow from controller to database.
130: -   **Manual API Tests**: Use PowerShell `Invoke-RestMethod` to verify endpoints.
131: -   **Test Coverage**: Aim for high code coverage for refactored components.
132: -   **Reference**: `error-tracking` skill for overall testing guidelines.
133: 
134: ## Deliverable Format
135: 
136: ```markdown
137: # Refactoring Plan: [Module/Feature Name]
138: 
139: **Date**: YYYY-MM-DD
140: **Author**: Claude Code
141: **Estimated Duration**: [X hours/days]
142: 
143: ---
144: 
145: ## Executive Summary
146: 
147: **Current State**: [Brief description of the problem/technical debt being addressed.]
148: **Target State**: [Brief description of the desired Clean Architecture-compliant structure.]
149: **Business Value**: [Explain why this refactoring is important (e.g., improved maintainability, testability, performance).]
150: 
151: ---
152: 
153: ## CRITICAL RULES Checklist (Pre-Refactoring Check)
154: 
155: Before proceeding, ensure the refactoring plan explicitly addresses these critical rules. If not, the plan requires revision.
156: 
157: - [ ] Repositories return entities (not DTOs) - See `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`, `dotnet-efcore-guidelines`
158: - [ ] Validators use manual instantiation (not DI) - See `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`, `clean-architecture-rules`
159: - [ ] Commands return BaseCommandResponse<Guid> - See `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`
160: - [ ] GET = AllowAnonymous, Write = Authorize - See `auth-patterns`
161: - [ ] UserId extraction with fallback pattern - See `auth-patterns`
162: - [ ] Use int instead of long (except size/cursor) - See `dotnet-efcore-guidelines`
163: - [ ] No default values in entities - See `dotnet-efcore-guidelines`
164: - [ ] Navigation properties are readonly (link tables) - See `dotnet-efcore-guidelines`
165: - [ ] File-scoped namespaces used - See `clean-architecture-rules` (though not explicit)
166: - [ ] Keep all using statements - See `code-refactor-master` (though not explicit)
167: 
168: ---
169: 
170: ## Current State Analysis: Problem Areas Identified
171: 
172: List the specific code sections or patterns that require refactoring.
173: 
174: 1.  **[Problem Title]**: [Brief description of the problem, e.g., "Fat Controller: {Entity}Controller contains direct DbContext calls and business logic"].
175:     -   **Violation**: [Reference violated critical rule or architectural principle, e.g., "Violates Clean Architecture's separation of concerns. See `clean-architecture-rules` (layer responsibilities)."]
176:     -   **Impact**: [e.g., "High coupling, low testability, difficult to maintain."]
177:     -   **Code Snippet (Current)**: (Optional: provide small, relevant snippet)
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## Target Architecture
182: 
183: Provide a high-level overview or diagram of the desired structure after refactoring.
184: 
185: ```
186: Controller (Thin)
187: └─> MediatR Command/Query (Application Layer)
188:     └─> Handler (Application Layer)
189:         ├─> Manual Validator Instantiation
190:         ├─> Repository (returns entities)
191:         └─> AutoMapper (handler maps to DTOs)
192: ```
193: -   **Reference**: `clean-architecture-rules`, `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`, `dotnet-efcore-guidelines`.
194: 
195: ---
196: 
197: ## Phased Execution Plan
198: 
199: Detailed steps for each phase, focusing on incremental changes and verification.
200: 
201: ### Phase 1: Create Abstractions (Non-Breaking)
202: 
203: -   **Objective**: Introduce MediatR commands/queries, handlers, and ensure repositories return entities without changing existing controller logic.
204: -   **Steps**:
205:     1.  Create `Create{Entity}Command` and `{Entity}Dto` in `{Project}.Application`.
206:     2.  Create `{Entity}CommandHandler` in `{Project}.Application`, implementing manual validator instantiation and using repository interfaces.
207:     3.  Ensure existing repository methods in `{Project}.Persistence` return domain entities.
208: -   **Verification**: `dotnet build`, `dotnet test` (for new unit tests).
209: -   **Risk Level**: 🟢 Low (non-breaking additions).
210: 
211: ### Phase 2: Switch Implementation
212: 
213: -   **Objective**: Update existing controllers to utilize the new MediatR abstractions.
214: -   **Steps**:
215:     1.  Modify `{Entity}Controller` to inject `IMediator`.
216:     2.  Replace direct `DbContext` calls/business logic with `await _mediator.Send(command/query)`.
217:     3.  Apply `[AllowAnonymous]` to `GET` endpoints and `[Authorize]` to `POST`/`PUT`/`DELETE` endpoints.
218:     4.  Implement user ID extraction with the fallback pattern.
219: -   **Verification**: `dotnet build`, `dotnet test`, manual API testing via PowerShell `Invoke-RestMethod`.
220: -   **Risk Level**: 🟡 Medium (requires thorough testing).
221: 
222: ### Phase 3: Cleanup
223: 
224: -   **Objective**: Remove old, deprecated code after the new implementation is proven stable and thoroughly tested.
225: -   **Steps**:
226:     1.  Remove old, direct `DbContext` usage and related DTOs/services from controllers.
227:     2.  Remove any unused DI registrations.
228:     3.  Run code analysis tools (`dotnet format --verify-no-changes`).
229: -   **Verification**: `dotnet clean`, `dotnet build`, `dotnet test`.
230: -   **Risk Level**: 🟢 Low (already tested in Phase 2).
231: 
232: ---
233: 
234: ## Testing Commands (PowerShell)
235: 
236: ```powershell
237: # Build the solution
238: dotnet build {Project}.sln
239: 
240: # Run all tests
241: dotnet test
242: 
243: # Run the application with Aspire (for integration testing/manual testing)
244: dotnet run --project {Project}.AppHost
245: 
246: # Check API logs for runtime errors
247: $today = Get-Date -Format "yyyyMMdd"

249: ```
250: 
251: ---
252: 
253: ## Success Criteria
254: 
255: - [ ] All automated tests passing.
256: - [ ] No breaking changes to existing API contracts (unless explicitly planned).
257: - [ ] All handlers use manual validator instantiation.
258: - [ ] All repositories return entities.
259: - [ ] Controllers are thin, mediating requests to MediatR.
260: - [ ] Endpoint authorization (`[AllowAnonymous]`, `[Authorize]`) is correctly applied.
261: - [ ] User ID extraction uses the fallback pattern.
262:

268: - [`cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`](../skills/cqrs-mediatr-guidelines/SKILL.md) - **CRITICAL**: CQRS patterns, handler logic, validation, DTO mapping.

## File: .claude/skills/clean-architecture-rules/resources/dependency-rules.md
````markdown
  1: # Dependency Rules - Complete Reference
  2: 
  3: > **Project-Agnostic Dependency Rules**
  4: >
  5: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
  6: 
  7: ## Dependency Matrix
  8: 
  9: | Layer | Can Reference | Cannot Reference | Framework Dependencies Allowed |
 10: |-------|---------------|------------------|-------------------------------|
 11: | **{Project}.Domain** | Nothing | Everything | None (pure C#) |
 12: | **{Project}.Application** | Domain | Infrastructure, Persistence, API, Blazor | MediatR, FluentValidation, AutoMapper |
 13: | **{Project}.Persistence** | Application, Domain | API, Blazor | EF Core, Database Provider, PostGIS |
 14: | **{Project}.Infrastructure** | Application, Domain | API, Blazor | Any (email, file storage, external APIs) |
 15: | **{Project}.API** | All | None (top layer) | ASP.NET Core, Swashbuckle, Serilog |
 16: | **{Project}.Blazor** | All | None (top layer) | Blazor, MudBlazor, SignalR |
 17: | **{Project}.Blazor.Client** | Shared DTOs | Server components | Blazor WebAssembly, MudBlazor |
 18: 
 19: ## Visual Dependency Flow
 20: 
 21: ```mermaid
 22: graph TD
 23:     subgraph Presentation Layer
 24:         A[{Project}.API]
 25:         B[{Project}.Blazor]
 26:     end
 27: 
 28:     subgraph Infrastructure Layer
 29:         C[{Project}.Persistence]
 30:         D[{Project}.Infrastructure]
 31:     end
 32: 
 33:     subgraph Application Layer
 34:         E[{Project}.Application]
 35:     end
 36: 
 37:     subgraph Domain Layer
 38:         F[{Project}.Domain]
 39:     end
 40: 
 41:     A --> E
 42:     A --> C
 43:     A --> D
 44: 
 45:     B --> E
 46:     B --> C
 47:     B --> D
 48: 
 49:     C --> E
 50:     C --> F
 51: 
 52:     D --> E
 53:     D --> F
 54: 
 55:     E --> F
 56: 
 57:     style A fill:#fbe5c5,stroke:#333
 58:     style B fill:#fbe5c5,stroke:#333
 59:     style C fill:#c5fbe5,stroke:#333
 60:     style D fill:#c5fbe5,stroke:#333
 61:     style E fill:#e5c5fb,stroke:#333
 62:     style F fill:#c5fbc5,stroke:#333
 63: ```
 64: 
 65: ## The Dependency Inversion Principle (DIP)
 66: 
 67: **Core Idea**: High-level modules should not depend on low-level modules. Both should depend on abstractions.
 68: 
 69: ### Example: Application needs Database Access
 70: 
 71: **❌ WITHOUT Dependency Inversion** (Violation):
 72: ```
 73: Application ──────> Infrastructure
 74: (high-level)        (low-level, concrete)
 75: 
 76: Create{Entity}CommandHandler → {DbContext}
 77: ```
 78: *Problem*: Application layer depends on concrete Infrastructure implementation.
 79: 
 80: **✅ WITH Dependency Inversion** (Correct):
 81: ```
 82: Application ──────> I{Entity}Repository (Interface)
 83:                            ▲
 84:                            │ implements
 85: Infrastructure ────────────┘
 86: {Entity}Repository (implements I{Entity}Repository)
 87: ```
 88: *Solution*: Both depend on abstraction (interface) defined in Application.
 89: 
 90: ## Allowed `using` Statements by Layer
 91: 
 92: ### {Project}.Domain
 93: 
 94: ```csharp
 95: // File: {Project}.Domain/{Entity}.cs
 96: namespace {Project}.Domain;
 97: 
 98: // ✅ ALLOWED - Pure C# only
 99: using System;
100: using System.Collections.Generic;
101: using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations.Schema;
102: 
103: public class {Entity}
104: {
105:     public {IdType} Id { get; set; }
106: 
107:     [ForeignKey("{LookupEntity}")]
108:     public {LookupIdType} {LookupEntity}Id { get; set; }
109:     public {LookupEntity} {LookupEntity} { get; set; }
110: 
111:     [ForeignKey("{RelatedEntity}")]
112:     public {IdType} {RelatedEntity}Id { get; set; }
113:     public {RelatedEntity} {RelatedEntity} { get; set; }
114: 
115:     // ... more navigation properties
116: }
117: 
118: // ❌ NOT ALLOWED in Domain
119: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;           // Infrastructure concern
120: using {Project}.Application;                   // Layer above
121: using {Project}.Infrastructure;                // Layer above
122: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;                // Presentation concern
123: using MediatR;                                 // Application concern
124: ```
125: 
126: ### {Project}.Application
127: 
128: ```csharp
129: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Handlers/Commands/Create{Entity}CommandHandler.cs
130: namespace {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Handlers.Commands;
131: 
132: // ✅ ALLOWED
133: using System;
134: using System.Collections.Generic;
135: using System.Linq;
136: using System.Threading;
137: using System.Threading.Tasks;
138: using AutoMapper;                                       // Application framework
139: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;     // Same layer
140: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity};             // Same layer
141: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity}.Validators;  // Same layer
142: using {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Commands;  // Same layer
143: using {Project}.Application.Responses;                 // Same layer
144: using {Project}.Domain;                                // Domain entities
145: using MediatR;                                         // CQRS framework
146: 
147: // ❌ NOT ALLOWED
148: using {Project}.Persistence;                   // Infrastructure layer
149: using {Project}.Infrastructure;                // Infrastructure layer
150: using {Project}.API;                           // Presentation layer
151: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;           // Infrastructure concern
152: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;                // Presentation concern
153: ```
154: 
155: ### {Project}.Persistence
156: 
157: ```csharp
158: // File: {Project}.Persistence/Repositories/{Entity}Repository.cs
159: namespace {Project}.Persistence.Repositories;
160: 
161: // ✅ ALLOWED
162: using System;
163: using System.Collections.Generic;
164: using System.Linq;
165: using System.Threading.Tasks;
166: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;     // Application interfaces
167: using {Project}.Domain;                                // Domain entities
168: using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore;                   // ORM framework
169: 
170: // ❌ NOT ALLOWED
171: using {Project}.API;                           // Presentation layer
172: using {Project}.Blazor;                        // Presentation layer
173: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;                // Presentation concern
174: ```
175: 
176: ### {Project}.Infrastructure
177: 
178: ```csharp
179: // File: {Project}.Infrastructure/Email/EmailService.cs
180: namespace {Project}.Infrastructure.Email;
181: 
182: // ✅ ALLOWED
183: using {Project}.Domain;                                   // Domain entities
184: using {Project}.Application.Contracts.Infrastructure;     // Application interfaces
185: using SendGrid;                                           // External service
186: using Azure.Storage.Blobs;                                // External service
187: 
188: // ❌ NOT ALLOWED
189: using {Project}.API;                           // Presentation layer
190: using {Project}.Blazor;                        // Presentation layer
191: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;                // Presentation concern
192: ```
193: 
194: ### {Project}.API
195: 
196: ```csharp
197: // File: {Project}.API/Controllers/{Entity}Controller.cs
198: namespace {Project}.API.Controllers;
199: 
200: // ✅ ALLOWED (Everything)
201: using System;
202: using System.Collections.Generic;
203: using System.Linq;
204: using System.Security.Claims;
205: using System.Threading.Tasks;
206: using {Project}.Application.DTOs.{Entity};                          // DTOs
207: using {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Commands;
208: using {Project}.Application.Features.{Entities}.Requests.Queries;
209: using {Project}.Application.Responses;                              // Response wrappers
210: using MediatR;                                                      // CQRS
211: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization;                           // Auth
212: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Http;                                    // HTTP context
213: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc;                                     // Controllers
214: // ... any other dependencies
215: ```
216: 
217: ## Project Reference Rules (.csproj)
218: 
219: ### {Project}.Domain.csproj
220: ```xml
221: <Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
222:   <PropertyGroup>
223:     <TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>
224:   </PropertyGroup>
225: 
226:   <!-- ✅ NO PROJECT REFERENCES -->
227:   <ItemGroup>
228:     <!-- Only System.ComponentModel.Annotations for [ForeignKey] -->
229:     <PackageReference Include="System.ComponentModel.Annotations" Version="10.0.0" />
230:   </ItemGroup>
231: </Project>
232: ```
233: 
234: ### {Project}.Application.csproj
235: ```xml
236: <Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
237:   <ItemGroup>
238:     <!-- ✅ ALLOWED: Reference to Domain -->
239:     <ProjectReference Include="..\{Project}.Domain\{Project}.Domain.csproj" />
240:   </ItemGroup>
241: 
242:   <ItemGroup>
243:     <!-- ✅ ALLOWED: Framework packages -->
244:     <PackageReference Include="MediatR" Version="12.4.0" />
245:     <PackageReference Include="FluentValidation" Version="11.9.0" />
246:     <PackageReference Include="AutoMapper" Version="13.0.1" />
247:   </ItemGroup>
248: 
249:   <!-- ❌ NOT ALLOWED: References to Infrastructure, Persistence, API, Blazor -->
250: </Project>
251: ```
252: 
253: ### {Project}.Persistence.csproj
254: ```xml
255: <Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk">
256:   <ItemGroup>
257:     <!-- ✅ ALLOWED: References to Domain and Application -->
258:     <ProjectReference Include="..\{Project}.Domain\{Project}.Domain.csproj" />
259:     <ProjectReference Include="..\{Project}.Application\{Project}.Application.csproj" />
260:   </ItemGroup>
261: 
262:   <ItemGroup>
263:     <!-- ✅ ALLOWED: EF Core and database packages -->
264:     <PackageReference Include="Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore" Version="10.0.0" />
265:     <PackageReference Include="Npgsql.EntityFrameworkCore.PostgreSQL" Version="10.0.0" />
266:   </ItemGroup>
267: </Project>
268: ```
269: 
270: ### {Project}.API.csproj
271: ```xml
272: <Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web">
273:   <ItemGroup>
274:     <!-- ✅ ALLOWED: References to ALL -->
275:     <ProjectReference Include="..\{Project}.Application\{Project}.Application.csproj" />
276:     <ProjectReference Include="..\{Project}.Infrastructure\{Project}.Infrastructure.csproj" />
277:     <ProjectReference Include="..\{Project}.Persistence\{Project}.Persistence.csproj" />
278:   </ItemGroup>
279: </Project>
280: ```
281: 
282: ## Verification Commands
283: 
284: ### Check Project References
285: ```bash
286: # Domain should have NO project references
287: dotnet list {Project}.Domain/{Project}.Domain.csproj reference
288: 
289: # Application should ONLY reference Domain
290: dotnet list {Project}.Application/{Project}.Application.csproj reference
291: 
292: # Persistence should reference Domain + Application
293: dotnet list {Project}.Persistence/{Project}.Persistence.csproj reference
294: ```
295: 
296: ### Search for Violations
297: ```bash
298: # Find prohibited using statements in Domain
299: rg "using (Microsoft\.(EntityFrameworkCore|AspNetCore)|{Project}\.(Application|Infrastructure|API|Blazor))" {Project}.Domain/
300: 
301: # Find validation annotations in Domain (except [ForeignKey])
302: rg "\[Required\]|\[MaxLength\]|\[Range\]|\[StringLength\]" {Project}.Domain/
303: ```
304: 
305: ## Common Questions
306: 
307: ### Q: Can Domain use System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations?
308: **A**: LIMITED USE. Only `[ForeignKey]` is acceptable for EF Core relationships. Avoid `[Required]`, `[MaxLength]`, `[Range]` etc.
309: 
310: ```csharp
311: // File: {Project}.Domain/{Entity}.cs
312: public class {Entity}
313: {
314:     public {IdType} Id { get; set; }
315: 
316:     // ✅ OK - Specifies foreign key relationship
317:     [ForeignKey("{LookupEntity}")]
318:     public {LookupIdType} {LookupEntity}Id { get; set; }
319:     public {LookupEntity} {LookupEntity} { get; set; }
320: 
321:     // ❌ NOT OK - Validation annotations
322:     // [Required]
323:     // [MaxLength(200)]
324:     public string Title { get; set; } = string.Empty;
325: }
326: ```
327: 
328: **Why**: `[ForeignKey]` is metadata for EF Core navigation, not validation. Use FluentValidation in Application layer for validation rules.
329: 
330: ### Q: Can Application use AutoMapper?
331: **A**: ✅ YES. AutoMapper is an Application-layer concern for mapping Domain entities to DTOs.
332: 
333: ```csharp
334: // File: {Project}.Application/Features/{Entities}/Handlers/Queries/Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler.cs
335: public class Get{Entity}ListRequestHandler : IRequestHandler<Get{Entity}ListRequest, List<{Entity}ListDto>>
336: {
337:     private readonly I{Entity}Repository _{entity}Repository;
338:     private readonly IMapper _mapper;
339: 
340:     public async Task<List<{Entity}ListDto>> Handle(Get{Entity}ListRequest request, CancellationToken cancellationToken)
341:     {
342:         var {entities} = await _{entity}Repository.Get{Entities}WithDetails();  // Returns List<{Entity}>
343:         return _mapper.Map<List<{Entity}ListDto>>({entities});  // ✅ Maps to DTOs
344:     }
345: }
346: ```
347: 
348: ### Q: Can Application reference EF Core for IQueryable?
349: **A**: ❌ NO. Define repository interfaces that return `Task<List<T>>` instead. Let Infrastructure handle IQueryable.
350: 
351: **Correct Pattern**:
352: ```csharp
353: // File: {Project}.Application/Contracts/Persistence/I{Entity}Repository.cs
354: namespace {Project}.Application.Contracts.Persistence;
355: 
356: public interface I{Entity}Repository : IGenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>
357: {
358:     Task<{Entity}?> Get{Entity}WithDetails({IdType} id);
359:     Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails();  // ✅ Returns List<{Entity}>, not IQueryable
360: }
361: 
362: // File: {Project}.Persistence/Repositories/{Entity}Repository.cs
363: public class {Entity}Repository : GenericRepository<{Entity}, {IdType}>, I{Entity}Repository
364: {
365:     public async Task<List<{Entity}>> Get{Entities}WithDetails()
366:     {
367:         return await _dbContext.{Entities}  // ✅ EF Core IQueryable handled here
368:             .Include(e => e.{LookupEntity})
369:             .Include(e => e.{RelatedEntity})
370:             .ToListAsync();  // ✅ Materializes to List
371:     }
372: }
373: ```
374: 
375: ### Q: Where do I put Email sending logic?
376: **A**:
377: - **Interface**: `{Project}.Application/Contracts/Infrastructure/IEmailService.cs`
378: - **Implementation**: `{Project}.Infrastructure/Services/EmailService.cs`
379: - **Usage**: Application layer uses `IEmailService`, Infrastructure provides concrete implementation
380: 
381: ### Q: Can Blazor.Client reference Persistence?
382: **A**: ❌ NO. Blazor.Client runs in the browser (WebAssembly) and cannot access databases directly. Use shared DTOs and API calls.
383: 
384: **Correct Pattern**:
385: ```csharp
386: // Shared DTO in {Project}.Application
387: public record {Entity}ListDto
388: {
389:     public {IdType} Id { get; set; }
390:     public string Title { get; set; } = string.Empty;
391:     public string {LookupEntity}Name { get; set; } = string.Empty;
392: }
393: 
394: // API endpoint in {Project}.API
395: [HttpGet]
396: [AllowAnonymous]
397: public async Task<ActionResult<List<{Entity}ListDto>>> GetAll()
398: {
399:     var {entities} = await _mediator.Send(new Get{Entity}ListRequest());
400:     return Ok({entities});
401: }
402: 
403: // Blazor.Client calls API
404: @inject HttpClient Http
405: 
406: var {entities} = await Http.GetFromJsonAsync<List<{Entity}ListDto>>("/api/{entity}");
407: ```
408: 
409: ---
410:
