  38: 
  39: ---
  40: 
  41: ## 1. Overview
  42: 
  43: The `{Project}.API` is a stateless REST API built on ASP.NET Core, following Clean Architecture and CQRS patterns.
  44: 
  45: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
  46: 
  47: - **API Project**: `Explore.API`
  48: - **Technology**: ASP.NET Core 10.0
  49: - **Architecture**: Clean Architecture + CQRS + MediatR
  50: 
  51: ### Key Characteristics
  52: 
  53: | Aspect | Implementation |
  54: |--------|----------------|
  55: | Framework | ASP.NET Core 10.0 |
  56: | Architecture | Clean Architecture + CQRS |
  57: | Authentication | JWT Bearer (Keycloak) |
  58: | Documentation | OpenAPI 3.0 (Scalar + Swagger) |
  59: | Versioning | URL path (`/api/`) |
  60: | Serialization | System.Text.Json |
  61: 
  62: ### Request Flow
  63: 
  64: ```
  65: HTTP Request → Controller → MediatR → Handler → Repository → Entity → DTO → Response
  66: ```
  67: 
  68: ---
  69: 
  70: ## 2. Base URL & Versioning
  71: 
  72: ### Development URLs
  73: 
  74: | Service | URL |
  75: |---------|-----|
  76: | API | `https://localhost:7001` |
  77: | Scalar Docs | `https://localhost:7001/scalar/v1` |
  78: | Swagger UI | `https://localhost:7001/swagger` |
  79: | OpenAPI JSON | `https://localhost:7001/openapi/v1.json` |
  80: 
  81: ### URL Structure
  82: 
  83: **Generic Pattern:**
  84: ```
  85: /api/{resource}
  86: /api/{resource}/{id}
  87: /api/{resource}/{id}/{subresource}
  88: ```
  89: 
  90: **Generic Examples:**
  91: - `GET /api/{entity}` - List entities
  92: - `GET /api/{entity}/{id}` - Get entity details
  93: - `GET /api/{childEntity}/by-{parentEntity}/{parentId}` - Get children
  94: - `POST /api/{entity}` - Create entity
  95: 
  96: ### Implementation Examples: ISLAMU Event
  97: - `GET /api/event` - List events
  98: - `GET /api/event/{id}` - Get event details
  99: - `GET /api/eventsession/by-event/{eventId}` - Get sessions for event
 100: - `POST /api/organization` - Create organization
 101: 
 102: ---
 103: 
 104: ## 3. Controller Conventions
 105: 
 106: ### Standard Controller Structure
 107: 
 108: **Generic Template:**
 109: 
 110: ```csharp
 111: [Route("api/[controller]")]
 112: [ApiController]
 113: public class {Entity}Controller : ControllerBase
 114: {
 115:     private readonly IMediator _mediator;
 116:     private readonly IHttpContextAccessor _httpContextAccessor;
 117:     private readonly ILogger<{Entity}Controller> _logger;
 118: 
 119:     public {Entity}Controller(
 120:         IMediator mediator,
 121:         IHttpContextAccessor httpContextAccessor,
 122:         ILogger<{Entity}Controller> logger)
 123:     {
 124:         _mediator = mediator;
 125:         _httpContextAccessor = httpContextAccessor;
 126:         _logger = logger;
 127:     }
 128: }
 129: ```
 130: 
 131: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
 132: 
 133: ```csharp
 134: [Route("api/[controller]")]
 135: [ApiController]
 136: public class EventController : ControllerBase
 137: {
 138:     private readonly IMediator _mediator;
 139:     private readonly IHttpContextAccessor _httpContextAccessor;
 140:     private readonly ILogger<EventController> _logger;
 141: 
 142:     public EventController(
 143:         IMediator mediator,
 144:         IHttpContextAccessor httpContextAccessor,
 145:         ILogger<EventController> logger)
 146:     {
 147:         _mediator = mediator;
 148:         _httpContextAccessor = httpContextAccessor;
 149:         _logger = logger;
 150:     }
 151: }
 152: ```
 153: 
 154: ### CRUD Operations
 155: 
 156: | Operation | HTTP Method | Route | Auth | Returns |
 157: |-----------|-------------|-------|------|---------|
 158: | List | `GET` | `/` | `[AllowAnonymous]` | `PaginatedResult<{Entity}ListDto>` |
 159: | Get | `GET` | `/{id}` | `[AllowAnonymous]` | `{Entity}Dto` |
 160: | Create | `POST` | `/` | `[Authorize]` | `BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>` |
 161: | Update | `PUT` | `/{id}` | `[Authorize]` | `BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>` |
 162: | Delete | `DELETE` | `/{id}` | `[Authorize]` | `NoContent` or `NotFound` |
 163: 
 164: ### Thin Controllers
 165: 
 166: Controllers should be thin - they only:
 167: 1. Extract data from HTTP request
 168: 2. Send command/query to MediatR
 169: 3. Return appropriate HTTP response
 170: 
 171: **Generic Template:**
 172: 
 173: ```csharp
 174: [HttpPost]
 175: [Authorize]
 176: public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>> Create([FromBody] Create{Entity}Dto dto)
 177: {
 178:     var command = new Create{Entity}Command { {Entity}Dto = dto };
 179:     var response = await _mediator.Send(command);
 180: 
 181:     if (!response.Success)
 182:     {
 183:         return BadRequest(response);
 184:     }
 185: 
 186:     return Ok(response);
 187: }
 188: ```
 189: 
 190: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
 191: 
 192: ```csharp
 193: [HttpPost]
 194: [Authorize]
 195: public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<Guid>>> Create([FromBody] CreateEventDto dto)
 196: {
 197:     var command = new CreateEventCommand { EventDto = dto };
 198:     var response = await _mediator.Send(command);
 199: 
 200:     if (!response.Success)
 201:     {
 202:         return BadRequest(response);
 203:     }
 204: 
 205:     return Ok(response);
 206: }
 207: ```
 208: 
 209: ---
 210: 
 211: ## 4. Authentication & Authorization
 212: 
 213: ### JWT Bearer Authentication
 214: 
 215: The API uses JWT Bearer tokens issued by Keycloak:
 216: 
 217: ```csharp
 218: // In Program.cs
 219: builder.Services.AddAuthentication(JwtBearerDefaults.AuthenticationScheme)
 220:     .AddJwtBearer(options =>
 221:     {
 222:         options.Authority = builder.Configuration["Keycloak:Authority"];
 223:         options.Audience = builder.Configuration["Keycloak:Audience"];
 224:         options.RequireHttpsMetadata = false; // Dev only
 225:     });
 226: ```
 227: 
 228: ### Authorization Patterns
 229: 
 230: **Read Operations** - Public access:
 231: ```csharp
 232: [HttpGet]
 233: [AllowAnonymous]
 234: [EndpointSummary("Get all {Entities}")]
 235: public async Task<ActionResult<PaginatedResult<{Entity}ListDto>>> GetAll(...)
 236: ```
 237: 
 238: **Write Operations** - Authenticated users:
 239: ```csharp
 240: [HttpPost]
 241: [Authorize]
 242: [EndpointSummary("Create a new {Entity}")]
 243: public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>> Create(...)
 244: ```
 245: 
 246: ### User ID Extraction
 247: 
 248: Use the fallback pattern for extracting user ID from JWT claims:
 249: 
 250: ```csharp
 251: var userId = _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.User?.FindFirst("sub")?.Value
 252:     ?? _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.User?.FindFirst("http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/nameidentifier")?.Value
 253:     ?? _httpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.User?.FindFirst("sid")?.Value;
 254: 
 255: if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(userId))
 256: {
 257:     return Unauthorized(new { error = "User ID not found in token" });
 258: }
 259: ```
 260: 
 261: ---
 262: 
 263: ## 5. Request/Response Patterns
 264: 
 265: ### HATEOAS / HAL+JSON Implementation
 266: 
 267: The API implements **HATEOAS (Hypermedia as the Engine of Application State)** using the HAL+JSON format. This allows clients to discover available actions dynamically based on their permissions and the resource state.
 268: 
 269: #### Core Components
 270: 
 271: 1.  **`IResourceAssembler<TDto, TListDto>`**:
 272:     The central service that converts DTOs into `HalResource<T>` or `HalCollectionResource<T>`.
 273:     - Automatically handles `Prefer: return=minimal` header to strip links.
 274:     - Evaluates authorization policies before adding links.
 275:     - Uses `ResourceAssemblerBase` for shared logic.
 276: 
 277: 2.  **`ILinkPolicy<T>`**:
 278:     Defines *which* links apply to a specific resource.
 279:     - `GetLinks(dto, user)`: Returns links for a single resource.
 280:     - `GetCollectionLinks(user)`: Returns links for the collection root (e.g., "create").
 281: 
 282: 3.  **`IHateoasAuthorizationEvaluator`**:
 283:     Integrates with **Cerbos** to filter links. If a user lacks permission for an action (e.g., `update`), the corresponding link is automatically omitted from the response.
 284: 
 285: #### Defining Links
 286: 
 287: Links are defined using a fluent API in Policy classes:
 288: 
 289: ```csharp
 290: public class EventLinkPolicy : ILinkPolicy<EventDto>
 291: {
 292:     public IEnumerable<LinkDefinition> GetLinks(EventDto dto, ClaimsPrincipal user)
 293:     {
 294:         // Self link (always visible)
 295:         yield return new LinkDefinition(
 296:             rel: LinkRelations.Self,
 297:             routeName: RouteNames.GetEvent,
 298:             routeValues: new { id = dto.Id });
 299: 
 300:         // Update link (only if user has permission)
 301:         yield return new LinkDefinition(
 302:             rel: LinkRelations.Update,
 303:             routeName: RouteNames.UpdateEvent,
 304:             routeValues: new { id = dto.Id })
 305:             .RequirePermission(CerbosPermissionAction.Update, dto); // Checks Cerbos policy
 306:     }
 307: }
 308: ```
 309: 
 310: #### Response Wrapper Types
 311: 
 312: **For Single Resources:**
 313: ```csharp
 314: public class HalResource<T>
 315: {
 316:     public T Data { get; set; }  // The actual DTO payload
 317:     public Dictionary<string, HalLink> _links { get; set; }  // Hypermedia links
 318: }
 319: ```
 320: 
 321: **For Collections:**
 322: ```csharp
 323: public class HalCollectionResource<T>
 324: {
 325:     public Dictionary<string, object> _embedded { get; set; }  // Contains "items" array
 326:     public Dictionary<string, HalLink> _links { get; set; }   // Collection navigation links
 327:     public int TotalCount { get; set; }
 328:     public int PageNumber { get; set; }
 329:     public int PageSize { get; set; }
 330:     public int TotalPages { get; set; }
 331: }
 332: ```
 333: 
 334: #### Example Response
 335: 
 336: **Request:**
 337: ```http
 338: GET /api/events/123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000
 339: Accept: application/hal+json
 340: ```
 341: 
 342: **Response:**
 343: ```json
 344: {
 345:   "data": {
 346:     "id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
 347:     "title": "Community Iftar 2026",
 348:     "status": "Published"
 349:   },
 350:   "_links": {
 351:     "self": {
 352:       "href": "/api/events/123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
 353:       "method": "GET"
 354:     },
 355:     "update": {
 356:       "href": "/api/events/123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
 357:       "method": "PUT"
 358:     }
 359:   }
 360: }
 361: ```
 362: 
 363: #### Optimization: Minimal Response
 364: 
 365: Clients can request payloads without hypermedia overhead using the standard `Prefer` header. This is useful for mobile apps or internal services that don't need discovery.
 366: 
 367: **Request:**
 368: ```http
 369: GET /api/events/123...
 370: Prefer: return=minimal
 371: ```
 372: 
 373: **Response (Pure JSON):**
 374: ```json
 375: {
 376:   "data": {
 377:     "id": "123...",
 378:     "title": "Community Iftar 2026"
 379:   }
 380: }
 381: ```
 382: 
 383: ### Command Response
 384: 
 385: 
 386: All write operations return `BaseCommandResponse<T>`:
 387: 
 388: ```csharp
 389: public class BaseCommandResponse<T>
 390: {
 391:     public bool Success { get; set; }
 392:     public string Message { get; set; } = string.Empty;
 393:     public T? Id { get; set; }
 394:     public List<string> Errors { get; set; } = new();
 395: }
 396: ```
 397: 
 398: **Success Response**:
 399: ```json
 400: {
 401:     "success": true,
 402:     "message": "{Entity} created successfully.",
 403:     "id": "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6",
 404:     "errors": []
 405: }
 406: ```
 407: 
 408: **Failure Response**:
 409: ```json
 410: {
 411:     "success": false,
 412:     "message": "{Entity} creation failed.",
 413:     "id": null,
 414:     "errors": [
 415:         "Title is required",
 416:         "{RelatedEntity}Id not found"
 417:     ]
 418: }
 419: ```
 420: 
 421: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
 422: 
 423: **Success Response**:
 424: ```json
 425: {
 426:     "success": true,
 427:     "message": "Event created successfully.",
 428:     "id": "3fa85f64-5717-4562-b3fc-2c963f66afa6",
 429:     "errors": []
 430: }
 431: ```
 432: 
 433: **Failure Response**:
 434: ```json
 435: {
 436:     "success": false,
 437:     "message": "Event creation failed.",
 438:     "id": null,
 439:     "errors": [
 440:         "Title is required",
 441:         "EventTypeId not found"
 442:     ]
 443: }
 444: ```
 445: 
 446: ### Query Response
 447: 
 448: Read operations return DTOs directly or wrapped in `PaginatedResult<T>`:
 449: 
 450: **Generic Pattern:**
 451: 
 452: ```csharp
 453: // Single entity
 454: public async Task<ActionResult<{Entity}Dto>> GetById({IdType} id)
 455: 
 456: // List with pagination
 457: public async Task<ActionResult<PaginatedResult<{Entity}ListDto>>> GetAll(...)
 458: ```
 459: 
 460: ### HATEOAS / HAL+JSON Response Format
 461: 
 462: All API responses are wrapped in **HAL (Hypertext Application Language)** format, providing hypermedia links for discoverability and navigation.
 463: 
 464: #### Response Wrapper Types
 465: 
 466: **For Single Resources:**
 467: ```csharp
 468: public class HalResource<T>
 469: {
 470:     public T Data { get; set; }  // The actual DTO payload
 471:     public Dictionary<string, HalLink> _links { get; set; }  // Hypermedia links
 472: }
 473: 
 474: public class HalLink
 475: {
 476:     public string Href { get; set; }       // URL
 477:     public string? Method { get; set; }    // HTTP method (GET, POST, etc.)
 478:     public string? Rel { get; set; }       // Link relation type
 479: }
 480: ```
 481: 
 482: **For Collections:**
 483: ```csharp
 484: public class HalCollectionResource<T>
 485: {
 486:     public Dictionary<string, object> _embedded { get; set; }  // Contains "items" array
 487:     public Dictionary<string, HalLink> _links { get; set; }   // Collection navigation links
 488:     public int TotalCount { get; set; }
 489:     public int PageNumber { get; set; }
 490:     public int PageSize { get; set; }
 491:     public int TotalPages { get; set; }
 492: }
 493: ```
 494: 
 495: #### Example Single Resource Response
 496: 
 497: **Request:**
 498: ```http
 499: GET /api/events/123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000
 500: Accept: application/hal+json
 501: ```
 502: 
 503: **Response:**
 504: ```json
 505: {
 506:   "data": {
 507:     "id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
 508:     "title": "Community Iftar 2026",
 509:     "startDate": "2026-03-15T18:00:00Z",
 510:     "location": "Amsterdam Mosque",
 511:     "status": "Published"
 512:   },
 513:   "_links": {
 514:     "self": {
 515:       "href": "/api/events/123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
 516:       "method": "GET"
 517:     },
 518:     "update": {
 519:       "href": "/api/events/123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
 520:       "method": "PUT"
 521:     },
 522:     "delete": {
 523:       "href": "/api/events/123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
 524:       "method": "DELETE"
 525:     },
 526:     "sessions": {
 527:       "href": "/api/events/123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000/sessions",
 528:       "method": "GET"
 529:     }
 530:   }
 531: }
 532: ```
 533: 
 534: #### Example Collection Response
 535: 
 536: **Request:**
 537: ```http
 538: GET /api/events?pageNumber=1&pageSize=10
 539: Accept: application/hal+json
 540: ```
 541: 
 542: **Response:**
 543: ```json
 544: {
 545:   "_embedded": {
 546:     "items": [
 547:       {
 548:         "id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
 549:         "title": "Community Iftar 2026",
 550:         "startDate": "2026-03-15T18:00:00Z"
 551:       },
 552:       {
 553:         "id": "987e6543-e21c-45d6-b789-123456789abc",
 554:         "title": "Tech Workshop: Clean Architecture",
 555:         "startDate": "2026-04-01T14:00:00Z"
 556:       }
 557:     ]
 558:   },
 559:   "_links": {
 560:     "self": {
 561:       "href": "/api/events?pageNumber=1&pageSize=10",
 562:       "method": "GET"
 563:     },
 564:     "first": {
 565:       "href": "/api/events?pageNumber=1&pageSize=10",
 566:       "method": "GET"
 567:     },
 568:     "next": {
 569:       "href": "/api/events?pageNumber=2&pageSize=10",
 570:       "method": "GET"
 571:     },
 572:     "last": {
 573:       "href": "/api/events?pageNumber=5&pageSize=10",
 574:       "method": "GET"
 575:     }
 576:   },
 577:   "totalCount": 47,
 578:   "pageNumber": 1,
 579:   "pageSize": 10,
 580:   "totalPages": 5
 581: }
 582: ```
 583: 
 584: #### Prefer Header Support
 585: 
 586: Clients can request minimal responses without hypermedia links using the `Prefer` header:
 587: 
 588: **Request:**
 589: ```http
 590: GET /api/events/123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000
 591: Prefer: return=minimal
 592: ```
 593: 
 594: **Response (without _links):**
 595: ```json
 596: {
 597:   "data": {
 598:     "id": "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
 599:     "title": "Community Iftar 2026",
 600:     "startDate": "2026-03-15T18:00:00Z",
 601:     "location": "Amsterdam Mosque",
 602:     "status": "Published"
 603:   }
 604: }
 605: ```
 606: 
 607: #### Resource Assembler Pattern
 608: 
 609: Controllers use `IResourceAssembler<TDto, TListDto>` to build HAL responses:
 610: 
 611: **Generic Pattern:**
 612: ```csharp
 613: public class {Entity}Controller : ControllerBase
 614: {
 615:     private readonly IMediator _mediator;
 616:     private readonly IResourceAssembler<{Entity}Dto, {Entity}ListDto> _resourceAssembler;
 617: 
 618:     [HttpGet("{id}")]
 619:     public async Task<ActionResult<HalResource<{Entity}Dto>>> GetById({IdType} id)
 620:     {
 621:         var dto = await _mediator.Send(new Get{Entity}DetailsRequest { Id = id });
 622:         if (dto == null) return NotFound();
 623: 
 624:         var resource = _resourceAssembler.ToResource(dto, RouteNames.Get{Entity});
 625:         return Ok(resource);
 626:     }
 627: 
 628:     [HttpGet]
 629:     public async Task<ActionResult<HalCollectionResource<{Entity}ListDto>>> GetAll(...)
 630:     {
 631:         var dtos = await _mediator.Send(new Get{Entity}ListRequest { ... });
 632:         var resource = _resourceAssembler.ToCollectionResource(
 633:             dtos,
 634:             RouteNames.Get{Entities},
 635:             totalCount,
 636:             pageNumber,
 637:             pageSize);
 638:         return Ok(resource);
 639:     }
 640: }
 641: ```
 642: 
 643: **RouteNames Constants:**
 644: Route names are defined in `RouteNames.cs` for consistency:
 645: ```csharp
 646: public static class RouteNames
 647: {
 648:     public const string GetEvent = "GetEvent";
 649:     public const string GetEvents = "GetEvents";
 650:     public const string UpdateEvent = "UpdateEvent";
 651:     public const string DeleteEvent = "DeleteEvent";
 652:     // ...
 653: }
 654: ```
 655: 
 656: #### Benefits
 657: 
 658: - **Discoverability**: Clients can navigate the API without hardcoding URLs
 659: - **Evolvability**: Server can change URLs without breaking clients
 660: - **Self-Documenting**: Links show available actions based on current state
 661: - **Bandwidth Control**: Use `Prefer: return=minimal` to reduce payload size
 662: 
 663: **See Also**: [CODEBASE_INSIGHTS.md](CODEBASE_INSIGHTS.md) Section 14 for HATEOAS implementation details
 664: 
 665: ---
 666: 
 667: ## 6. Pagination
 668: 
 669: ### Paginated Response Structure
 670: 
 671: ```csharp
 672: public class PaginatedResult<T>
 673: {
 674:     public ICollection<T> Items { get; set; } = new List<T>();
 675:     public int TotalCount { get; set; }
 676:     public int PageNumber { get; set; }
 677:     public int PageSize { get; set; }
 678:     public int TotalPages => (int)Math.Ceiling((double)TotalCount / PageSize);
 679:     public bool HasPreviousPage => PageNumber > 1;
 680:     public bool HasNextPage => PageNumber < TotalPages;
 681: }
 682: ```
 683: 
 684: ### Query Parameters
 685: 
 686: **Generic Pattern:**
 687: ```
 688: GET /api/{entity}?pageNumber=1&pageSize=20
 689: ```
 690: 
 691: **Example (ISLAMU Event):**
 692: ```
 693: GET /api/event?pageNumber=1&pageSize=20
 694: ```
 695: 
 696: | Parameter | Type | Default | Max | Description |
 697: |-----------|------|---------|-----|-------------|
 698: | `pageNumber` | int | 1 | - | Page number (1-indexed) |
 699: | `pageSize` | int | 20 | 100 | Items per page |
 700: 
 701: ### Example Response
 702: 
 703: ```json
 704: {
 705:     "items": [
 706:         { "id": "...", "title": "Event 1", ... },
 707:         { "id": "...", "title": "Event 2", ... }
 708:     ],
 709:     "totalCount": 150,
 710:     "pageNumber": 1,
 711:     "pageSize": 20,
 712:     "totalPages": 8,
 713:     "hasPreviousPage": false,
 714:     "hasNextPage": true
 715: }
 716: ```
 717: 
 718: ---
 719: 
 720: ## 7. Error Handling
 721: 
 722: ### Standardization
 723: 
 724: The API follows **RFC 7807 (Problem Details for HTTP APIs)** for all unhandled exceptions, while using structured `BaseCommandResponse` for domain logic failures.
 725: 
 726: ### 7.1. Global Exception Handler
 727: 
 728: Any unhandled exception (System.Exception) is caught by the global `ExceptionHandler` middleware and converted into a standardized JSON response.
 729: 
 730: **Response Format (ProblemDetails):**
 731: ```json
 732: {
 733:   "type": "https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc9110#section-15.6.1",
 734:   "title": "An error occurred while processing your request.",
 735:   "status": 500,
 736:   "detail": "Database connection timeout",
 737:   "instance": "/api/events"
 738: }
 739: ```
 740: 
 741: ### 7.2. Domain Logic Errors (Command Response)
 742: 
 743: For expected business rule violations (e.g., validation failures, logic conflicts), endpoints return a `200 OK` or `400 Bad Request` with a structured `BaseCommandResponse`.
 744: 
 745: **Response Format:**
 746: ```json
 747: {
 748:     "success": false,
 749:     "message": "Validation failed",
 750:     "id": null,
 751:     "errors": [
 752:         "Event date cannot be in the past.",
 753:         "Title is required."
 754:     ]
 755: }
 756: ```
 757: 
 758: ### 7.3. HTTP Status Codes
 759: 
 760: | Code | Meaning | When Used |
 761: |------|---------|-----------|
 762: | `200 OK` | Success | GET, PUT, POST success |
 763: | `201 Created` | Resource created | POST (alternative) |
 764: | `204 No Content` | Success, no body | DELETE success |
 765: | `400 Bad Request` | Validation failed | Business rule violation |
 766: | `401 Unauthorized` | Not authenticated | Missing/invalid token |
 767: | `403 Forbidden` | Not authorized | Insufficient permissions (Cerbos denial) |
 768: | `404 Not Found` | Resource not found | Invalid ID |
 769: | `500 Internal Error` | Server error | Unexpected exception (Unhandled) |
 770: 
 771: ### 7.4. Exception Handling Pattern in Controllers
 772: 
 773: Controllers should use `try-catch` blocks only when specific recovery or logging context is needed. Otherwise, let the global handler manage 500s.
 774: 
 775: **Recommended Pattern:**
 776: 
 777: ```csharp
 778: [HttpDelete("{id}")]
 779: [Authorize]
 780: public async Task<ActionResult> Delete(Guid id)
 781: {
 782:     try
 783:     {
 784:         // ... logic ...
 785:     }
 786:     catch (Exception ex)
 787:     {
 788:         // Only catch if you need to add context before re-throwing
 789:         // or if you want to return a specific status code manually
 790:         _logger.LogError(ex, "Error deleting event {EventId}", id);
 791:         return StatusCode(500, new { error = "An unexpected error occurred." });
 792:     }
 793: }
 794: ```
 795: 
 796: ---
 797: 
 798: ## 8. OpenAPI Documentation
 799: 
 800: ### Required Attributes
 801: 
 802: All controller actions must include:
 803: 
 804: **Generic Template:**
 805: 
 806: ```csharp
 807: [HttpGet("{id}")]
 808: [EndpointSummary("Get {Entity} Details")]
 809: [EndpointDescription("Returns detailed information about a specific {entity} including related data.")]
 810: [AllowAnonymous]
 811: [ProducesResponseType(typeof({Entity}Dto), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
 812: [ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status404NotFound)]
 813: public async Task<ActionResult<{Entity}Dto>> GetById({IdType} id)
 814: ```
 815: 
 816: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
 817: 
 818: ```csharp
 819: [HttpGet("{id}")]
 820: [EndpointSummary("Get Event Details")]
 821: [EndpointDescription("Returns detailed information about a specific event including sessions.")]
 822: [AllowAnonymous]
 823: [ProducesResponseType(typeof(EventDto), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
 824: [ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status404NotFound)]
 825: public async Task<ActionResult<EventDto>> GetById(Guid id)
 826: ```
 827: 
 828: ### Attribute Guidelines
 829: 
 830: | Attribute | Required | Purpose |
 831: |-----------|----------|---------|
 832: | `[EndpointSummary]` | Yes | Short title in API docs |
 833: | `[EndpointDescription]` | Yes | Detailed description |
 834: | `[ProducesResponseType]` | Yes | Document response types |
 835: | `[Consumes]` | For POST/PUT | Request content type |
 836: 
 837: ### Example with Full Documentation
 838: 
 839: **Generic Template:**
 840: 
 841: ```csharp
 842: [HttpPost]
 843: [EndpointSummary("Create a new {Entity}")]
 844: [EndpointDescription("Creates a new {entity} under the specified {relatedEntity}. User must have appropriate permissions.")]
 845: [Authorize]
 846: [Consumes("application/json")]
 847: [ProducesResponseType(typeof(BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
 848: [ProducesResponseType(typeof(BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>), StatusCodes.Status400BadRequest)]
 849: [ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status401Unauthorized)]
 850: public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>>> Create([FromBody] Create{Entity}Dto dto)
 851: ```
 852: 
 853: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
 854: 
 855: ```csharp
 856: [HttpPost]
 857: [EndpointSummary("Create a new Event")]
 858: [EndpointDescription("Creates a new event under the specified organization. User must be an admin of the organization.")]
 859: [Authorize]
 860: [Consumes("application/json")]
 861: [ProducesResponseType(typeof(BaseCommandResponse<Guid>), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
 862: [ProducesResponseType(typeof(BaseCommandResponse<Guid>), StatusCodes.Status400BadRequest)]
 863: [ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status401Unauthorized)]
 864: public async Task<ActionResult<BaseCommandResponse<Guid>>> Create([FromBody] CreateEventDto dto)
 865: ```
 866: 
 867: ---
 868: 
 869: ## 9. Caching Strategy
 870: 
 871: The API implements a **Dual-Layer Caching Strategy** to maximize performance while ensuring data consistency.
 872: 
 873: ### 9.1. Layer 1: Output Caching (HTTP Level)
 874: 
 875: **Purpose**: Caches the entire HTTP response body.
 876: **Use Case**: Public, read-only endpoints (lists, details) that don't vary per user.
 877: **Mechanism**: ASP.NET Core Output Caching Middleware.
 878: 
 879: **Configuration**:
 880: Policies are defined in `Program.cs`:
 881: - `ListData`: Expire 5m, Vary by Query keys (page, size, search).
 882: - `DetailData`: Expire 10m, Vary by Route Value (id).
 883: 
 884: **Usage in Controllers**:
 885: ```csharp
 886: [HttpGet("{id}")]
 887: [AllowAnonymous]
 888: [OutputCache(PolicyName = "DetailData")]
 889: public async Task<ActionResult> GetById(Guid id) { ... }
 890: ```
 891: 
 892: ### 9.2. Layer 2: Hybrid Caching (Application Level)
 893: 
 894: **Purpose**: Caches domain entities or calculation results within the application logic.
 895: **Use Case**:
 896: - Data needed by multiple handlers.
 897: - Data that is expensive to compute/fetch but used in authenticated endpoints (where OutputCache isn't suitable).
 898: - Scenarios requiring **stampede protection**.
 899: **Mechanism**: .NET 9+ `HybridCache` (L1 In-Memory + L2 Redis).
 900: 
 901: **Usage in Handlers (Query Side)**:
 902: Use `GetOrCreateAsync` to fetch-or-cache:
 903: 
 904: ```csharp
 905: public async Task<EventDto> Handle(GetEventDetailsRequest request, CancellationToken ct)
 906: {
 907:     var cacheKey = $"event:{request.Id}";
 908:     
 909:     return await _hybridCache.GetOrCreateAsync(
 910:         cacheKey,
 911:         async cancel => await _repository.GetByIdAsync(request.Id, cancel),
 912:         options: new HybridCacheEntryOptions { Expiration = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10) },
 913:         cancellationToken: ct
 914:     );
 915: }
 916: ```
 917: 
 918: **Usage in Handlers (Command Side)**:
 919: Explicitly invalidate cache after updates:
 920: 
 921: ```csharp
 922: public async Task<BaseCommandResponse> Handle(UpdateEventCommand request, CancellationToken ct)
 923: {
 924:     // ... update logic ...
 925:     
 926:     // Invalidate the specific entity cache
 927:     await _hybridCache.RemoveAsync($"event:{request.Id}", ct);
 928:     
 929:     return response;
 930: }
 931: ```
 932: 
 933: ### 9.3. Caching Guidelines
 934: 
 935: | Feature | Use **Output Cache** | Use **Hybrid Cache** |
 936: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
 937: | **Public Public Data** (e.g., Event List) | ✅ Yes | ❌ No |
 938: | **Authenticated Data** (e.g., "My Events") | ❌ No | ✅ Yes |
 939: | **Lookup Tables** (e.g., Categories) | ✅ Yes | ✅ Yes (if reused internally) |
 940: | **User-Specific Content** | ❌ No | ✅ Yes (Keyed by UserID) |
 941: | **Write Operations** | ❌ Never | ❌ Use to Invalidate |
 942: 
 943: ---

 988: ## 11. Multi-Tenancy
 989: 
 990: ### Tenant Header
 991: 
 992: All requests must include the tenant ID header:
 993: 
 994: ```
 995: X-Tenant-Id: 018e4e5c-7f00-7000-8000-000000000001
 996: ```
 997: 
 998: ### Default Tenant
 999: 
1000: For single-instance deployments, use the default tenant:
1001: 
1002: ```
1003: 018e4e5c-7f00-7000-8000-000000000001
1004: ```
1005: 
1006: This MUST match across:
1007: - `{Project}.API/Services/TenantContext.cs`
1008: - `{Project}.Blazor/Program.cs` (YARP transform)
1009: - `{Project}.Blazor/Services/CircuitAccessTokenService.cs`
1010: - `{Project}.Persistence/SeedIds.cs`
1011: 
1012: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
1013: - `Explore.API/Services/TenantContext.cs`
1014: - `Explore.Blazor/Program.cs` (YARP transform)
1015: - `Explore.Blazor/Services/CircuitAccessTokenService.cs`
1016: - `Explore.Persistence/SeedIds.cs`
1017: 
1018: ### Tenant Context Service
1019: 
1020: ```csharp
1021: public interface ITenantContext
1022: {
1023:     Guid TenantId { get; }
1024: }
1025: 
1026: public class TenantContext : ITenantContext
1027: {
1028:     public const string DefaultTenantIdString = "018e4e5c-7f00-7000-8000-000000000001";
1029:     public static readonly Guid DefaultTenantId = Guid.Parse(DefaultTenantIdString);
1030: 
1031:     public Guid TenantId { get; }
1032: 
1033:     public TenantContext(IHttpContextAccessor httpContextAccessor)
1034:     {
1035:         var header = httpContextAccessor.HttpContext?.Request.Headers["X-Tenant-Id"].FirstOrDefault();
1036:         TenantId = Guid.TryParse(header, out var tenantId) ? tenantId : DefaultTenantId;
1037:     }
1038: }
1039: ```
1040: 
1041: ### Global Query Filters
1042: 
1043: EF Core automatically filters all queries by tenant:
1044: 
1045: **Generic Template:**
1046: 
1047: ```csharp
1048: // In {DbContext}
1049: protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder)
1050: {
1051:     // Apply tenant filter to all entities with TenantId
1052:     modelBuilder.Entity<{Entity}>().HasQueryFilter(e => e.TenantId == _tenantContext.TenantId);
1053:     // ... etc for all tenant-scoped entities
1054: }
1055: ```
1056: 
1057: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
1058: 
1059: ```csharp
1060: // In ExploreDbContext
1061: protected override void OnModelCreating(ModelBuilder modelBuilder)
1062: {
1063:     // Apply tenant filter to all entities with TenantId
1064:     modelBuilder.Entity<Event>().HasQueryFilter(e => e.TenantId == _tenantContext.TenantId);
1065:     // ... etc for all tenant-scoped entities
1066: }
1067: ```

 28: 
 29: ## 1. Technology Stack
 30: 
 31: | Layer | Technology | Purpose |
 32: |-------|------------|---------|
 33: | **Runtime** | .NET 10.0 | Primary framework |
 34: | **Orchestration** | .NET Aspire | Service orchestration, observability |
 35: | **Web UI** | Blazor (Server + WebAssembly) | Hybrid rendering model |
 36: | **UI Components** | MudBlazor | Material Design components |
 37: | **Database** | PostgreSQL + PostGIS | Primary datastore with spatial queries |
 38: | **ORM** | Entity Framework Core | Data access layer |
 39: | **Authentication** | Keycloak | OIDC/JWT identity provider |
 40: | **Authorization** | ASP.NET Core Authorization | `[Authorize]` attributes and resource-based logic |
 41: | **Secrets** | Infisical | Secrets management |
 42: | **Logging** | Serilog | Structured logging |
 43: | **Telemetry** | OpenTelemetry | Distributed tracing and metrics |
 44: | **API Docs** | Scalar + Swagger | OpenAPI documentation |
 45: | **Federation** | ATProto / ActivityPub (Planned) | Domain model exists; federation endpoints are not yet implemented. |
 46: 
 47: ## 2. Architectural Paradigm: Clean Architecture + CQRS
 48: 
 49: The project is built upon **Clean Architecture** principles to ensure a separation of concerns, testability, and maintainability. It uses **Command Query Responsibility Segregation (CQRS)** to separate read and write operations within the application layer.
 50: 
 51: ### Layer Dependencies
 52: 
 53: Dependencies must only flow inwards. The domain layer has no dependencies on any other layer.
 54: 
 55: **Generic Structure:**
 56: - **Presentation Layer**: `{Project}.API`, `{Project}.Blazor`
 57: - **Application Layer**: `{Project}.Application`
 58: - **Domain Layer**: `{Project}.Domain`
 59: - **Infrastructure Layer**: `{Project}.Persistence`, `{Project}.Infrastructure`
 60: 
 61: **Diagram (Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event):**
 62: 
 63: ```mermaid
 64: graph TD
 65:     subgraph Presentation Layer
 66:         A[Explore.API]
 67:         B[Explore.Blazor]
 68:     end
 69: 
 70:     subgraph Application Layer
 71:         C[Explore.Application]
 72:     end
 73: 
 74:     subgraph Domain Layer
 75:         D[Explore.Domain]
 76:     end
 77: 
 78:     subgraph Infrastructure Layer
 79:         E[Explore.Persistence]
 80:         F[Explore.Infrastructure]
 81:     end
 82: 
 83:     A --> C
 84:     B --> C
 85:     C --> D
 86:     E --> C
 87:     F --> C
 88: ```
 89: 
 90: *Substitute "Explore" with your `{Project}` name.*
 91: 
 92: **Layer Responsibilities:**
 93: 
 94: -   **Domain**: Contains pure business logic, entities, and value objects. It is the core of the application and has no external dependencies.
 95: -   **Application**: Orchestrates the domain logic. It contains use cases (commands/queries), DTOs, and interfaces for infrastructure services. It depends only on the Domain layer.
 96: -   **Infrastructure**: Provides concrete implementations for data access with repository pattern (Persistence via `{Project}.Persistence`) and external services (email, file storage via `{Project}.Infrastructure`). It depends on the Application layer to implement its interfaces.
 97: -   **Presentation**: The entry points to the application, including the REST API (`{Project}.API`) and the Blazor UI (`{Project}.Blazor`). This layer composes the other layers and handles user interaction and HTTP requests.
 98: 
 99: ### Data Flow (CQRS Pattern)
100: 
101: The CQRS pattern is implemented using the **MediatR** library.
102: 
103: **Generic Flow:**
104: 1. Client sends HTTP request to `{Entity}Controller`
105: 2. Controller sends command/query to MediatR
106: 3. MediatR routes to appropriate handler
107: 4. Handler interacts with repository
108: 5. Response flows back through the chain
109: 
110: **Sequence Diagram:**
111: 
112: ```mermaid
113: sequenceDiagram
114:     participant Client
115:     participant Controller
116:     participant MediatR
117:     participant Handler
118:     participant Repository
119: 
120:     Client->>Controller: HTTP Request (e.g., POST /api/{entity})
121:     Controller->>MediatR: `_mediator.Send(command)`
122:     MediatR->>Handler: `Handle(command)`
123:     Handler->>Repository: `_repository.Create(entity)`
124:     Repository-->>Handler: Returns updated entity
125:     Handler-->>MediatR: Returns `BaseCommandResponse<{IdType}>`
126:     MediatR-->>Controller: Returns response
127:     Controller-->>Client: HTTP Response (e.g., 200 OK)
128: ```
129: 
130: *Replace `{entity}` with your resource name (e.g., `event`, `order`, `product`) and `{IdType}` with your ID type (`Guid`, `int`).*
131: 
132: *For detailed implementation guidance, see the `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` skill.*
133: 
134: ## 3. Frontend Architecture: Blazor Hybrid with BFF
135: 
136: The frontend is a **Blazor Hybrid** application that uses the **Backend-for-Frontend (BFF)** pattern for security and performance.
137: 
138: ### Rendering Mode: InteractiveAuto
139: 
140: The application uses the `InteractiveAuto` render mode by default.
141: 
142: 1.  **Fast Initial Load**: The first visit renders pages on the **server** via a SignalR connection, providing immediate content to the user.
143: 2.  **Background Download**: The Blazor **WebAssembly** runtime and application DLLs are downloaded in the background.
144: 3.  **Seamless Transition**: Once the WASM assets are cached, the application transitions to client-side rendering, offloading work from the server and enabling potential offline capabilities.
145: 
146: ### BFF Security Model
147: 
148: The `{Project}.Blazor` project acts as a security gateway for the `{Project}.Blazor.Client` frontend.
149: 
150: **Architecture Flow:**
151: 
152: ```mermaid
153: graph LR
154:     A[Browser / WASM] -- Cookie --> B[BFF / Blazor Server]
155:     B -- OIDC Redirect --> C[OIDC Provider]
156:     B -- YARP Proxy --> D[Backend API]
157:     D -- JWT Auth --> D
158: ```
159: 
160: **Security Layers:**
161: 
162: -   The **BFF** (`{Project}.Blazor`) handles the OIDC authentication flow with your identity provider (e.g., Keycloak) and maintains the user session in a secure, `HttpOnly` cookie.
163: -   The **WASM Client** (`{Project}.Blazor.Client`) is "dumb" regarding authentication; it simply sends the cookie with each request to the BFF.
164: -   The **BFF** uses **YARP** as a reverse proxy. When a request for `/api/...` arrives, it reads the access token from the session cookie and forwards the request to the `{Project}.API` backend with a `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header.
165: -   This architecture ensures **no tokens are ever exposed to the browser**.
166: 
167: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
168: 
169: - **BFF**: `Explore.Blazor` (Blazor Server)
170: - **WASM Client**: `Explore.Blazor.Client`
171: - **Backend API**: `Explore.API`
172: - **OIDC Provider**: Keycloak
173: 
174: *For detailed implementation guidance, see the `blazor-bff-patterns` and `auth-patterns` skills.*
175: 
176: ## 4. API Architecture
177: 
178: The `{Project}.API` project is a standard ASP.NET Core REST API following Clean Architecture principles.
179: 
180: ### Key Conventions
181: 
182: -   **Stateless**: The API is stateless and relies solely on the provided JWT for authentication and authorization.
183: -   **Thin Controllers**: Controllers are minimal. Their only job is to receive an HTTP request, send a command or query to MediatR, and return an appropriate HTTP response.
184: -   **Authorization**: Write endpoints (`POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`) are protected with `[Authorize]`. Read endpoints (`GET`) are public with `[AllowAnonymous]`.
185: -   **Documentation**: Endpoints are documented using `[EndpointSummary]`, `[EndpointDescription]`, and `[ProducesResponseType]` attributes for OpenAPI generation.
186: 
187: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
188: 
189: - **API Project**: `Explore.API`
190: - **Base URL**: `https://localhost:7001/api/v1`
191: 
192: *For detailed implementation guidance, see `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` skill.*
193: 
194: ## 5. Project Structure
195: 
196: The solution is organized into projects that directly map to the layers of Clean Architecture.
197: 
198: ### Generic Template
199: 
200: ```
201: {Project}.sln
202: ├── {Project}.Domain/              # Domain layer: Entities, Enums, Value Objects
203: ├── {Project}.Application/         # Application layer: CQRS handlers, DTOs, Interfaces
204: ├── {Project}.Persistence/         # Infrastructure: EF Core DbContext, Repositories
205: ├── {Project}.Infrastructure/      # Infrastructure: External services (email, storage, etc.)
206: ├── {Project}.API/                 # Presentation: REST API
207: ├── {Project}.Blazor/              # Presentation: Blazor Server (BFF)
208: ├── {Project}.Blazor.Client/       # Presentation: Blazor WebAssembly (UI)
209: ├── {Project}.AppHost/             # .NET Aspire Orchestrator
210: └── {Project}.ServiceDefaults/     # Shared Aspire configuration (observability, resilience)
211: ├── tests/
212: │   ├── {Project}.Application.UnitTests/
213: │   ├── {Project}.Domain.UnitTests/
214: │   └── {Project}.API.IntegrationTests/
215: └── docs/
216:     └── ... (Architecture documentation, guides)
217: ```
218: 
219: ### Implementation Example: ISLAMU Event
220: 
221: ```
222: Explore.sln
223: ├── Explore.Domain/              # Domain layer: Event, Organization, User entities
224: ├── Explore.Application/         # Application layer: Event handlers, DTOs
225: ├── Explore.Persistence/         # Infrastructure: ExploreDbContext, Repositories
226: ├── Explore.Infrastructure/      # Infrastructure: Email, file storage services
227: ├── Explore.API/                 # Presentation: REST API
228: ├── Explore.Blazor/              # Presentation: Blazor Server (BFF)
229: ├── Explore.Blazor.Client/       # Presentation: Blazor WebAssembly (UI)
230: ├── Explore.AppHost/             # .NET Aspire Orchestrator
231: └── Explore.ServiceDefaults/     # Shared Aspire configuration
232: ├── tests/
233: │   ├── Event.Application.UnitTests/
234: │   └── ... (other test projects)
235: └── docs/
236:     └── ... (High-level documentation)
237: ```
238: 
239: *Substitute `{Project}` with your solution name (e.g., `OrderSystem`, `InventoryApp`, `HRPortal`).*
````

````csharp
  1: using System;
  2: using System.Collections.Generic;
  3: using System.Threading.Tasks;
  4: using Asp.Versioning;
  5: using Explore.Application.DTOs.StorageObject;
  6: using Explore.Application.Features.StorageObjects.Requests.Commands;
  7: using Explore.Application.Features.StorageObjects.Requests.Queries;
  8: using Explore.Application.Responses;

 12: using Microsoft.AspNetCore.OutputCaching;
 13: 
 14: namespace Explore.API.Controllers;
 15: 
 16: [ApiVersion("0.1")]
 17: [Route("api/[controller]")]
 18: [ApiController]
 19: public class StorageObjectController : ControllerBase
 20: {
 21:     private readonly IMediator _mediator;
 22: 
 23:     public StorageObjectController(IMediator mediator)
 24:     {
 25:         _mediator = mediator;
 26:     }
 27: 
 28: 
 29:     [HttpGet]
 30:     [EndpointSummary("Get all Storage Objects")]
 31:     [EndpointDescription("Retrieve a paginated list of all storage objects (files, images, documents, etc.). Default page size is 20, max is 100.")]
 32:     [AllowAnonymous]
 33:     [ProducesResponseType(typeof(PaginatedResult<StorageObjectListDto>), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
 34:     [OutputCache(PolicyName = "ListData")]
 35:     public async Task<ActionResult<PaginatedResult<StorageObjectListDto>>> GetAll([FromQuery] int pageNumber = 1, [FromQuery] int pageSize = 20, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 36:     {
 37:         var storageObjects = await _mediator.Send(new GetStorageObjectListRequest
 38:         {
 39:             PageNumber = pageNumber,
 40:             PageSize = pageSize
 41:         }, cancellationToken);
 42:         return Ok(storageObjects);
 43:     }
 44: 
 45: 
 46:     [HttpGet("{id}")]
 47:     [EndpointSummary("Get Storage Object by ID")]
 48:     [EndpointDescription("Retrieve details of a specific storage object")]
 49:     [AllowAnonymous]
 50:     [ProducesResponseType(typeof(StorageObjectDto), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
 51:     [ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status404NotFound)]
 52:     [OutputCache(PolicyName = "DetailData")]
 53:     public async Task<ActionResult<StorageObjectDto>> GetById(Guid id, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 54:     {
 55:         var storageObject = await _mediator.Send(new GetStorageObjectDetailsRequest { Id = id }, cancellationToken);
 56: 
 57:         if (storageObject == null)
 58:         {
 59:             return NotFound(new { error = "Storage object not found" });
 60:         }
 61: 
 62:         return Ok(storageObject);
 63:     }
 64: 
 65: 
 66:     [HttpGet("file/{*fileKey}")]
 67:     [EndpointSummary("Get File Content")]
 68:     [EndpointDescription("Retrieve the content of a file from storage by its key")]
 69:     [AllowAnonymous]
 70:     [ResponseCache(Duration = 86400, Location = ResponseCacheLocation.Any)]
 71:     [OutputCache(PolicyName = "DetailData")]
 72:     public async Task<IActionResult> GetFile(string fileKey, CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
 73:     {
 74:         if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(fileKey))
 75:         {
 76:             return BadRequest("File key cannot be empty.");
 77:         }
 78: 
 79:         try
 80:         {
 81:             var result = await _mediator.Send(new GetStorageObjectFileRequest { FileKey = fileKey }, cancellationToken);
 82:             return File(result.FileStream, result.ContentType, enableRangeProcessing: true);
 83:         }
 84:         catch (KeyNotFoundException)
 85:         {
 86:             return NotFound("File not found.");
 87:         }
 88:         catch (Exception)
 89:         {
 90:             return StatusCode(500, "An internal error occurred.");
 91:         }
 92:     }
 93: 
 94: 
 95:     [HttpGet("{id}/presigned-url")]
 96:     [EndpointSummary("Get Presigned Download URL")]
 97:     [EndpointDescription("Generate a time-limited presigned URL for viewing/downloading a file from S3-compatible storage")]
 98:     [AllowAnonymous]
 99:     [ProducesResponseType(typeof(PresignedDownloadUrlResponseDto), StatusCodes.Status200OK)]
100:     [ProducesResponseType(StatusCodes.Status404NotFound)]
101:     [OutputCache(PolicyName = "DetailData")]

 51:                     ?? User.FindFirst(ClaimTypes.Email)?.Value ?? "";
 52:

 54:                         ?? User.FindFirst(ClaimTypes.GivenName)?.Value ?? "";
 55:

 57:                        ?? User.FindFirst(ClaimTypes.Surname)?.Value ?? "";
 58:

 60:                        ?? User.FindFirst(ClaimTypes.Name)?.Value ?? "";
 61:

 64:         {
 65:             return BadRequest(new BaseCommandResponse<Guid>
 66:             {

 78:             LastName = string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(lastName) ? "" : lastName,
 79:             Username = username
 80:         };

 84:

 86:         {
 87:             return BadRequest(response);
 88:         }
 89: 
 90:         return Ok(response);

````csharp
  1: using Explore.Application.Contracts.Persistence;

  5: 
  6: namespace Explore.Persistence.Repositories;
  7: 
  8: public class EventRepository : GenericRepository<Event, Guid>, IEventRepository
  9: {
 10:     private static readonly Func<ExploreDbContext, Guid, Task<Event?>> GetByIdCompiled =
 11:         EF.CompileAsyncQuery((ExploreDbContext ctx, Guid id) =>
 12:             ctx.Events
 13:                 .AsNoTracking()
 14:                 .FirstOrDefault(e => e.Id == id));
 15: 
 16:     private readonly ExploreDbContext _dbContext;
 17: 
 18:     public EventRepository(ExploreDbContext dbContext) : base(dbContext)
 19:     {
 20:         _dbContext = dbContext;
 21:     }
 22: 
 23:     public new async Task<Event?> GetById(Guid id)
 24:     {
 25:         return await GetByIdCompiled(_dbContext, id);
 26:     }
 27: 
 28:     public async Task<List<Event>> GetEventsWithDetails()
 29:     {
 30:         return await _dbContext.Events
 31:             .AsNoTrackingWithIdentityResolution()
 32:             .AsSplitQuery()
 33:             .Include(e => e.EventType)
 34:             .Include(e => e.AudienceGender)
 35:             .Include(e => e.AudienceAge)
 36:             .Include(e => e.Actor)
 37:                 .ThenInclude(a => a.ActorType)
 38:             .Include(e => e.Actor)
 39:                 .ThenInclude(a => a!.ProfilePicture)
 40:             .Include(e => e.FeaturedImage)
 41:             .Include(e => e.EventStatus)
 42:             .Include(e => e.VisibilityType)
 43:             .Include(e => e.EventFormat)
 44:             .Include(e => e.Madhab)
 45:             .Include(e => e.IslamicAspect)
 46:                 .ThenInclude(a => a!.Madhab)
 47:             .Include(e => e.IslamicAspect)
 48:                 .ThenInclude(a => a!.PrimaryLanguage)
 49:             .Include(e => e.TechAspect)
 50:             .ToListAsync();
 51:     }
 52: 
 53:     public async Task<Event?> GetEventWithDetails(Guid id)
 54:     {

152:     public async Task<(List<Event> Items, int TotalCount)> GetEventsWithDetailsPaged(
153:         int pageNumber, int pageSize, EventQuerySpecification specification)
154:     {
155:         var query = _dbContext.Events
156:             .AsNoTrackingWithIdentityResolution()
157:             .AsSplitQuery()
158:             .Include(e => e.EventType)
159:             .Include(e => e.AudienceGender)
160:             .Include(e => e.AudienceAge)
161:             .Include(e => e.Actor)
162:                 .ThenInclude(a => a.ActorType)
163:             .Include(e => e.Actor)
164:                 .ThenInclude(a => a!.ProfilePicture)
165:             .Include(e => e.FeaturedImage)
166:             .Include(e => e.EventStatus)
167:             .Include(e => e.VisibilityType)
168:             .Include(e => e.EventFormat)
169:             .Include(e => e.Madhab)
170:             .Include(e => e.IslamicAspect)
171:                 .ThenInclude(a => a!.Madhab)
172:             .Include(e => e.IslamicAspect)
173:                 .ThenInclude(a => a!.PrimaryLanguage)
174:             .Include(e => e.TechAspect)
175:             .AsQueryable();
176: 
177: 
178:         query = ApplySubqueryFilters(query, specification);
179: 
180: 
181:         query = (IQueryable<Event>)specification.Apply(query);
182: 
183: 
184:         if (!specification.HasSort)
185:         {
186:             query = query.OrderByDescending(e => e.FirstSessionDate);
187:         }
188: 
189:         var totalCount = await query.CountAsync();
190:         var items = await query
191:             .Skip((pageNumber - 1) * pageSize)
192:             .Take(pageSize)
193:             .ToListAsync();
194: 
195:         return (items, totalCount);
196:     }
197: 
198: 
199: 
200: 
201: 
202: 
203:     private IQueryable<Event> ApplySubqueryFilters(
204:         IQueryable<Event> query, EventQuerySpecification specification)
205:     {
206:         foreach (var subFilter in specification.SubqueryFilters)
207:         {
208:             query = subFilter.FilterType switch
209:             {
210:                 EventSubqueryFilterType.Category => query.Where(e =>
211:                     _dbContext.EventCategories.Any(ec =>
212:                         ec.EventId == e.Id && ec.CategoryId == (Guid)subFilter.Value)),
213: 
214:                 EventSubqueryFilterType.Tag => query.Where(e =>
215:                     _dbContext.EventTags.Any(et =>
216:                         et.EventId == e.Id && et.TagId == (Guid)subFilter.Value)),
217: 
218:                 EventSubqueryFilterType.Location => query.Where(e =>
219:                     _dbContext.EventSessions.Any(es =>
220:                         es.EventId == e.Id && es.LocationId == (Guid)subFilter.Value)),
221: 
222:                 EventSubqueryFilterType.RegistrationMode => query.Where(e =>
223:                     _dbContext.EventSessions.Any(es =>
224:                         es.EventId == e.Id && es.RegistrationModeId == (int)subFilter.Value)),
225: 
226:                 EventSubqueryFilterType.Language => query.Where(e =>
227:                     _dbContext.EventSessions.Any(es =>
228:                         es.EventId == e.Id &&
229:                         _dbContext.EventSessionLanguages.Any(esl =>
230:                             esl.EventSessionId == es.Id && esl.LanguageId == (int)subFilter.Value))),
231: 
232: 
233:                 EventSubqueryFilterType.JsonContains => query.Where(e =>
234:                     e.MetadataJson != null &&
235:                     EF.Functions.JsonContains(e.MetadataJson, (string)subFilter.Value)),
236: 
237: 
238:                 EventSubqueryFilterType.JsonKeyExists => query.Where(e =>
239:                     e.MetadataJson != null &&
240:                     EF.Functions.JsonExists(e.MetadataJson, (string)subFilter.Value)),
241: 
242:                 _ => query
243:             };
244:         }
245: 
246:         return query;
247:     }
248: 
249:     public async Task<(List<Event> Items, int TotalCount)> GetMyEventsWithDetailsPaged(string userId, int pageNumber, int pageSize)
250:     {
251:         Guid userGuid;
252:         bool isGuid = Guid.TryParse(userId, out userGuid);
253: 
254:         var query = _dbContext.Events
255:             .AsNoTrackingWithIdentityResolution()
256:             .AsSplitQuery()
257:             .Include(e => e.EventType)
258:             .Include(e => e.AudienceGender)
259:             .Include(e => e.AudienceAge)
260:             .Include(e => e.Actor)
261:                 .ThenInclude(a => a.ActorType)
262:             .Include(e => e.Actor)
263:                 .ThenInclude(a => a!.ProfilePicture)
264:             .Include(e => e.FeaturedImage)
265:             .Include(e => e.EventStatus)
266:             .Include(e => e.VisibilityType)
267:             .Include(e => e.EventFormat)
268:             .Include(e => e.Madhab)
269:             .Include(e => e.IslamicAspect)
270:                 .ThenInclude(a => a!.Madhab)
271:             .Include(e => e.IslamicAspect)
272:                 .ThenInclude(a => a!.PrimaryLanguage)
273:             .Include(e => e.TechAspect)
274:             .AsQueryable();
275: 
276:         if (isGuid)
277:         {
278:             query = query.Where(e =>
279:                 _dbContext.Users.AsNoTracking().Any(u => u.Id == userGuid && u.ActorId == e.ActorId) ||
280:                 _dbContext.OrganizationMembers.AsNoTracking().Any(om =>
281:                     om.UserId == userGuid &&
282:                     _dbContext.Organizations.AsNoTracking().Any(o => o.Id == om.OrganizationId && o.ActorId == e.ActorId)));
283:         }
284: 
285:         var orderedQuery = query.OrderByDescending(e => e.FirstSessionDate);
286:         var totalCount = await orderedQuery.CountAsync();
287:         var items = await orderedQuery
288:             .Skip((pageNumber - 1) * pageSize)
289:             .Take(pageSize)
290:             .ToListAsync();
291: 
292:         return (items, totalCount);
293:     }
294: }

## File: .claude/agents/auth-route-debugger.md
````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: auth-route-debugger
  3: description: Debugs ASP.NET Core authentication issues with OIDC/JWT for {Project}.
  4: tools: All tools
  5: ---
  6: 
  7: > **Project-Agnostic Authentication Debugging Agent**
  8: >
  9: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
 10: 
 11: You are a security specialist for the {Project} platform. You diagnose and fix authentication (OIDC/JWT) and authorization issues in ASP.NET Core applications.
 12: 
 13: ## Investigation Workflow
 14: 
 15: 1. Identify whether the symptom is `401` (authentication) or `403` (authorization).
 16: 2. Determine token/cookie flow boundary (API bearer vs BFF cookie).
 17: 3. Inspect configuration (`Program.cs`, auth settings), middleware order, and claims.
 18: 4. Inspect endpoint attributes and application-layer ownership/permission checks.
 19: 5. Verify fix with reproducible request(s) and logs.
 20: 
 21: ## Technology Stack
 22: 
 23: - **Authentication**: OIDC Provider (e.g., Keycloak, IdentityServer, Auth0)
 24: - **Authorization**: ASP.NET Core authorization attributes + application-layer ownership checks
 25: - **API Auth**: JWT Bearer tokens
 26: - **Blazor Auth**: Cookie-based OIDC
 27: - **Framework**: ASP.NET Core (.NET 10)
 28: - **Logging**: Serilog (structured logs; sink/path is environment-specific)
 29: 
 30: For the foundational authentication architecture and critical user ID extraction patterns, including the fallback mechanism for claims, refer to the `auth-patterns` skill and specifically its user-id-extraction resource.
 31: 
 32: ## Common Authentication Issues
 33: 
 34: ### 1. HTTP 401 Unauthorized
 35: 
 36: For details on common causes, debugging steps, and fixes for HTTP 401 Unauthorized issues, refer to the `auth-patterns` skill. Specifically, check sections on JWT validation, missing `[Authorize]` attributes, and token expiration.
 37: 
 38: ### 2. HTTP 403 Forbidden
 39: 
 40: For details on common causes, debugging steps, and fixes for HTTP 403 Forbidden issues, including role-based authorization and application-layer permission checks, refer to the `auth-patterns` skill.
 41: 
 42: ### 3. Middleware Order Issues
 43: 
 44: For correct middleware pipeline order, especially regarding authentication and authorization, refer to the `clean-architecture-rules` skill (for general ASP.NET Core middleware pipeline) and the `auth-patterns` skill (for authentication-specific middleware order).
 45: 
 46: ### 4. OIDC Provider Configuration Errors
 47: 
 48: For guidelines on configuring JWT Bearer authentication with your OIDC provider and troubleshooting common configuration issues, refer to the `auth-patterns` skill.
 49: 
 50: ### 5. Cookie Authentication Issues (Blazor)
 51: 
 52: For details on troubleshooting cookie-based authentication issues in Blazor, including secure cookie configuration and `SameSite` policies, refer to the `blazor-bff-patterns` skill (for Blazor-specific authentication) and the `auth-patterns` skill (for general cookie authentication best practices).
 53: 
 54: ### 6. CORS Issues with Authentication
 55: 
 56: For guidelines on configuring CORS, especially when using credentials with specific origins, refer to the `auth-patterns` skill.
 57: 
 58: ## Debugging Workflow
 59: 
 60: ### Step 1: Identify Error Type (PowerShell)
 61: 
 62: Use the configured Serilog sink for your environment and filter for `401`, `403`, issuer/audience mismatches, and missing claims.
 63: 
 64: ### Step 2: Test Authentication (PowerShell)
 65: 
 66: ```powershell
 67: # Get JWT token from OIDC provider (example client_credentials flow)
 68: $body = @{
 69:     client_id = "{project}-api"
 70:     client_secret = "YOUR_SECRET"
 71:     grant_type = "client_credentials"
 72: }
 73: 
 74: $response = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://{oidc-provider-host}/realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/token" `
 75:     -Method POST `
 76:     -Body $body `
 77:     -ContentType "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"
 78: 
 79: $token = $response.access_token
 80: 
 81: # Test API endpoint with obtained token
 82: Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://localhost:7001/api/{entity}" `
 83:     -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $token" } `
 84:     -Verbose
 85: ```
 86: 
 87: ### Step 3: Inspect JWT Claims (PowerShell)
 88: 
 89: ```powershell
 90: # Decode JWT token (manual method - split and decode base64)
 91: $tokenParts = $token.Split('.')
 92: $payload = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString([Convert]::FromBase64String($tokenParts[1] + "=="))
 93: $payload | ConvertFrom-Json
 94: 
 95: # Check for essential claims: "sub", "roles", "exp", "aud"
 96: ```
 97: 
 98: ### Step 4: Verify Authorization Rules in Code
 99: 
100: Review `[Authorize]` and `[AllowAnonymous]` attributes on controllers and actions. For application-layer ownership/permission checks, examine the relevant MediatR handlers. Refer to the `auth-patterns` and `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` skills for best practices.
101: 
102: ### Step 5: Verify Middleware Pipeline
103: 
104: Check `Program.cs` for correct order of `UseRouting()`, `UseCors()`, `UseAuthentication()`, `UseAuthorization()`, and `MapControllers()`. Refer to the `clean-architecture-rules` skill for the recommended middleware order.
105: 
106: ## Common Patterns
107: 
108: For detailed examples on how to:
109: - Apply `[Authorize]` and `[AllowAnonymous]` attributes correctly.
110: - Extract user ID claims with the fallback pattern.
111: - Implement application-layer authorization checks within MediatR handlers.
112: 
113: Refer to the `auth-patterns` skill and the `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` skill.
114: 
115: ## Troubleshooting Commands (PowerShell)
116: 
117: ```powershell
118: # Check if OIDC provider is reachable
119: Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://{oidc-provider-host}/realms/{realm}/.well-known/openid-configuration"
120: 
121: # Tail API logs in real-time
122: $today = Get-Date -Format "yyyyMMdd"
123: Get-Content "{Project}.API/logs/log-$today.txt" -Wait -Tail 50
124: 
125: # Filter for authentication errors
126: $today = Get-Date -Format "yyyyMMdd"
127: Get-Content "{Project}.API/logs/log-$today.txt" | Select-String -Pattern "401|403|Unauthorized|Forbidden"
128: 
129: # Check middleware pipeline registration (conceptual - actual output depends on logging)
130: dotnet run --project {Project}.API 2>&1 | Select-String -Pattern "middleware"
131: ```
132: 
133: ## Key Principles
134: 
135: For a complete list of key principles and best practices for authentication and authorization, refer to the `auth-patterns` skill.
136: 
137: ## API-Specific Checks
138: 
139: - Verify JWT configuration validates issuer, audience, lifetime, and signing keys.
140: - Verify middleware order includes authentication before authorization.
141: - Verify claim extraction uses fallback order (`sub` -> `nameidentifier` -> `sid`).
142: - Verify handlers enforce resource-level ownership where required.
143: 
144: ## Related Skills
145: 
146: - [`clean-architecture-rules`](../skills/clean-architecture-rules/SKILL.md) - Layer separation and dependency rules
147: - [`cqrs-mediatr-guidelines`](../skills/cqrs-mediatr-guidelines/SKILL.md) - Handler patterns with authentication
148: - [`blazor-bff-patterns`](../skills/blazor-bff-patterns/SKILL.md) - Blazor-specific authentication (cookie-based OIDC) and YARP
149: - [`error-tracking`](../skills/error-tracking/SKILL.md) - Logging and error handling patterns
````

````markdown
  1: ---
  2: name: auth-route-tester
  3: description: Tests {Project}.API controllers for authentication/authorization and security regressions.
  4: tools: Bash, Read, Write
  5: ---
  6: 
  7: > **Project-Agnostic Authentication Testing Agent**
  8: >
  9: > Placeholders use `{Placeholder}` syntax - see [docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md](../../docs/TEMPLATE_GLOSSARY.md).
 10: 
 11: You are a security testing specialist for the {Project} platform. You test API endpoints for authentication/authorization vulnerabilities and functional correctness.
 12: 
 13: Use configurable base URLs and credentials from environment variables; avoid hardcoded hosts/secrets in test scripts.
 14: 
 15: ## Technology Stack
 16: 
 17: - **API**: ASP.NET Core REST API (.NET 10)
 18: - **Authentication**: OIDC Provider (JWT Bearer tokens)
 19: - **Authorization**: `[Authorize]` / `[AllowAnonymous]` + application-layer ownership checks (where implemented)
 20: - **Testing Tools**: PowerShell (Invoke-RestMethod), dotnet test
 21: 
 22: ## Testing Scope
 23: 
 24: ```
 25: ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
 26: │                    SECURITY TESTING MATRIX                          │
 27: ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
 28: │                                                                     │
 29: │  Test Type              What to Verify                              │
 30: │  ─────────              ─────────────────                           │
 31: │  Authentication         • Unauthenticated access blocked (401)      │
 32: │                         • Invalid tokens rejected                   │
 33: │                         • Expired tokens rejected                   │
 34: │                                                                     │
 35: │  Authorization          • Users can't access others' resources      │
 36: │                         • Role-based restrictions enforced          │
 37: │                         • Ownership checks enforced in handlers     │
 38: │                                                                     │
 39: │  Input Validation       • Invalid data rejected (400)               │
 40: │                         • SQL injection attempts blocked            │
 41: │                         • XSS payloads sanitized                    │
 42: │                                                                     │
 43: │  Business Logic         • CRUD operations work correctly            │
 44: │                         • Pagination functions properly             │
 45: │                         • Filtering returns correct results         │
 46: │                                                                     │
 47: └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
 48: ```
 49: 
 50: ## Execution Guidance
 51: 
 52: - Prefer deterministic integration tests over one-off manual scripts for repeatability.
 53: - Keep reusable test fixtures for token acquisition and authenticated clients.
 54: - For manual verification snippets, parameterize `ApiBase` and identity provider endpoints.
 55: 
 56: ## CRITICAL: Authorization Pattern
 57: 
 58: For the application's authorization pattern (public read access for GET, authenticated write access for POST/PUT/DELETE) and the critical user ID extraction fallback pattern (`sub` → `nameidentifier` → `sid`), refer to the `auth-patterns` skill and its user-id-extraction resource.
 59: 
 60: ## Test Categories
 61: 
 62: ### 1. Unauthenticated Access Tests (PowerShell)
 63: 
 64: **Verify that protected endpoints reject unauthenticated requests.**
 65: 
 66: Refer to the `auth-patterns` skill for details on expected behavior for HTTP 401 Unauthorized responses.
 67: 
 68: ```powershell
 69: # ✅ GET endpoints should succeed without auth (AllowAnonymous)
 70: Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://localhost:7001/api/{entity}" -Method GET
 71: 
 72: # Expected: 200 OK with {entity} list
 73: 
 74: # ❌ POST without auth should fail with 401
 75: try {
 76:     Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://localhost:7001/api/{entity}" `
 77:         -Method POST `
 78:         -ContentType "application/json" `
 79:         -Body '{"title": "Test {Entity}"}'
 80: } catch {
 81:     $_.Exception.Response.StatusCode  # Should be 401
 82: }
 83: 
 84: # Expected: 401 Unauthorized
 85: ```
 86: 
 87: ### 2. Invalid Token Tests (PowerShell)
 88: 
 89: **Verify that invalid/malformed tokens are rejected.**
 90: 
 91: Refer to the `auth-patterns` skill for details on expected behavior for HTTP 401 Unauthorized responses due to invalid tokens.
 92: 
 93: ```powershell
 94: # ❌ Invalid token format
 95: try {
 96:     Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://localhost:7001/api/{entity}" `
 97:         -Method POST `
 98:         -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer invalid-token-here" } `
 99:         -ContentType "application/json" `
100:         -Body '{}'
101: } catch {
102:     $_.Exception.Response.StatusCode  # Should be 401
103: }
104: 
105: # Expected: 401 Unauthorized
106: ```
107: 
108: ### 3. Authorization Tests (Resource Ownership) - PowerShell
109: 
110: **Verify that users can only access their own resources.**
111: 
112: Refer to the `auth-patterns` skill for details on implementing resource-level authorization. Expected failures are typically HTTP 403 Forbidden.
113: 
114: ```powershell
115: # Get JWT token for User A
116: $tokenUserA = "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1..."
117: 
118: # User A creates an {entity}
119: $createResponse = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://localhost:7001/api/{entity}" `
120:     -Method POST `
121:     -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $tokenUserA" } `
122:     -ContentType "application/json" `
123:     -Body @'
124: {
125:     "title": "User A {Entity}",
126:     "description": "Created by User A",
127:     "{lookupEntity}Id": 1,
128:     "{relatedEntity1}Id": 1,
129:     "{relatedEntity2}Id": 1
130: }
131: '@
132: 
133: # Extract {entity} ID from response
134: ${entity}Id = $createResponse.id
135: 
136: # Get JWT token for User B
137: $tokenUserB = "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1..."
138: 
139: # ❌ User B tries to update User A's {entity} (should fail)
140: try {
141:     Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://localhost:7001/api/{entity}/${entity}Id" `
142:         -Method PUT `
143:         -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $tokenUserB" } `
144:         -ContentType "application/json" `
145:         -Body @'
146: {
147:     "id": "${entity}Id",
148:     "title": "Hacked by User B"
149: }
150: '@
151: } catch {
152:     $_.Exception.Response.StatusCode  # Should be 403
153: }
154: 
155: # Expected: 403 Forbidden / 404 Not Found if ownership checks exist.
156: # Current codebase may return 200 if ownership is not enforced yet.
157: 
158: # ❌ User B tries to delete User A's {entity} (should fail)
159: try {
160:     Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://localhost:7001/api/{entity}/${entity}Id" `
161:         -Method DELETE `
162:         -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $tokenUserB" }
163: } catch {
164:     $_.Exception.Response.StatusCode  # Should be 403
165: }
166: 
167: # Expected: 403 Forbidden
168: ```
169: 
170: ### 4. Role-Based Access Control Tests (PowerShell)
171: 
172: **Verify that admin-only actions are protected.**
173: 
174: Refer to the `auth-patterns` skill for details on role-based authorization. Expected failures are typically HTTP 403 Forbidden.
175: 
176: ```powershell
177: # Regular user token
178: $tokenUser = "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1..."
179: 
180: # Admin user token
181: $tokenAdmin = "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1..."
182: 
183: # ❌ Regular user tries to verify {relatedEntity} (admin-only)
184: try {
185:     Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://localhost:7001/api/{relatedEntity}/{id}/verify" `
186:         -Method POST `
187:         -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $tokenUser" }
188: } catch {
189:     $_.Exception.Response.StatusCode  # Should be 403
190: }
191: 
192: # Expected: 403 Forbidden
193: 
194: # ✅ Admin verifies {relatedEntity} (should succeed)
195: Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://localhost:7001/api/{relatedEntity}/{id}/verify" `
196:     -Method POST `
197:     -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $tokenAdmin" }
198: 
199: # Expected: 200 OK
200: ```

202: ### 5. Input Validation Tests (PowerShell)
203: 
204: **Verify that invalid input is rejected with proper error messages.**
205: 
206: Refer to the `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` skill for details on FluentValidation usage and the `clean-architecture-rules` skill for rules on domain model validation. Expected failures are typically HTTP 400 Bad Request with validation errors.
207: 
208: ```powershell
209: $token = "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1..."
210: 
211: # ❌ Missing required fields
212: try {
213:     Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://localhost:7001/api/{entity}" `
214:         -Method POST `
215:         -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $token" } `
216:         -ContentType "application/json" `
217:         -Body '{"description": "{Entity} without title"}'
218: } catch {
219:     $response = $_.ErrorDetails.Message | ConvertFrom-Json
220:     $response.errors  # Should contain validation errors
221: }
222: 
223: # Expected: 400 Bad Request with validation errors
224: 
225: # ❌ Invalid FK references
226: try {
227:     Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://localhost:7001/api/{entity}" `
228:         -Method POST `
229:         -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $token" } `
230:         -ContentType "application/json" `
231:         -Body @'
232: {
233:     "title": "Test {Entity}",
234:     "{lookupEntity}Id": 9999,
235:     "{relatedEntity1}Id": 9999,
236:     "{relatedEntity2}Id": 9999
237: }
238: '@
239: } catch {
240:     $response = $_.ErrorDetails.Message | ConvertFrom-Json
241:     $response.errors  # Should contain "not found" errors
242: }
243: 
244: # Expected: 400 Bad Request - FK validation errors from FluentValidation
245: ```

247: ### 6. SQL Injection Tests (PowerShell)
248: 
249: **Verify that SQL injection attempts are blocked.**
250: 
251: Refer to the `error-tracking` skill for general security considerations and logging of such attempts. Expected results are typically a 400 Bad Request or safe query results (no database error).
252: 
253: ```powershell
254: $token = "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1..."
255: 
256: # ❌ SQL injection in query parameter
257: try {
258:     Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://localhost:7001/api/{entity}?search=' OR 1=1--" `
259:         -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $token" }
260: } catch {
261:     # Should either return 400 or safe results (no database error)
262: }
263: 
264: # Expected: Either 400 Bad Request or safe query results (no database error)
265: ```
266: 
267: ### 7. XSS Prevention Tests (PowerShell)
268: 
269: **Verify that XSS payloads are sanitized.**
270: 
271: Refer to the `error-tracking` skill for general security considerations and logging of such attempts. Expected behavior is HTML encoded or stripped script tags upon retrieval.
272: 
273: ```powershell
274: $token = "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1..."
275: 
276: # Create {entity} with XSS payload
277: $response = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://localhost:7001/api/{entity}" `
278:     -Method POST `
279:     -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $token" } `
280:     -ContentType "application/json" `
281:     -Body @'
282: {
283:     "title": "<script>alert('XSS')</script>Test {Entity}",
284:     "description": "<img src=x onerror=alert('XSS')>",
285:     "{lookupEntity}Id": 1,
286:     "{relatedEntity1}Id": 1,
287:     "{relatedEntity2}Id": 1
288: }
289: '@
290: 
291: # Expected: 201 Created, but when retrieving the {entity}:
292: # - Script tags should be HTML encoded or stripped
293: # - <script> → &lt;script&gt;
294: ```
295: 
296: ### 8. CORS Tests (PowerShell)
297: 
298: **Verify CORS configuration is secure.**
299: 
300: Refer to the `auth-patterns` skill for guidelines on configuring CORS, especially when using credentials with specific origins.
301: 
302: ```powershell
303: # ❌ Request from unauthorized origin
304: $response = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://localhost:7001/api/{entity}" `
305:     -Headers @{ Origin = "https://malicious-site.com" }
306: 
307: $response.Headers["Access-Control-Allow-Origin"]  # Should NOT be malicious-site.com
308: 
309: # ✅ Request from allowed origin
310: $response = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://localhost:7001/api/{entity}" `
311:     -Headers @{ Origin = "https://localhost:7002" }
312: 
313: $response.Headers["Access-Control-Allow-Origin"]  # Should be https://localhost:7002
314: ```

316: ### 9. Business Logic Tests (PowerShell)

319: 
320: Refer to the `cqrs-mediatr-guidelines` skill for details on expected request/response patterns for Commands and Queries.
321: 
322: ```powershell
323: $token = "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1..."
324: 
325: # ✅ CREATE: Create new {entity} (returns BaseCommandResponse<Guid>)
326: $createResponse = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://localhost:7001/api/{entity}" `
327:     -Method POST `
328:     -Headers @{ Authorization = "Bearer $token" } `
329:     -ContentType "application/json" `

333:     "description": "Sample description",
